article.articleHeadline: ಸಾಂಕ್ರಾಮಿಕ ರೋಗ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣಕ್ಕೆ ಶಾಸಕರ ಸಮಿತಿ, ಎಬೋಲಾ ಹರಡುವಿಕೆ ತಡೆಗೆ ಏರ್‌ಪೋರ್ಟ್‌ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಕ್ರೀನಿಂಗ್: ಯುಟಿ ಖಾದರ್ ಘೋಷಣೆ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Legislative Committee for Infectious Disease Control, Screening at Airports to Prevent the Spread of Ebola: UT Khader's Announcement
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-20, Karnataka Health Department will form Special Committees led by legislators from each constituency to strengthen local infectious disease control. Health Minister UT Khader announced in Bengaluru a new emergency management system enabling rapid district-level information flow and coordinated response. To curb Ebola risk, airports screen travelers arriving from Congo, Uganda, and other Ebola-affected African countries, with ongoing border surveillance. Malaria cases in the state fell by about 70% and dengue by 33% compared with the same period last year; authorities are conducting house-to-house larval surveys and recruiting lab technicians and pharmacists. Private hospitals treating infectious diseases must report cases to the health department, and SOPs prevent unnecessary charging.

triage.headline_ja: 感染症対策のための議員委員会設置、エボラ拡大防止のため空港でスクリーニング実施：UTカダル氏発表
triage.triage_reason: 記事はカルナタカ州における予防的行政対応（委員会設置、空港スクリーニング）が主題であり、インド国内でのエボラ発生はなく、マラリア・デングも前年比で減少傾向にあるため、新規の異常なアウトブレイクシグナルとは言えない。
triage.notes: エボラはコンゴ・ウガンダなどアフリカ流行国からの入国者に対する予防的スクリーニングの文脈で言及されており、インド国内での発生は確認されていない。マラリア・デングはインド（カルナタカ州）で実際に発生しているが、前年比で大幅減少しており深刻度は低い。DRC・ウガンダは背景情報としての言及であり、記事の主題ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : le Canada ferme ses frontières à certains voyageurs en provenance de RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Canada closes its borders to certain travelers from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Facing an accelerating Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Canada tightened border controls. The country barred entry to foreign nationals who have recently stayed in the DRC within the past 21 days, effective Monday, while Canadian citizens and permanent residents remain exempt from the ban but must undergo a 21‑day quarantine on arrival if they have traveled recently to the DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan. The measures run through August 29 as a precaution, even though Canada’s risk remains low and no travel-linked imported cases have been detected. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned the outbreak is spreading faster than any prior Ebola episode. As of July 15, the WHO counts 2,124 cases and 828 deaths in the DRC, though officials say the true scale may be 2–4 times higher.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：カナダがコンゴ民主共和国からの一部渡航者に対し国境を閉鎖
triage.triage_reason: WHO事務局長が過去最速の拡大と警告するDRCのエボラ流行で、死者828人・症例2,124人（実数はさらに多い可能性）に達し、カナダが渡航制限を導入するなど国際的対応が発生しているためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はDRCで進行中のエボラ流行であり、カナダは渡航制限を課している側であって発生国ではない。ウガンダ・南スーダンは渡航歴に基づく検疫対象として言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Kanada od danas ne dozvoljava ulazak stranim državljanima koji su bili u Kongu zbog ebole
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Canada as of today will not allow entry to foreign nationals who have been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo because of Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Canada will bar entry to foreign nationals who have been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo within the last three weeks because of Ebola. The Public Health Agency of Canada announced the measure, which applies from Monday, July 20, as part of an enhanced plan to limit risks of imported disease, with no details on duration or exemptions. The policy aims to reduce the health risks posed to Canadians by Ebola exposure and to streamline border screening for travelers, including humanitarian workers returning home. Officials emphasized that the restriction is targeted to those who have recently been in the DRC, reflecting concern about ongoing Ebola transmission in the region. The announcement did not specify how long the rule will last or whether exemptions may be made in humanitarian cases.

triage.headline_ja: カナダ、エボラのため今日からコンゴ民主共和国に滞在歴のある外国人の入国を禁止
triage.triage_reason: カナダがDRCでのエボラ拡大を理由に外国人の入国制限を導入したことは、国際的拡大懸念と渡航制限措置の発生を示し、IHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへの移行が適切。
triage.notes: 記事はカナダの入国制限措置に焦点を当てているが、根本原因はDRCでのエボラ流行であるため、感染発生地としてDRCのみを検証済み地域とした。カナダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: كندا تحظر دخول الأجانب القادمين من الكونغو الديمقراطية بسبب تفشي إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Canada bans entry of foreigners arriving from the Democratic Republic of the Congo due to an Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Canada imposed a temporary entry ban on all foreigners who visited the Democratic Republic of the Congo within the 21 days before arrival, effective July 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. The restriction applies to visa and eTA holders who traveled to DRC in the prior three weeks. Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and others with legal entry rights are exempt but will undergo health screening on arrival; asymptomatic individuals could be quarantined for 21 days, while those with suspected Ebola symptoms are diverted to a health facility for testing and isolation. The action follows a worsening Ebola outbreak in DRC, with more than 2,100 infections and 828 deaths as of July 15, 2026. Ebola spreads mainly through direct contact with bodily fluids or contaminated surfaces. Canada says risk remains low, but violations carry fines up to CAD 150,000 for individuals and CAD 1.5 million for companies; WHO opposes travel restrictions.

triage.headline_ja: カナダ、エボラ流行を理由にコンゴ民主共和国からの外国人入国を禁止
triage.triage_reason: DRCで2100人超の感染・828人の死亡という大規模なエボラ流行が続いており、カナダが渡航制限措置を導入したことでIHR基準（重大な公衆衛生影響、渡航制限）に複数該当するため。
triage.notes: カナダは対象国外のため発生地域には含めない。DRCのエボラ流行が主題であり、カナダの入国制限は流行への対応措置として言及されている。WHOは渡航制限に反対の立場を示している点も注記。

article.articleHeadline: Minden korábbinál gyorsabban terjed a gyilkos járvány: nincs ellenszer, drasztikus korlátozást vezettek be
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deadly epidemic spreading faster than ever before: no cure, drastic restrictions have been imposed
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, the Ebola Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths since its May 15 beginning in Ituri province, with spread to other provinces and neighboring Uganda. In the last 24 hours, 37 deaths were recorded. About 724 patients remain in isolation or hospital care. The DRC reports at least 12 attacks on health facilities in the past two months, and at least 36 health workers have died. There is no licensed vaccine or proven effective treatment for this strain. Canada announced a temporary entry ban for foreign nationals who have been in the DRC in the previous 21 days; Canadians and residents may enter but must quarantine for 21 days, in place until late August. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus notes the outbreak is spreading faster than any previous Ebola outbreak in Congo.

triage.headline_ja: 史上最速で拡大する致死性感染症：治療法なし、各国で厳格な入国制限が導入
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）がDRCで2,344例・930死亡と大規模化し、ウガンダへの越境拡大、医療施設への攻撃、カナダの入国制限措置まで発生しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大な公衆衛生危機である。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの拡大が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。カナダは渡航制限措置の対象国であり発生国ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: कांगो में इबोला के प्रकोप से अब तक कम से कम 930 लोगों की मौत
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Congo, the Ebola outbreak has killed at least 930 people so far.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Bunia, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, has killed at least 930 people, with 2,344 confirmed cases reported by the Ministry of Health. In the last 24 hours, 37 deaths were recorded, among the highest daily tallies. The outbreak, declared on May 15 in eastern Congo, is described as the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record. It is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a less commonly detected species, and there is currently no approved vaccine or treatment. The ministry’s late-night briefing provides the latest counts but does not detail symptoms or transmission chains. Public health authorities continue surveillance and response measures across affected districts as the outbreak persists.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱の流行、死者少なくとも930人に
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の急速な拡大により死者930人・確定例2344件、承認済みワクチン・治療法がない状況であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当するため。
triage.notes: 史上最速拡大とされるエボラ流行で、Bundibugyoエボラウイルスによる非承認治療薬・ワクチン状況下での拡大。フルRRAへの移行が必要。

article.articleHeadline: وفاة 930 شخصًا في الكونغو نتيجة تفشي فيروس إيبولا.. والإصابات بالمئات - الأسبوع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 930 people have died in the Congo as a result of an Ebola virus outbreak, with hundreds of cases - Weekly
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 2,344 lab-confirmed Ebola infections and 930 deaths through July 18 in the current outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare strain with no licensed vaccine or approved treatment. Since the outbreak was declared about two months ago, more than 2,000 infections and 796 deaths have been confirmed, making it the third-largest Ebola outbreak on record. The World Health Organization warns the transmission rate is faster than in previous outbreaks. Despite intensified response efforts, more than 80% of new infections are among people not listed in known contact tracing, indicating several undetected transmission chains.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラウイルス感染拡大により930人死亡、感染者数百人規模に
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模流行（感染者2,344人、死者930人）で史上3番目の規模とされ、WHOも伝播速度の速さを警告しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナルである。
triage.notes: ワクチンや承認された治療法がないBundibugyoエボラウイルス株による流行で、感染者の80%以上が既知の接触者リストに含まれておらず、複数の未検出感染連鎖が存在する可能性が示唆されている。

article.articleHeadline: Why Is the DRC Struggling to Stop Ebola From Spreading Through Funerals?
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) involving the Bundibugyo strain has surpassed 2,000 reported cases and 700 deaths across the DRC and neighboring Uganda as of 2026-07-20. Transmission is driven by transporting infected bodies for traditional funerals; over 100 cross-district body transfers have been documented, with at least one linked to new infections, and nearly two-thirds of Ebola deaths occur outside hospitals. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) and World Health Organization (WHO) advocate safe and dignified burials as a core control measure. WHO’s 12-step protocol covers protective equipment, secure body bags, environment disinfection, safe transport, respectful burial, and ongoing community engagement, explicitly avoiding washing or embalming. A Lancet Global Health analysis of 2018-2020 eastern DRC (3,194 confirmed/probable cases; 7,823 safe and dignified burials) supports burial practices alongside surveillance, contact tracing, and vaccination. Community dialogue and culturally acceptable practices enhance trust and cooperation, including cross-border coordination with Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国はなぜ葬儀を通じたエボラの拡大を止められないのか？
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCとウガンダで2000例・700人以上の死者を出し国境を越えて拡大しており、深刻性・異常性・国際的拡大リスクともに該当するため、フルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていないが、越境感染の文脈として重要。

article.articleHeadline: Omicron RF.5 variant detected in Andhra Pradesh: what experts say about its risk
article.articleSummary: Omicron RF.5 detected in four COVID-19 samples from Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh, confirmed by genome sequencing in Pune. Andhra Pradesh reports 16 cases in total, with 12 up to July 16, and officials say hospitals are prepared with wards, beds and testing kits for detection and treatment. RF.5 is a recombinant Omicron sub-lineage monitored in routine genomic surveillance; WHO tracks strain, with higher numbers reported in Singapore and Asia. There is no indication RF.5 is more dangerous than other Omicron variants; vigilance is advised, but no panic. Experts say RF.5 may accumulate mutations that enable immune escape but not full escape; vaccines may not fully prevent infection but reduce severe disease. Clinical presentation is generally mild to moderate; risk remains higher for older adults, diabetes, heart disease, chronic lung conditions, and immunocompromised individuals. Guidance: test with symptoms; protect vulnerable contacts; seek care if symptoms persist or oxygen drops.

triage.headline_ja: アンドラプラデーシュ州でオミクロンRF.5variantを検出：専門家によるリスク評価
triage.triage_reason: 既知のオミクロン系統の亜系統であり、重症度が高いという証拠はなく、症例数も少数（16例）で通常のサーベイランス範囲内の事象と判断される。
triage.notes: 記事はRF.5がこれまでのオミクロン系統より危険性が高いという証拠はないと明言しており、症状も軽度から中等度。ルーティンのゲノムサーベイランスの一環として検出されたものであり、パニックの必要はないと専門家が述べている。

article.articleHeadline: WHO Warns As Congo Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 2,000 Cases, Spreads To Uganda | Outlook India
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 2,000 confirmed cases, with 2,124 cases and 828 deaths reported as of last week. Uganda has 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, all in Kampala and linked to travel from the DRC. One confirmed case has also been reported in France, indicating exportation of infection. The CDC said the outbreak is spreading substantially faster than previous Ebola outbreaks and is now the third largest on record. The situation underscores ongoing transmission and cross-border health risks, including travel-associated cases, highlighting the need for rapid laboratory confirmation and coordinated public health responses.

triage.headline_ja: WHOが警告:コンゴのエボラ流行が2,000例超え、ウガンダへ拡大
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで2,000例超・828人死亡と重大な公衆衛生影響があり、ウガンダおよびフランスへの国際的拡散も確認されているため、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダとフランスは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていないが、国際拡散の重要な証拠として本文に反映済み。CDCは本流行を史上3番目に大きい規模かつ拡大速度が過去より速いと評価している。

article.articleHeadline: ارتفاع إصابات فيروس إيبولا المؤكدة لـ2344 بينها 930 حالة وفاة بالكونغو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Confirmed Ebola virus infections rise to 2,344, including 930 deaths, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Confirmed Ebola virus disease infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have risen to 2,344 with 930 deaths as of July 18, 2026. The outbreak’s trajectory continues to be described by the World Health Organization as faster than any previous Ebola epidemic. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said more than 2,000 cases (including 796 deaths) have been confirmed since the outbreak was declared about two months earlier, making it the third-largest Ebola outbreak on record. The figures indicate sustained transmission and ongoing public health risk in the DRC. The numbers reflect confirmed cases, underscoring the need for intensified containment, surveillance, and response measures in affected provinces.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラウイルス確定感染者2,344人に増加、死者930人
triage.triage_reason: WHOが過去最速の拡大速度と評価する大規模エボラ流行であり、致死率も高く、国際的拡大・公衆衛生上の深刻な影響が明確なため、フルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断する。
triage.notes: WHOが過去最速の流行拡大かつ史上3番目の規模と明言している点は重大なシグナルであり、フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: ارتفاع إصابات إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية إلى 2344 حالة والوفيات تبلغ 930
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rise in Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to 2,344, with 930 deaths.
article.articleSummary: 2,344 confirmed Ebola cases and 930 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as of July 18, 2026. The outbreak is spreading at an unprecedented pace, with WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus noting it as the third-largest global Ebola surge. The surge is driven by the rare Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain, for which there is no licensed vaccine or approved treatment, complicating containment efforts. More than 80% of new infections are among people not on known contact lists, indicating ongoing, hidden transmission chains. The DRC government, with WHO and international partners, continues response activities, including treatment centers, infection prevention and control, risk communication, and enhanced case detection and contact tracing to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ感染者が2,344人に増加、死者930人
triage.triage_reason: 致死率が高いエボラ出血熱がDRCで異例の速度で拡大し、ワクチン・治療法未承認のブンディブギョ株が原因で隠れた感染連鎖が続いており、国際的関心・支援が既に発生しているためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: WHO事務局長が過去3番目の規模のエボラ流行と言及し、既往接触者リスト外での感染が80%超と拡大リスクが高い。ワクチン・治療薬未承認のブンディブギョ株であることが特に懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola si v Kongu už vyžiadala najmenej 930 mŕtvych
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has already claimed at least 930 lives in the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in Ituri province in the northeast, has reached at least 930 deaths from 2,344 confirmed cases, with 724 patients currently in isolation or hospital as of July 20, 2026. Since mid-May, the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak is the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record, and there is no vaccine or specific therapy for this strain. Existing vaccines developed in 2018–2019 protect only against the Zaire ebolavirus strain and are not effective here; as of July, clinical trials of two treatments targeting Bundibugyo have begun. Security concerns have hampered responses, including at least 12 attacks on health facilities and response teams in Ituri, and the departure of healthcare workers over unpaid salaries; at least 36 infected workers have died. Authorities say measures are being intensified in affected zones.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ、コンゴで死者数がすでに少なくとも930人に達する
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州でのブンディブギョ型エボラ出血熱の急速な拡大（2344例、930人死亡）で、有効なワクチン・治療法が存在せず、治安悪化により対応が阻害されているため、深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスクが高い。
triage.notes: 史上最速の拡大とされるブンディブギョ型エボラ出血熱の流行で、既存ワクチン（ザイール株用）が無効であり、治安悪化・医療従事者の離職・未払い賃金等が対応を妨げている。新規治療薬の臨床試験が開始されたが結果は不明。フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 6 tháng đầu năm, TP Hồ Chí Minh ghi nhận 5 người tử vong do bệnh dại
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the first six months of the year, Ho Chi Minh City recorded five rabies deaths.
article.articleSummary: Five rabies deaths were recorded in Ho Chi Minh City in six months of 2026, with three in Long Hai, one in Cu Chi, and one in Hoa Hiep. On July 20, the city Center for Disease Control (HCDC) warned of rising rabies incidence and problems with stray dogs and cats unvaccinated. All five patients were unvaccinated and did not receive rabies immunoglobulin; 40% of cases involved improper wound care. A fatal case involved a man bitten while exercising who declined vaccination in favor of a folk remedy 'taking venom' from a village healer, dying later after transfer to tertiary hospital. Southern region rabies deaths totalled 20 so far in 2026, about half of 2025's total. Dr. Luong Chan Quang of Pasteur Institute Ho Chi Minh City cites persistent belief in folk cures; no evidence supports such remedies, and once the virus reaches the nervous system, mortality is nearly 100%.

triage.headline_ja: 2026年上半期、ホーチミン市で狂犬病による死者5人を記録
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病はベトナムで既知の流行病であり国際的な異常性・拡大リスクは低いが、未接種の野良犬猫問題や民間療法への依存など管理上の課題が続いており、地域当局（HCDC）が注意喚起を行っているため継続的な観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はベトナム・ホーチミン市における狂犬病の国内動向報告であり、中国（河南省）は発生地域として付与されているが記事本文では言及されていないため除外した。狂犬病は人獣共通感染症で人-人感染はなく、国際的拡大リスクは低い。

article.articleHeadline: Epidémia eboly v Konžskej demokratickej republike si vyžiadala už najmenej 930 obetí
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has already claimed at least 930 lives.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has claimed at least 930 lives, with 2,344 confirmed infections and 724 patients currently in isolation or hospitals. The northeast Ituri province has seen escalating violence against responders, with at least 12 attacks on health facilities and teams since the outbreak began in mid-May. Thousands of people are infected and hundreds are isolated. Health workers, many unpaid, have left postings; at least 36 of those infected have died. The outbreak is described as the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in the virus’s history. It is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment. Vaccines developed in 2018–2019 protect only against the Zaire strain; since July, clinical trials of two drugs have begun. Authorities say measures are being intensified in affected zones.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、死者数少なくとも930人に

article.articleHeadline: India Approves First Dengue Vaccine QDENGA for People Aged 4 to 60
article.articleSummary: India approves its first dengue vaccine, QDENGA, for people aged 4 to 60, after market authorization by the Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) to Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India. QDENGA offers protection against all four dengue virus serotypes and can be administered without prior testing for previous dengue infection, enabling easier inclusion in vaccination programs. The vaccine has already been approved in 43 countries, with more than 32 million doses distributed globally. Health authorities anticipate this will bolster India's efforts to cut dengue-related illnesses and hospitalisations, particularly during the annual monsoon season when cases surge. Takeda has partnered with Indian vaccine manufacturer Biological E to expand production capacity, supporting domestic supply and global demand. The development marks a significant step in addressing dengue as a persistent public health challenge in India.

article.articleHeadline: Punjab: जानलेवा बीमारी का खतरा बढ़ा, 194 गांव हाई रिस्क एरिया घोषित, पढ़ें पूरी खबर
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Punjab: The threat of a deadly disease has increased; 194 villages declared high-risk areas; Read the full news.
article.articleSummary: Punjab's Amritsar district faces a rising TB threat, with 194 villages declared high-risk after a 100-day government survey identifying 2,139 TB patients among 30,074 screened (13,143 with X-ray; ~5,500 underwent detailed testing). Demographics: 1,113 men, 1,026 women, 280 children. Authorities have deployed over 500 field teams, conducting house-to-house screening; mobile X-ray vans were used. The district records about 160 TB deaths annually and currently around 5,000 patients are on TB therapy. Free drugs are available at government and private centers; government hospitals offer free TB treatment. Symptoms include persistent cough, coughing up blood, fever, weight loss, night sweats, and fatigue; two-week persistent cough warrants immediate testing. TB is airborne; contacts should be tested. The campaign includes free testing, medications, counseling, nutrition support, and an ASHA worker incentive of Rs 500 per identified positive case.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chiayi City records its first confirmed case of imported dengue fever | The Epoch Times
article.articleSummary: Chiayi City, Taiwan reports its first confirmed imported dengue fever case for 2026 (115th year). The patient, a Taiwanese national with recent travel to Vietnam, developed fever, headache, and retro-orbital pain on July 15, sought care July 16, and was PCR-confirmed on July 18. In response, the Chiayi City Health Bureau intensified vector control around the home, conducted mosquito density surveys, and on July 20 completed indoor/outdoor spraying within a 100-meter radius, with education for the case and contacts. Nationally, as of July 20, Taiwan has 97 confirmed dengue cases: 90 imported, 7 locally transmitted. Officials urge vigilance in hot, humid weather, advise eliminating standing water per the “巡、倒、清、刷” guidance, wear light clothing, and use government-approved repellent. Returning travelers with fever or dengue-like symptoms should wear a mask and promptly visit one of 41 NS1 rapid-diagnostic clinics, informing clinicians of travel history. See CDC Taiwan or call 05-2338066 for more information.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak Spreads Across Central and East Africa Amid Global Health Concerns
article.articleSummary: As of 20 July 2026, Ebola outbreak spreads across Central and East Africa driven by the Bundibugyo strain, not covered by existing vaccines or treatments. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, confirmed infections exceed 2,000 with nearly 800 deaths, one of the largest outbreaks. Uganda reports 20 infections and two deaths; the last patient has been discharged, and there are no clear transmission chains, with preparedness helping limit deaths. Response is hampered by conflict and restricted access, including an attack on a treatment center in Ituri province. A new response roadmap emphasizes early detection, contact tracing, and community engagement; Africa CDC endorses this approach. CDC modeling warns that without proper isolation and treatment, cases could exceed 20,000 and deaths over 2,000; even under best-case scenarios, infections may exceed 10,000 within three months. Travel restrictions and screening persist; the U.S. reports no confirmed cases, while France and Canada monitor travelers.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 'Dangerous' dengue vaccine approved; who can receive the vaccine and how much will it cost?
article.articleSummary: India's CDSCO approved Takeda Pharmaceutical's QDENGA dengue vaccine for use in the country after expert committee recommendation. The tetravalent live attenuated vaccine protects against all four dengue virus serotypes and is indicated for individuals aged 4 to 60 who have not previously been infected. Two-dose regimen; estimated cost for both doses is INR 6,000–12,000, with potential price reductions if produced at scale in India by a Hyderabad-based manufacturer. Long-term clinical data show the vaccine reduces dengue illness caused by all four serotypes by about 61–80%, and lowers dengue-related hospitalizations by approximately 84–90% after two doses. This marks the first dengue vaccine available in India, aiming to curb dengue burden and hospitalizations.

article.articleHeadline: Mulheres fazem história com estudo mineiro que pode acelerar vacina universal contra a malária
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Women Make History with a Minas Gerais Study That Could Accelerate a Universal Malaria Vaccine
article.articleSummary: Minas Gerais researchers unveil a potential universal malaria vaccine. Three scientists from CT-Vacinas in Belo Horizonte mapped Plasmodium antigens, identifying conserved targets across species and life-cycle stages, including antigens present in Brazilian and African malaria parasites. They report that 71% of identified antigens are conserved across species and 75% are expressed in multiple life-cycle stages, enabling vaccines targeting diverse parasite forms. The findings also suggest vaccines could activate T-cell responses in addition to antibodies, potentially boosting efficacy. Published in Nature—the first Brazilian-led article in 157 years—the work marks a milestone for Brazilian science. Brazil logged 44,871 malaria cases Jan–Jun 2026, with 96% in the Amazon region (Acre, Amazonas, Amapá, Pará, Rondônia, Roraima, Tocantins, Mato Grosso, Maranhão). Nineteen cases occurred outside the Amazon (Ceará, Espírito Santo, Goiás, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, São Paulo); fatalities are higher outside the Amazon.

article.articleHeadline: Congo reports 930 Ebola deaths amid worsening outbreak
article.articleSummary: Across eastern Congo, the Ebola outbreak declared May 15 has reached 2,344 laboratory-confirmed cases and 930 deaths as of 18 July 2026, with 37 deaths reported over the previous 24 hours. The Bundibugyo virus is responsible; there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Transmission occurs from wild animals and via contact with infected bodily fluids and contaminated surfaces. The outbreak has spread to five eastern provinces, with Ituri the hardest hit, amid rebel violence and security constraints hampering response. Attacks against health facilities/teams total at least 12; many health workers have left over nonpayment; at least 36 health workers infected have died. WHO notes about 80% of new cases stem from unknown transmission chains, indicating rapid, hard-to-track spread. 724 patients are in isolation in care facilities; 22 new recoveries in the last 24 hours. Response efforts are intensifying despite safety concerns.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ、悪化するエボラ流行で930人の死者を報告

triage.notes: 承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しないブンディブギョウイルス種によるエボラ流行。新規症例の約80%が感染経路不明であり、医療施設への攻撃・医療従事者の離脱等、治安要因が対応を阻害している点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola Death Toll Reaches 930 as Health Officials Step Up Response - Diaspora Digital Media (DDM News) - Nigeria Breaking News, Africa and World News and Updates
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak: 930 deaths, 2,344 confirmed cases, with 37 new deaths in the last 24 hours. Declared in May 2026, caused by the Bundibugyo strain (no approved vaccine or specific treatment). Ituri Province is the hardest hit, and transmission continues in remote communities, complicating containment. Insecurity hampers response, including attacks on facilities and response teams and unpaid wages; 36 health workers have died. Despite challenges, 724 patients remain in isolation or hospitals as response teams expand services. Government, WHO, and international partners are scaling up contact tracing, laboratory testing, infection prevention, and community awareness. WHO warns many new infections arise from unknown transmission chains and calls for continued surveillance, safe burials, and regional cross-border preparedness. Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids; early symptoms include fever, severe headache, muscle pain, weakness, vomiting, diarrhea, and unexplained bleeding in severe cases.

article.articleHeadline: Ekkert lát á út­breiðslu ebólu í Austur-Kongó
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: No let-up in the spread of Ebola in eastern Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo continues unabated. As of 20 July 2026, at least 2,344 cases and 930 deaths have been reported, with 37 deaths recorded on the most recent Saturday. The vast majority of transmission is concentrated across five districts in eastern DRC, amid ongoing security threats, attacks on health facilities and workers, and staff strikes over unpaid pay. WHO warns that most new cases have not been traced, suggesting wider transmission than official tallies and calls for better protection for health workers. This is the 17th outbreak in eastern Congo since 1976, believed to originate from bats; about 15,000 Africans have died from Ebola in Africa over five decades. The current outbreak is due to Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no vaccine or treatment; there is no cure, and fatalities are high. Uganda has also reported Ebola, with responses there appearing more effective.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola deaths in DR Congo rise to 930
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reached 930 deaths from 2,344 cases, as of the latest update. In the past 24 hours, 37 deaths were recorded, one of the highest daily totals. Alarm over safety has hampered response in Ituri province, with at least 12 attacks on health facilities and teams. Medical staff have protested over unpaid wages, contributing to 36 infected health workers and deaths. DR Congo's Ministry of Health reports 724 patients in isolation or hospitals and says response efforts are intensifying; 22 recoveries in 24 hours. Outside DRC, 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths in Uganda, plus 1 case in France. A UK trial plans to test a new Bundibugyo vaccine in adults.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chandipura virus scare in Dungarpur, Rajasthan, health department on alert after death of a six-year-old girl.
article.articleSummary: Chandipura virus (CHPV) infection is suspected in Dungarpur district, Rajasthan, after the death of six-year-old Rinku from Ratanpura village at a government hospital in Himatnagar, Gujarat. She fell ill on 13 July 2026 and was treated at a private hospital in the region, then Modasa, before dying on 15 July 2026. Samples were collected in Himatnagar; Gujarat notified Rajasthan, and Jaipur directed intensified surveillance. In Dungarpur, CMHO Dr. Alankar Gupta said teams are deployed in Ratanpura; about 353 residents have been screened with house-to-house visits. Authorities have intensified sanitation, monitoring, and awareness campaigns; residents are urged to seek care for fever, vomiting, weakness, or other suspected symptoms. CHPV spreads via mosquitoes, ticks, and sand flies, predominantly affecting children under 15, and can cause high fever, flu-like illness, and encephalitis. Lab confirmation pending.

triage.headline_ja: ラジャスタン州ドゥンガルプルでチャンディプラウイルスの脅威、6歳女児死亡後に保健当局が警戒

article.articleHeadline: India Approves First Dengue Vaccine QDENGA; Approved for Ages 4-60 Regardless of Prior Infection History
article.articleSummary: India approves its first dengue vaccine, QDENGA, with market authorization granted to Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India Pvt Ltd by the DCGI. The vaccine is approved for individuals aged 4–60 years and can be administered irrespective of prior dengue infection history, and does not require pre-vaccination screening. The decision follows WHO recommendations, and Takeda has partnered with Biological E for production in India. This marks the first dengue vaccine approval in India, potentially expanding vaccination options in dengue-endemic regions through a screening-free protocol. As of 20 July 2026, the regulatory move enables easier uptake among populations at risk of dengue transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Three EAC countries secure $13M funding to contain Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: Three East African Community (EAC) members—Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Uganda and South Sudan—secured $13 million from the African Development Bank to contain Ebola virus disease. The grant will bolster national emergency responses to the outbreak, funded through the WHO ($10 million drawn from the DRC portfolio) and a second $3 million under the Multi-Country Emergency Assistance Project (DRC, Uganda, South Sudan) to be implemented by Africa CDC. DRC receives the largest share at $11 million; Uganda and South Sudan get $1 million each. DRC has declared a new Ebola outbreak in Ituri province, with cases reported in Bunia, Rwampara and Mongwalu, and spread to North Kivu and South Kivu. The AfDB emphasizes support to protect lives, strengthen health systems, and prevent regional spread.

article.articleHeadline: Massive surge in Influenza A cases in Mumbai: Doctor explains why infections are rising - India TV News
article.articleSummary: Influenza A surge in Mumbai, India, as of 20 July 2026, with hospitals reporting a rising number of patients presenting high fever, cough, sore throat, fatigue, body aches, and occasional GI symptoms. Doctors say the surge is epidemic-like but part of seasonal patterns; no panic. Most healthy individuals recover in 5–7 days with rest and supportive care, but older adults, children under five, pregnant women, and people with diabetes, asthma or chronic heart/kidney disease, or weakened immunity are at higher risk of complications such as pneumonia and hospitalization. Symptoms can resemble a cold or COVID-19, delaying care. Seek medical help for high fever >3 days, breathing difficulties, chest pain, confusion, dehydration, or if symptoms worsen after initial improvement. Antibiotics are not effective; antivirals may help high-risk patients when started within 48 hours. Prevention: hand hygiene, masks, vaccination, and staying home when ill.

triage.notes: 記事は季節性インフルエンザAの流行を報じており、専門家は季節的パターンの一部としており緊急性は低いと説明。ただし高齢者・幼児・基礎疾患患者への注意が必要。続報でムンバイ以外への拡大や重症化率の情報があれば再評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: ETV Bharat's Monsoon Manual Provides A State-By-State Report On The Rainy Season's Biggest Health Risks, Outbreaks And Prevention
article.articleSummary: India faces a rising monsoon health risk as climate change disrupts rainfall and expands dengue across states such as Assam, Kerala, Delhi, and Tamil Nadu, per ETV Bharat's nationwide series (published 20 July 2026). Five-year state-wise data show dengue surging while malaria and kala-azar decline due to sustained interventions. Heavy rains and floods create stagnant water that breeds mosquitoes and contaminate drinking water with sewage, fueling typhoid, cholera, hepatitis A, leptospirosis, and acute diarrhoeal illnesses. Intermittent downpours and floods complicate prediction of outbreaks, with non-communicable diseases like diabetes, hypertension, and heart disease worsening outcomes in infected individuals. Young children under five bear the highest burden, with diarrhoea, pneumonia, and mosquito-borne illnesses driving hospitalisations; vaccination and adequate nutrition remain key defenses. The state-by-state approach highlights local risk profiles across Assam, Delhi, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and beyond.

article.articleHeadline: भारत में डेंगू की पहली वैक्सीन, Takeda के QDENGA को DCGI से मिली मंजूरी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India's first dengue vaccine, Takeda's QDENGA, has received approval from DCGI.
article.articleSummary: India grants DCGI market authorization for Takeda’s QDENGA, the country’s first dengue vaccine, for individuals aged 4–60 years. The vaccine can be administered irrespective of prior dengue infection, with no pre-vaccination testing required. It is given subcutaneously in two 0.5 ml doses at least three months apart and provides protection against all four dengue virus serotypes. Global program data from over 28,000 participants across 19 Phase 1–3 trials, including the DEN-302 Phase 3 study in India, support its safety and immunogenicity. Since 2022, QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries with about 32 million doses distributed. WHO recommends use in dengue-endemic areas and supports immunization programs without prior screening in high-risk regions. Dengue remains a major public health challenge in India, where all four serotypes circulate amid urbanization and climate-driven factors.

article.articleHeadline: СЗО: Епидемијата на ебола во Конго може да биде до четири пати поголема од официјалните податоци
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: The Ebola outbreak in Congo may be up to four times larger than official data.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ebola outbreak has reached 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths as of late Sunday, indicating a severe and ongoing crisis. Congo’s response is hampered by a shortage of treatment centers and community resistance to strict hygiene measures. World Health Organization Emergency Program Director for Health Emergencies, Chikwe Ihekweazu, said the true number of Ebola cases is at least two, and perhaps four times higher than the official figure, based on analysis and mathematical models. He disclosed these findings at a Geneva press conference, as reported by Reuters. The article highlights potential under-detection amid continuing transmission and challenges in outbreak control. Key details emphasize disease name (Ebola), location (DRC), confirmed case and death counts, the possible scale of underreporting, and the need for enhanced response capacity.

The outbreak spans five eastern provinces, with Ituri the worst-affected, where safety fears have restricted response efforts amid ongoing rebel violence.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : Moscou mise sur ses vaccins pour éviter des cas importés en Russie
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Moscow bets on its vaccines to prevent imported cases in Russia.
article.articleSummary: Russia says its vaccines could prevent imported Ebola cases as Moscow notes no cases on its soil since the current Central African outbreak began. Europe has reported three imported cases: a U.S. citizen evacuated to Germany in May 2026; a France case on June 24; and a U.S. humanitarian worker infected in the DRC and evacuated to Germany (CDC, July 10). The Congolese outbreak, declared May 15, 2026, is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC since 1976 and is due to the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine or treatment is licensed. By July 16, the DRC tallied 2,124 cases and 828 deaths, with 725 hospitalized; most recent cases are in Ituri. Uganda’s outbreak is waning, with its last patient discharged on July 16 and a 42-day countdown to end. Africa CDC aims for a licensed vaccine and therapy by end-2026; WHO is evaluating candidates for trials.

article.articleHeadline: உள்நாட்டில் கண்டுபிடிக்கப்பட்ட டெங்கு காய்ச்சலுக்கான முதல் தடுப்பூசி: இந்தியா ஒப்புதல்
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: First domestically developed dengue fever vaccine: India approves.
article.articleSummary: India's Drugs Controller General has approved Takeda's dengue vaccine Qdenga for 4–60-year-olds, marking the first domestically developed dengue vaccine to receive approval in India. The vaccine does not require prior pre-screening; eligible individuals can receive it even if they have had dengue before, and those with a past infection do not need initial serology testing. Since its 2022 introduction, Qdenga has been approved in 43 countries and more than 32 million doses have been distributed worldwide. The Indian approval is a major step in strengthening dengue prevention in India. Seven years of long-term data indicate that Qdenga protects against all four dengue virus serotypes.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Jabalpur News: Seasonal diseases on the rise; outbreaks of jaundice and typhoid alongside viral infections.
article.articleSummary: In Jabalpur, monsoon-triggered seasonal diseases are rising, stretching OPD and IPD services at Victoria District Hospital and Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Medical College. Over the past week, patient load has increased beyond normal, with fever, jaundice, typhoid, and diarrhea among the most common presentations, in addition to viral infections. Health experts warn that waterlogged areas will boost mosquito breeding, increasing the upcoming risk of dengue, malaria, and chikungunya. Parents are advised to offer boiled water and avoid stale or street foods, and to seek prompt medical evaluation for high fever, vomiting, or diarrhea rather than self-treatment. Doctors attribute the surge to humidity and temperature fluctuations that favor bacterial growth. The development highlights the need for vigilant monitoring and preventive measures during Jabalpur’s monsoon season to curb both waterborne and vector-borne illnesses.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Centre approves dengue vaccine for the first time in India; who will be able to receive 'Qdenga'?
article.articleSummary: India approves Takeda's Qdenga, the first dengue vaccine, for 4-60 years old, by DCGI. Qdenga is a tetravalent live-attenuated vaccine with two 0.5 mL doses given 3 months apart; no prior dengue testing required. The approval comes as India records heavy dengue burden, with 113,000+ cases reported in 2025, though actual numbers are believed higher. WHO has endorsed use in dengue-prone areas and granted prequalification; since 2022, Qdenga has been approved in 43 countries across Asia, Europe, and Latin America, with over 32 million doses administered. In clinical trials, after the second dose at 12 months, vaccine efficacy against dengue infection was 80.2%, and hospitalization risk reduction was 90.4%; long-term data show 4.5-year protection against hospitalization at 84.1%, and up to seven years of safety and efficacy. India's Takeda will begin market introduction, but launch date and price remain undisclosed. Complementary mosquito control and personal protection remain essential.

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو تشهد "أسوأ موجة" Ebolا منذ سنوات والإصابات 2344
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Congo experiences its "worst Ebola wave" in years, with 2,344 cases.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 2,344 confirmed Ebola cases and 930 deaths as of July 18, 2026, in what officials describe as the fastest-spreading outbreak and the third-largest Ebola event globally. The surge is linked to the rare Bundibugyo strain, which has no licensed vaccines or approved treatments, complicating containment. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned that this is the fastest Ebola wave to date, surpassing 2,000 cases within about two months of onset. More than 80% of recent infections occur in individuals not identified among known contacts, signaling active, untraced transmission chains. National authorities, alongside WHO and partners, are sustaining surge efforts, expanding treatment centers, and reinforcing infection prevention and control measures to limit spread.

article.articleHeadline: At least 930 people died in Congo's Ebola outbreak - Africa - World
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in eastern Congo accelerates, with 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths reported as of Saturday. The Bundibugyo virus drives the outbreak, the fastest-growing Ebola event on record, across five eastern provinces, with Ituri hardest hit amid rebel violence. There is no approved vaccine or treatment. Transmission occurs from wild animals and between people through contact with bodily fluids and contaminated surfaces. Response is hindered by safety fears, with 12 attacks on health facilities and teams; many health workers have left their posts, and 36 infected health workers have died. The World Health Organization notes about 80% of new cases arise from unknown transmission chains, signaling rapid spread. As of the latest update, 724 patients are in isolation or hospitalized, and 22 recoveries were recorded in 24 hours, as containment efforts intensify.

article.articleHeadline: Canada bars foreign travelers over Ebola outbreak -- RT Africa
article.articleSummary: Canada will temporarily bar foreign nationals who have recently visited the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) from entering the country, effective 11:59 PM on Monday; applies to those who were in DR Congo in the previous 21 days; airlines must prevent affected passengers from boarding to Canada. Canadian citizens and permanent residents returning from DR Congo, Uganda, or South Sudan may enter but must undergo health assessments and 21-day quarantine. The policy, in place until August 29, follows earlier immigration suspensions for residents of the three countries; health risk to Canadians deemed low and no travel-related cases reported in Canada. WHO warns that travel bans risk stigma and do not define transmission; Ebola Bundibugyo strain lacks licensed vaccine or specific treatment. DR Congo reports 2,344 confirmed infections and 930 deaths; Uganda 20 cases and two deaths; Oxford began Phase I vaccine trial (ChAdOx1 BDBV).

article.articleHeadline: Enam Warga Meninggal Akibat Leptospirosis di Kota Semarang hingga Pertengahan 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Six Residents Die from Leptospirosis in Semarang City as of Mid-2026
article.articleSummary: Six residents in Semarang City, Central Java, Indonesia have died from leptospirosis as of mid-2026, according to the city Health Office. The six fatalities are linked to a rise in cases observed since late 2025 in densely populated, flood- and tidal-prone neighborhoods. Health officials note that crowded housing and frequent inundation facilitate transmission, particularly when immune defenses are low. In response, the Health Office, with primary health centers (puskesmas) and local community leaders, has launched a rodent-control campaign (OTT) that installs traps at high-risk sites and evaluates the intervention. Leptospira bacteria carried by rats, and related pathogens such as hantavirus, can cause serious illness, including kidney and heart complications, if not treated promptly. Efforts emphasize rodent eradication and sanitation to curb spread in vulnerable areas.

article.articleHeadline: At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak - CNBC TV18
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, Congo's eastern Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo virus, has 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths. In the last 24 hours (Friday into Saturday), 37 deaths were recorded, marking the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. The Bundibugyo strain is less common and has no approved vaccine or treatment. Ebola spreads from wild animals and through human contact with infected bodily fluids and contaminated surfaces; it is highly contagious and often fatal. The outbreak spans five eastern provinces, with Ituri hardest hit amid rampant rebel violence. Since mid-May, at least 12 attacks on health facilities and teams have occurred, and 36 health workers have died from infection. WHO notes about 80% of new cases emerge from unknown transmission chains. The health ministry reports 724 patients in isolation or hospital care, and 22 recoveries in 24 hours; response efforts are being intensified despite safety fears.

article.articleHeadline: RDCongo.- El brote de ébola decretado en mayo en RDC deja ya cerca...
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC - The Ebola outbreak declared in May in the DRC is already close to...
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak declared in mid-May in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached about 2,344 cases and 930 deaths, with 724 patients in isolation or hospitalized and 466 recovered. The case-fatality rate is 39.7% and contact tracing covers 85.8%. Five provinces are affected, led by Ituri (epicenter), with new transmissions in North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo, and Alto Uélé. In Ituri, 27 of 36 health zones are affected; North Kivu 11 of 34; South Kivu 1 of 34; Alto Uélé 4 of 13; Tshopo 3 of 23, including Kisangani. Sud-Kivu records 52 days without new cases. Médecins du Monde warns the response is highly complex amid conflict, population displacement and weak health systems, as Ebola, cholera, measles, and mpox are tackled simultaneously. Public messaging on vaccination, hygiene and rapid care is hindered by misinformation, straining already limited services. The DRC remains the most experienced Ebola country, with the Kasai outbreak ending in 2025.

article.articleHeadline: India Approves First Dengue Vaccine QDENGA for Ages 4 to 60
article.articleSummary: India approves first dengue vaccine QDENGA for ages 4-60, with no pre-screening blood test required and protection against all four dengue serotypes. In India, dengue remains high-era, with all four serotypes active across multiple regions. QDENGA is given as two 0.5 ml subcutaneous injections three months apart. Approval is based on Takeda’s DEN-302 Phase III Indian data showing safety and immune response in 4-60-year-olds, with seven years of follow-up indicating sustained protection and reduced dengue-related hospitalizations across serotypes. Globally, QDENGA has been approved since 2022 in 43 countries, with more than 32 million doses distributed. The decision strengthens India’s dengue prevention strategy alongside vector control, surveillance, and public health measures. Takeda notes the vaccine is effective regardless of prior infection history, aiding rapid rollout in high-burden areas.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Now dengue-related deaths will be prevented as India approves the first dengue vaccine.
article.articleSummary: India approves Takeda’s QDENGA—the first dengue vaccine—for use in individuals aged 4–60, regardless of prior dengue infection. article.articleHeadline: Congo-Ebola : des leaders communautaires formés pour renforcer la prévention
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo-Ebola: Community Leaders Trained to Strengthen Prevention.
article.articleSummary: Community leaders in Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo, were trained on July 17 to strengthen vigilance and response to Ebola virus threats. The session, organized by CNORE in partnership with Globus, aimed to bolster community capacities for prevention, detection, and response as Ebola persists in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. Participants learned transmission modes, warning signs, preventive measures, and procedures for suspected cases, with emphasis on rapid reporting to health authorities and disseminating best practices within communities. The action reflects regional health strengthening and ongoing preparedness to prevent Ebola's introduction into the Republic of Congo amid cross-border risk. No case counts were reported in the article.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ・エボラ：予防強化のためコミュニティリーダーを訓練
triage.triage_reason: 記事はコンゴ共和国での予防訓練活動を報じるものであり、DRCでのエボラ流行は既知の継続的状況として言及されているのみで新規症例数の報告はない。地域拡大の具体的兆候はないが、DRC情勢は継続監視が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はコンゴ共和国（対象国外）における予防訓練であり、症例数の報告はない。DRCでのエボラ流行は既知の背景情報として言及されている。新規性・具体的リスク情報が乏しいため続報を注視すべき。

article.articleHeadline: Вспышка Эболы в ДР Конго продолжает набирать обороты
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the DR Congo continues to gain momentum.
article.articleSummary: As of 20 July 2026, lab-confirmed Ebola virus disease cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) total 2,344, up 77 in the last 24 hours, with 930 deaths (case fatality rate 39.7%). Hospitals and isolation centers currently house 724 patients. Contact tracing of exposed individuals stands at 85.8%. The outbreak began on 15 May in eastern DRC and Uganda, with five Congolese provinces affected and the epicenter in Ituri Province. Ongoing transmission signals momentum across the region, underscoring the need for sustained clinical management, isolation capacity, and rigorous surveillance. The bulletin highlights daily updates from authorities, emphasizing monitoring of disease spread, patient outcomes, and effectiveness of contact tracing in mitigating further cases.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、勢いを増し続ける
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で2,344例・930人死亡（致死率39.7%）の大規模エボラ流行が継続し、ウガンダへの越境拡大も確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの拡大も報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。5州にわたる感染拡大と高い致死率から継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 退伍軍人病個案　過去一周錄2宗社區感染
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ex-servicemen’s disease case: two community transmissions recorded in the past week.
article.articleSummary: Two community-acquired cases of Legionnaires’ disease were identified in Hong Kong between July 12 and 18, 2026. A 67-year-old man from Kowloon City and a 69-year-old woman from the Central and Western District, both with chronic illnesses, were confirmed as part of the Centre for Health Protection’s ongoing surveillance. Epidemiological investigations are under way to determine infection sources and high-risk exposures, with preliminary findings indicating sporadic cases not linked to earlier local cases. As of July 20, 2026, Hong Kong has recorded 95 Legionnaires’ disease cases this year; 2025 saw 167 cases and 2024 had 135. The CHP notes Legionella bacteria can survive in various water environments, including cooling towers, underscoring environmental tracing needs. No evidence of imported or exported case connections is reported.

triage.headline_ja: 退役軍人病(レジオネラ症)、過去1週間で地域感染2件を記録
triage.triage_reason: 散発的な地域感染例であり、過去との関連は否定され、香港では例年一定数発生している疾患であるため、国際的拡大や重大な公衆衛生上のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: レジオネラ症は環境由来でヒト-ヒト感染しない疾患。香港では例年100件以上発生しており、今回の2件も既存サーベイランスの一部として検出された散発例。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو: ارتفاع إصابات إيبولا إلى 2344 والوفيات 930 حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Congo: Ebola infections rise to 2,344 and 930 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports Ebola outbreak: 2,344 confirmed infections and 930 deaths; 37 new fatalities in the last 24 hours as of Saturday. The eastern provinces, notably Ituri, remain hardest hit. The outbreak, declared May 15, is the fastest on record. Caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which no licensed vaccine or treatment exists. Security concerns and attacks on health facilities/teams (at least 12) hinder containment; health workers have protested delayed salaries. 36 health workers have died from infection. About 724 patients are currently in isolation centers and hospitals; authorities say they are scaling up response measures and interventions to curb spread.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ:エボラ感染者2,344人に増加、死者930人
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱がコンゴ東部で急速に拡大しており、症例数・死者数ともに多く、ワクチン・治療薬未承認かつ治安要因で対応が困難なため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大なシグナルである。
triage.notes: 史上最速の拡大速度とされ、医療従事者36人が死亡、医療施設への攻撃など治安上の課題も深刻。ワクチン・治療薬が存在しないBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる流行であり、国際的な支援・監視が必要と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: ثبت ۹۳۰ مورد مرگ ناشی از ابولا در کنگو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 930 Ebola deaths recorded in Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused at least 930 deaths among 2,344 confirmed cases, according to the country’s Ministry of Health and reported via AP/Ilna. As of Saturday, 37 new deaths were recorded in the last 24 hours, one of the highest daily tallies to date, underscoring the ongoing severity and mortality of the outbreak. The brief report provides no further infection-source details. Public health authorities continue monitoring and responding across affected regions within Congo, maintaining containment and surveillance initiatives. These figures reflect the current burden as of the 2026-07-20 publication date, highlighting the seriousness of the situation and the need for sustained public health measures.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴで930人がエボラで死亡
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱の大規模流行(2344例中930死亡)が継続し、直近24時間で37人死亡と増加傾向にあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: 感染源の詳細は不明。死亡率が高く、直近の死亡数増加が懸念される。続報でヒト-ヒト感染拡大や国際拡散リスクの確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: У ДР Конго кількість померлих через спалах Еболи зросла до 930
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the death toll from the Ebola outbreak has risen to 930.
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak in eastern provinces (Ituri) has reached 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths as of 20 July 2026, per Congolese MoH and AP via Ukrinform. The outbreak, declared 15 May, is the fastest-growing on record. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus is responsible; there is no approved vaccine or established treatment protocol for this strain. Daily toll rose to 37 deaths in the last 24 hours. Healthcare worker safety concerns have limited care, with at least 12 attacks on facilities/teams, and 36 health workers infected and dead. MoH reports 724 patients currently in isolation and hospital wards. The surge underscores strain on Ituri province's health system amid ongoing transmission and containment challenges.

triage.headline_ja: DR コンゴでエボラ流行による死者数が930人に増加
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク）に該当し、致死性の高いブンディブジョ型エボラウイルスによる史上最速の流行拡大とワクチン・治療プロトコルの欠如、医療従事者への攻撃が確認されているため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: ブンディブジョ型エボラウイルスは承認ワクチン・確立された治療法が存在せず、致死率が高い。医療施設・医療従事者への攻撃(12件)と36人の医療従事者感染・死亡が報告されており、対応能力の限界が懸念される。史上最速の流行拡大とされており、国際的な支援ニーズが高いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola deja ya cerca de 2.350 positivos y más de 925 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak has already left nearly 2,350 positive cases and more than 925 dead.
article.articleSummary: The Ebola outbreak declared in mid-May in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 2,344 cases and 930 deaths. Of these, 724 are in isolation or hospitalized and 466 have recovered (case fatality 39.7%; contact tracing 85.8%). Five provinces are affected, led by Ituri, with new cases in Tshopo, Alto Uélé, and in North and South Kivu, the latter partially controlled by the M23 rebel group. Kisangani, in Tshopo, a major logistics hub, underscores elevated spread risk. Doctors of the World warns the response faces a highly complex context due to conflict, displacement, and a health system stretched by four concurrent epidemics: Ebola, cholera, measles, mpox. RDC, which declared the end of its previous Ebola outbreak in Kasai in December 2025, has extensive Ebola experience since 1976.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行、感染者約2,350人、死者925人以上に達する
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部で拡大中のエボラ出血熱の流行が5州に及び、致死率約39.7%、主要物流拠点や武装勢力支配地域も含むため、国際的拡大リスクが高い重大なシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: コンゴ民主共和国では、エボラ、コレラ、麻疹、Mpoxの4つの流行が同時進行しており、武力衝突と住民移動により対応が非常に複雑化している。物流拠点キサンガニでの感染拡大は特に懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: बस्तर में फैल रहा मिक्स मलेरिया, 8426 लोग संक्रमित; जानें लक्षण और बचाव के तरीके
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mixed malaria spreading in Bastar, 8,426 people infected; learn the symptoms and ways to prevent.
article.articleSummary: Mixed malaria outbreak in Bastar division, Chhattisgarh, with 8,426 malaria cases since January 2026, including 254 mixed infections of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax. Over 663,000 blood samples have been tested. District counts: Bijapur 3,173; Sukma 1,686; Dantewada 1,344; Narayanpur 896; Bastar 809; Kondagaon 329; Kanker 189. Mixed malaria occurs when both parasite species are transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes, and is considered more dangerous due to potential severe complications affecting brain, kidneys, and liver. Common symptoms include high fever, chills, headache, vomiting, fatigue, and anemia, with fever potentially recurring. Preventive measures urged: eliminate standing water around homes, use bed nets regularly, and seek timely diagnosis and treatment for fever to curb spread. (Date reference: 2026-07-20.)

triage.headline_ja: バスタルで混合マラリアが拡大、8,426人が感染；症状と予防法を知る
triage.triage_reason: インド・チャッティースガル州バスタル地域の風土病性マラリア流行で症例数は多いが、毎年発生する既知の地域流行であり異常性・国際的拡大リスクは低い。重症化リスクや媒介環境の継続性からWPRO基準は一部該当するが、社会的関心・国際支援の必要性に関する情報が不足しているため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はヒンディー語の地方紙で、インド国内(チャッティースガル州バスタル地域)における風土病性マラリア流行を報じている。バングラデシュは発生地域リストに含まれるが記事主題ではないため除外。地方保健当局による血液検査・予防啓発活動が進行中で、国内対応可能な範囲と見られる。

article.articleHeadline: La RDC supera los 2.300 casos de ébola mientras la OMS alerta de una crisis agravada por cuatro epidemias simultáneas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The DRC surpasses 2,300 Ebola cases as the WHO warns of a crisis aggravated by four simultaneous epidemics.
article.articleSummary: As of July 18, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 2,344 confirmed Ebola cases, 930 deaths, 466 recoveries, and 724 hospitalized or isolated patients (case fatality 39.7%). Five provinces are affected: Haut-Uélé, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. 83 new Ebola cases and 22 recoveries were recorded, with contact tracing at 85.8%. Ituri remains the main transmission focus; Kivu del Sur and Tshopo are stable. The World Health Organization warns of rapid spread and elevated regional risk due to mobility, insecurity, and surveillance gaps. The country also faces cholera, measles, and mpox, straining a weakened health system. Doctors of the World notes competition for resources across diseases: Ebola isolation, cholera WASH, measles vaccination, mpox surveillance. Overlapping symptoms hinder early diagnosis, requiring strengthened laboratory capacity and surveillance. In Kivu del Sur, measles totals 1,583 cases and 50 deaths; cholera rises (275 weekly cases, +23%). Mpox remains active.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ感染者2,300人超え WHOは4つの同時流行による危機を警告
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱が複数州で拡大し死亡率約40%、コレラ・麻疹・Mpoxとの同時流行で医療体制が逼迫しており、WHOも地域的リスクの高まりを警告しているためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: エボラ、コレラ、麻疹、Mpoxの4疾患が同時流行し、資源競合と診断困難が生じている複合危機。WHOが地域拡大リスクを警告している点は重視すべき。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : l'administrateur d'Irumu appelle la population à soutenir la riposte contre Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: the administrator of Irumu calls on the population to support the Ebola response.
article.articleSummary: As of 20 July 2026, in Ituri province, the administrator of Irumu territory, Colonel N'siro Simba Bunga Jean, urged residents to back the Ebola virus disease (EVD) response during a 18 July visit to Nyankunde, capital of the Andisoma chiefdom, after deadly clashes on 15 July that killed a militiaman. The unrest led to the withdrawal of international aid groups amid safety fears. The official said discussions are underway with health authorities to allow the return of international organizations to Nyankunde and to relaunch patient treatment. The EVD response remains hampered by security challenges in Ituri, raising fear and limiting humanitarian access in insecure areas, with Ituri still the epicenter of the outbreak. No case or death counts were provided in the report.

triage.headline_ja: イツリ州:イルム行政官がエボラ対応への協力を住民に呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 既知のエボラ流行地域（イツリ州）で治安悪化により国際支援団体が撤退し対応が中断、感染対応能力に支障が出ている。エボラの重篤性と対応中断による感染拡大リスクからフルRRAへの移行が適切。
triage.notes: 治安不安（民兵衝突による死者）により国際援助団体がニャンクンデから撤退し、患者治療が中断。行政当局は保健当局と国際機関の復帰について協議中。症例数・死亡者数の具体的報告はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Viatris launches support project in Maharashtra to combat DR-TB
article.articleSummary: Viatris subsidiary Mylan Laboratories launches an 18-month TB support project in Nagpur, Maharashtra, focusing on drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) to strengthen diagnostics, prevention, and nutrition under a Public-Private Partnership with Doctors For You, Nagpur Municipal Corporation, and City TB Office. Part of India's National TB Elimination Program, the project follows the Detect-Treat-Prevent-Build approach, aiming to improve molecular diagnostic capacity and TB preventive treatment coverage in the Nagpur district. Key activities include processing more than 26,000 samples across four Nagpur locations, household tracing of confirmed TB and DR-TB cases targeting 22,000 households, and distribution of more than 450 nutrition kits to TB/DR-TB patients. Since 2020, Viatris has screened over 1.5 million people for TB in India and supported 58,000 people in Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra. Globally, Viatris has helped enable DR-TB treatment access for over 300,000 patients.

triage.headline_ja: Viatris、マハーラーシュトラ州で薬剤耐性結核(DR-TB)対策の支援プロジェクトを開始
triage.triage_reason: 既存の結核対策プログラムを強化する企業支援活動の発表であり、新規の異常な公衆衛生事象ではないため。
triage.notes: 記事は製薬企業による既存の結核対策プログラム支援の発表であり、新規の感染症アウトブレイクや異常事象を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: India Approves First Dengue Vaccine QDENGA for Ages 4-60 Years
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-20, India approves its first dengue vaccine, QDENGA, for individuals aged 4 to 60 years. The Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) granted approval under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials (NDCT) Rules, 2019, marking a milestone in India's public health response. Dengue, a mosquito-borne disease that annually affects millions across the country, now has an approved vaccination option aimed at broad age coverage. The report highlights this as a major breakthrough to strengthen dengue control and reduce disease burden, though it provides no details on dosing, rollout timelines, or population coverage.

triage.headline_ja: インド、初のデング熱ワクチン「QDENGA」を4~60歳向けに承認
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はワクチン承認に関するもので、疾病の発生・拡大や公衆衛生上の異常事態を報じるものではないため、シグナルとしての該当性は低い。
triage.notes: デング熱自体の発生状況やアウトブレイクを示す情報はなく、ワクチン承認という規制上のニュースであるため対象国の発生地域としては記載せず。

article.articleHeadline: 37 حالة وفاة جديدة بفيروس إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية خلال 24 ساعة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 37 new Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo within 24 hours.
article.articleSummary: On 20 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reported at least 930 Ebola-related deaths among 2,344 confirmed cases in the eastern outbreak, with 37 new fatalities in the last 24 hours. The outbreak, first reported in mid-May, is the fastest on record for Ebola. It is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a less common species with no licensed vaccine or approved treatment. The Ituri province, the hardest hit, has faced security challenges, including more than 12 attacks on facilities and response teams since the outbreak began. Health-system strain is evident, with salary delays contributing to healthcare worker resignations and at least 36 workers reported dead from Ebola. The report includes a site disclaimer; no details are given on imported or exported cases.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国で24時間以内にエボラ出血熱による新たな死者37人
triage.triage_reason: 致死率が高く症例数・死者数も多数（症例2,344件、死者930人）、記録上最速の拡大速度、ワクチン未承認の稀少株、治安悪化による対応困難など複数のIHR基準・WPRO基準に該当するため。
triage.notes: Ituri州はDRC国内の地域であり、対象国リストにはDRC自体が該当。国境を越えた輸出入例の詳細は記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-Ausbruch in Kongo-Kinshasa: fast 1000 Todesopfer
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo-Kinshasa: nearly 1,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (Congo-Kinshasa) has so far caused nearly 1,000 deaths, with at least 930 fatalities among 2,344 confirmed cases, more than one-third of infections resulting in death. The outbreak began a little over two months ago in the east and is described as the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record. Canada imposed a temporary entry ban for foreign nationals who were in DR Congo within the past 21 days, effective today; the United States has adopted a similar measure for travelers who were in DR Congo in the past 21 days. The World Health Organization advises against travel or trade restrictions, citing a low risk of international spread.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ（キンシャサ）でのエボラ出血熱流行：死者数ほぼ1000人に
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部で史上最速拡大とされるエボラ流行が発生し、死者約1000人・致死率3分の1超と深刻。米国・カナダが入国制限を実施しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: 米国・カナダは発生地域ではなく、入国制限を実施した国として記載されているため verified_locations には含めない。WHOは渡航・貿易制限に反対を表明しているが、実際に2カ国が制限を導入している点は国際的懸念の高さを示す。

article.articleHeadline: Число заболевших Эболой в ДР Конго перешагнуло за 2,3 тыс.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in DR Congo has surpassed 2,300.
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, DR Congo reports 2,344 laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases, up 77 from the previous day. Total deaths reach 930, with 37 fatalities in the past 24 hours, yielding a case-fatality rate of about 39.7%. There are 724 patients with confirmed Ebola under hospital and quarantine isolation. Contact tracing has reached 85.8% of identified contacts, aiding containment. The National Public Health Institute (INSP) has previously reported 828 deaths, with updated figures reflecting ongoing transmission. The report underscores sustained high mortality and ongoing outbreak conditions in DR Congo, highlighting continued laboratory confirmation, patient isolation, and contact-tracing efforts as critical components of the response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者数が2,300人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国で2,344例・930人死亡（致死率約39.7%）と大規模に拡大しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるため。
triage.notes: 致死率約39.7%と非常に高く、症例数・死亡者数ともに継続的に増加している。接触者追跡率85.8%は一定の対応能力を示すが、感染拡大が続いているため注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie d'Ebola en République démocratique du Congo a fait au moins 930 morts | L'actualité
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed at least 930 people | L'actualité
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo caused by Bundibugyo virus; at least 930 deaths among 2,344 confirmed cases since outbreak declared May 15 in eastern DRC; fastest-growing Ebola outbreak. The Bundibugyo strain has no vaccine or approved treatment; virus is highly contagious and can spread to humans from wild animals and via contact with bodily fluids (vomit, blood, semen) and contaminated surfaces and objects (bedding, clothing). Five provinces are affected, dominated by Ituri, with security concerns limiting interventions. Authorities report 724 patients in isolation or hospital care; 22 new recoveries in 24 hours. WHO warns that about 80% of new cases arise from unknown transmission chains, suggesting accelerating spread. There have been at least 12 attacks on health facilities; at least 36 health workers have died. Canada plans to ban foreign nationals who visited DRC in the last 21 days, effective Monday at 23:59.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱、死者数少なくとも930人に
triage.triage_reason: ワクチン・治療法のないブンディブギョ株による急速拡大中のエボラ流行で、死者930人・感染拡大が加速しており、国際的な渡航制限（カナダの入国禁止措置）も発生しているためIHR基準を複数満たす。

article.articleHeadline: भारत ने 4 से 60 साल की उम्र के लोगों के लिए पहली डेंगू वैक्सीन 'क्यूडेंगा' को दी मंजूरी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India approves the first dengue vaccine 'Qdenga' for people aged 4 to 60 years.
article.articleSummary: India’s Drugs Controller General has approved Takeda’s dengue vaccine Qdenga for individuals aged 4–60, marking the country’s first dengue vaccine authorization. The shot can be given to anyone regardless of prior dengue infection, with no pre-vaccination testing required. Qdenga is administered as two 0.5 mL subcutaneous injections three months apart. The decision draws on data from India’s Den-302 Phase 3 trial evaluating safety and immune response, and a global program involving over 28,000 participants across 19 Phase 1–3 trials. Long-term follow-up up to seven years indicates protection against dengue infection and hospitalization caused by all four serotypes. Since 2022, Qdenga has received approvals in 43 countries and distributed more than 32 million doses. With India facing high dengue burden and circulation of all four serotypes, the vaccine is a key addition to the national dengue prevention strategy alongside vector control, surveillance, and public health measures.

triage.headline_ja: インドが4歳から60歳の人々を対象とした初のデング熱ワクチン「Qdenga」を承認
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はワクチン承認に関する規制・保健政策上の話題であり、新規の感染症発生や異常な公衆衛生事象を報告するものではないため、シグナルとしての該当性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事はデング熱ワクチンの承認という保健政策ニュースであり、感染症の発生・拡大を報告するものではない。インドはデング熱の高負荷地域であるが、本記事自体は既存の予防策強化に関する内容。

article.articleHeadline: Kanada, Ebola Salgınına Yönelik Yeni Sınır Önlemleri Açıkladı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Canada announced new border measures aimed at the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Canada's Public Health Agency announced temporary border measures to curb Ebola virus entry and transmission. Foreign nationals who have spent the past 21 days in the Democratic Republic of the Congo will be prohibited from entering Canada, with the rules taking effect July 21, 2026 and lasting through August 29, 2026, under the existing orders framework. The measures are intended to reduce travel-related Ebola risk and ensure safe processing of travelers, including humanitarian aid workers. Canadian citizens, permanent residents, and persons protected by the Indian Act are not subject to new entry bans; however, upon arrival they must undergo health screening and complete a 21-day quarantine. The agency notes there have been no travel-associated Ebola cases in Canada to date. The measures are part of ongoing border controls to mitigate imported risk.

triage.headline_ja: カナダ、エボラ出血熱流行に対する新たな国境対策を発表
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱流行を受け、カナダが渡航制限を導入したことは国際的拡大リスクと渡航制限の両基準に該当し、IHR基準を複数満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はカナダの国境対策に関する内容だが、根本的な感染源はDRCでのエボラ出血熱流行であるため、DRCのみを発生地域として検証。カナダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: ठाण्यात साथीच्या आजारांवर लगाम; मलेरिया-डेंग्याच्या रुग्णसंख्येत मोठी घट
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Curbs on communicable diseases in Thane; malaria and dengue cases fall significantly.
article.articleSummary: Thane City’s health department reports a sharp year-on-year decline in vector-borne diseases during 1 June–15 July 2026, compared with the same period in 2025. Malaria 45 cases, dengue 40, chikungunya 1, H1N1 16, H3N2 2, leptospirosis 6, cholera zero. In 2025, malaria 186, dengue 210, chikungunya 33, H3N2 35, leptospirosis 2, cholera 1. Reductions are attributed to a later monsoon with less sustained rainfall, reducing mosquito breeding, and intensified preventive measures. Daily fever surveillance by city health centers, regular surveys of water-holding containers at homes, construction sites, and public places to locate breeding sites. The Filariasis Department conducted regular fogging and insecticide spraying. Public outreach through banners, posters, hoardings, stickers, and campaigns urged residents to avoid standing water, seek prompt fever assessment, and maintain cleanliness. Chief Medical Officer Dr. Prasad Patil notes effective control of vector-borne diseases this year.

triage.headline_ja: ターネー市で伝染病を抑制；マラリア・デング熱の患者数が大幅減少
triage.triage_reason: 記事はインド・ターネー市における媒介性疾患の症例数が前年比で大幅減少したという内容であり、公衆衛生上の懸念や異常事態ではなく、むしろ対策の成功を報告するもの。

article.articleHeadline: To måneder inn i ebola-utbruddet: Responsen må trappes opp raskt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Two months into the Ebola outbreak: The response must be ramped up quickly.
article.articleSummary: Two months after the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) was declared, more than 2,000 confirmed cases and 750 deaths have been reported, driven by Bundibugyo virus. It is the third-largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record: cases rose from about 650 to nearly 2,000 in under five weeks; deaths from roughly 130 to over 700. Ituri Province remains the epicenter, accounting for ~90% of cases, with spread to Nord-Kivu, South-Kivu, and Tshopo. Movement restrictions, border closures, and self-monitoring measures hinder deployment of specialized Ebola personnel. Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières has established treatment centers in Bunia, Mongbwalu, Komanda, Goma, Butembo, Bukavu, and Lwiro, plus more than 15 isolation units, and strengthened infection prevention. Hundreds of tons of supplies have been shipped; over 2,200 staff are involved, including 800 health ministry personnel supported by MSF. The situation unfolds amid conflict and other crises, with the rainy season expected to raise malaria cases.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱アウトブレイクから2ヶ月：対応の急速な強化が必要
triage.triage_reason: DRCでBundibugyoウイルスによるエボラ出血熱が2000例超・死亡750人超と急拡大し、史上3番目に大きく最速の増加を示す大規模アウトブレイクであり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当するため。
triage.notes: 紛争地域での対応であり、雨季によるマラリア増加も懸念材料として言及されている。国境封鎖・移動制限により専門人員の展開が阻害されている点も国際的拡大リスクを示唆。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus DBD di Klaten Turun Signifikan, Warga Diminta Tetap Waspada
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever cases in Klaten decline significantly; residents urged to remain vigilant.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever cases in Klaten Regency, Central Java, declined to 112 cases with 1 death through week 26 of 2026, down from 363 cases and 3 deaths in the same period last year. Klaten Health Office head Anggit Budiarto attributed the fall to intensified mosquito-nest elimination campaigns (PSN) and active larva-monitoring by jumantik volunteers, along with improved environmental cleanliness. The coordinated PSN drive and rapid medical response were cited as key factors in the significant reduction, with ongoing socialization efforts to maintain vigilance. Despite the drop, residents were urged to stay vigilant and sustain hygienic environments to prevent resurgence. The information was confirmed by Media Indonesia on July 20, 2026.

article.articleHeadline: भारत ने 4 से 60 साल की उम्र के लोगों के लिए पहली डेंगू वैक्सीन 'क्यूडेंगा' को दी मंजूरी | India approves first dengue vaccine QDENGA for people aged 4-60 years
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India approves first dengue vaccine QDENGA for people aged 4-60 years
article.articleSummary: India approves Takeda's QDENGA dengue vaccine for individuals aged 4–60, marking the country's first dengue vaccine approval by the DCGI. The vaccine is given as two 0.5 mL subcutaneous doses 3 months apart and requires no prior dengue testing. As India remains among the countries with the highest dengue burden and four serotypes circulate, this approval strengthens its dengue prevention strategy. Since its 2022 launch, QDENGA has secured approvals in 43 countries and distributed over 32 million doses. Indian phase 3 Den-302 data, plus long-term follow-up up to seven years, show safety and immune response in 4–60-year-olds and protection against dengue infection and hospitalizations from all four serotypes. The decision complements vector control, surveillance, and public health measures in India."
