article.articleHeadline: Historic milestone for India as country's first dengue vaccine approved, people from age 4-60 can now...
article.articleSummary: India's Drug Controller General (DCGI) has approved Takeda's QDENGA, the country's first dengue vaccine, for individuals aged 4 to 60. The tetravalent, live-attenuated vaccine requires no prior blood testing or infection screening and is administered as two 0.5 ml subcutaneous injections three months apart. The approval comes as India bears nearly one-third of the global dengue burden with all four dengue virus serotypes co-circulating nationwide. QDENGA's global development program includes 19 Phase I–III trials with more than 28,000 participants, and India's DEN-302 Phase III trial supported safety and immune response in ages 4–60. Long-term follow-up of up to seven years indicates sustained protection against dengue infection and dengue-related hospitalization for all four serotypes. Since its 2022 launch, QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries with over 32 million doses distributed.

triage.headline_ja: インドにとって歴史的な節目：国内初のデング熱ワクチンが承認、4歳から60歳までの人々が接種可能に
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はデング熱ワクチン（QDENGA）の承認に関する規制・保健政策ニュースであり、新規の感染症発生や公衆衛生上の異常事態を報告するものではないため、シグナルとして扱う必要はない。
triage.notes: 記事はインドにおけるデング熱ワクチン承認の発表であり、新規アウトブレイクや感染拡大の報告ではない。インドがデング熱流行国であることは既知情報であり、本記事自体は感染症危機事象ではなくワクチン承認という保健政策ニュースのため、verified_locationsも空とした。

article.articleHeadline: India Gets Its First Dengue Vaccine: Who Can Take It, Price, Effectiveness And Everything You Need To Know
article.articleSummary: India approves QDENGA, Takeda’s tetravalent dengue vaccine, for 4–60-year-olds in two doses with no pre-vaccination testing. It protects against all four dengue serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4) and can be given regardless of prior infection. 2025 dengue cases in India reached 121,824 with 131 deaths per NCVBDC; 2024 saw 297 deaths and 2023 had 485. Efficacy data suggest 61–80% reduction in moderate dengue and 84–90% reduction in dengue-related hospitalisations after two doses. Estimated cost per dose: Rs 6,000–12,000, with domestic production expanding via Hyderabad-based Biological E to 50 million doses/year, and Takeda aiming for 100 million doses annually by decade’s end. The vaccine supplements, not replaces, existing dengue prevention—mosquito control, repellents, protective clothing, window nets, and bed nets.

triage.notes: デング熱はインドで毎年流行している既知の疾患であり、本記事は新ワクチン承認という医療政策トピックが主眼。感染者数・死亡者数は既存データの引用であり新規アウトブレイクの報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Salgın dünyada hızla yayılıyor! Yetkililerden korkutan açıklama: Ölü sayısı 930'a yükseldi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The outbreak is spreading rapidly worldwide! Alarming statement from authorities: the death toll has risen to 930.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, declared May 15, with 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths (case fatality ~40%). Most infections are in Ituri Province in the northeast. Security issues and difficulties in tracing contacts hinder response efforts. The Ebola virus was first identified in 1976 in Nzara, Sudan, and Yambuku in what was then Zaire; this outbreak involves the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved vaccine. Historical context includes the 2014–2017 West Africa outbreak in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone, causing about 30,000 infections and over 11,000 deaths. WHO emphasizes diagnosis, rapid contact tracing, and supportive care as key control measures for this strain.

triage.headline_ja: 世界で感染拡大！当局から衝撃の発表：死者数930人に上昇
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国（イトゥリ州）でエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株、承認済みワクチンなし）が流行中。2,344例確認、死者930人（致死率約40%）と深刻な公衆衛生上の影響があり、治安上の問題で接触者追跡が困難なため国際的拡大リスクも高い。
triage.notes: 発生地域リストにはSudan、Sierra Leone、Angola、Liberia、Burundi、Guinea、Yambukuなどが含まれるが、これらは1976年の初発見地や2014-2017年西アフリカ流行の歴史的言及であり、現在の流行地はDRCイトゥリ州のみ。ワクチン未承認のブンディブギョ株であることが特に懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: 민주콩고 에볼라 확산 계속...확진 2천300명·사망 900명 넘어
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo... 2,300 confirmed cases, more than 900 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to spread. As of July 18, cumulative Ebola cases reached 2,344 with 930 deaths; 466 recoveries. The fatality rate stands at 39.7%. Three days after July 15, the numbers rose by 220 cases and 102 deaths. Contact tracing reached 85.8%. WHO warned that about 80% of new cases in the past week were not linked to known cases, implying many undetected transmission chains. Attacks on health facilities and personnel are hampering response, with health workers affected by wage arrears causing strikes and walkouts; at least 12 attacks on facilities and staff have been recorded since the outbreak was declared on May 15. The situation highlights ongoing challenge of outbreak control amid insecurity and misinformation in local communities.

triage.headline_ja: 民主コンゴでエボラ拡大続く…確定患者2,300人・死者900人超
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ大規模流行が拡大継続し、致死率約40%、未追跡感染連鎖が多数存在するなど公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクがあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 医療施設への攻撃や医療従事者のストライキなど対応能力低下要因があり、WHOも未検出の感染連鎖の多さを警告している。フルRRAでの詳細評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Goma confrontée à une recrudescence des cas de choléra
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Goma faces a resurgence of cholera cases.
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, Goma in North Kivu, DR Congo, faces a resurgent cholera outbreak linked to the dry season and use of untreated Lake Kivu water. At the CCLK health center, at least 18 cholera cases were admitted in two weeks. Ndaya Dubois, the lead nurse, cites lack of potable water and economic hardship driving households to lake water. Despite hygiene campaigns and chlorination sites, transmission remains high; last week the center referred six cases, the week before twelve. Community health workers intensify education on handwashing and consuming safe water. Health professionals urge rapid care at symptom onset, as cholera causes acute diarrhea and severe vomiting with dehydration and potential death. Authorities call residents to follow health guidance to limit spread in Goma and surrounding neighborhoods.

triage.headline_ja: ゴマでコレラ症例が再燃
triage.triage_reason: DRC・ゴマにおけるコレラの再流行で、水源汚染とヒト-ヒト感染拡大の可能性があり、既存の脆弱な医療体制・人道状況を踏まえフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 北キブ州ゴマでの季節性コレラ再流行。安全な水へのアクセス不足と経済的困窮が要因。地域の衛生インフラ・治安状況を考慮すると外部支援の必要性が高い可能性。

article.articleHeadline: DRC neighbors boost preparedness as Ebola cases surge
article.articleSummary: 2,344 Ebola cases and 930 deaths reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) as of 2026-07-20, with the outbreak centered in Ituri and caused by the Bundibugyo strain (no vaccine available). Began May 15, 2026, it is described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, and the WHO cautions true case numbers may be 2–4 times higher due to undetected infections in conflict-affected eastern DRC. Neighbouring Uganda, Rwanda and Zambia have bolstered preparedness to limit cross-border spread: border screening, frontline worker training, expanded disease surveillance, and activated emergency response centers. Zambia reports no confirmed cases yet, though infection prevention measures (disinfection, masks, handwashing) are intensified. Uganda identifies Kisoro, Kanungu and Rukungiri districts along the DRC border as high risk; Rwanda has strengthened border checks. The East African Community, Africa CDC and WHO are coordinating surveillance, lab testing and rapid response with a funding gap exceeding $400 million for the joint plan.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国の隣国、エボラ感染急増を受け対応準備を強化
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最速拡大とされるエボラ流行（2,344例・930死亡）が発生し、ワクチンのないブンディブジョ株が原因で近隣国への越境拡大リスクが高いため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: ザンビアは予防措置を強化しているが確認例は未報告のため実際の発生国としては含めていない。ウガンダ・ルワンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Страшный счёт растёт каждый день: новая вспышка Эболы вышла на критический уровень
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The terrifying toll grows every day: a new Ebola outbreak has reached a critical level.
article.articleSummary: As of 20 July 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 2,344 infections and 930 deaths, with 77 new cases recorded in the last 24 hours. Mortality is near 40%, reflecting an aggressive virus strain, late care, and limited treatment access. About 724 people with a confirmed diagnosis are hospitalized in specialized facilities or quarantine blocks. Contact tracing has reached 85.8%, supporting timely isolation of potential carriers to interrupt transmission. Ebola is a hemorrhagic virus transmitted by direct contact with blood, secretions, and contaminated materials. Early symptoms include sudden fever, weakness, and headaches, followed by vomiting, diarrhea, rash, and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding. Control emphasizes rapid isolation, strict infection-control measures, and sustained monitoring of contacts to prevent secondary outbreaks, especially in densely populated areas with challenging sanitary conditions.

triage.headline_ja: 恐ろしい死者数が日々増加：新たなエボラ出血熱の流行が危機的レベルに達する
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱の大規模流行（感染2,344人、死者930人、致死率約40%）であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 致死率約40%、接触追跡率85.8%と高いが、感染者数・死者数の急増が続いており、密集地域での二次感染拡大リスクが高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : Plus de 2.340 cas déjà confirmés
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: More than 2,340 cases have already been confirmed.
article.articleSummary: As of 20 July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 2,344 confirmed Ebola cases, 930 deaths and 466 recoveries. A total of 724 patients are currently in isolation or hospitalized. The case fatality rate stands at 39.7%, with contact tracing reaching 85.8%. The response is intensified across five affected provinces: Upper Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu and Tshopo, with surveillance, patient care and contact follow-up ongoing to curb transmission. Ituri remains the epidemic's epicenter, with authorities reinforcing monitoring and contact tracing there. Nationally, 83 new confirmed cases were recorded, alongside 22 new recoveries. South Kivu and Tshopo are described as stable, with no new health zones affected. The report underscores continued mobilization and strengthened response measures to contain Ebola.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：確認済み症例が既に2,340人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC5州で拡大し、致死率39.7%、死者930人と深刻な公衆衛生上の影響があり、国際的拡大リスクも否定できないためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 既に大規模流行であり、複数州（Upper Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo）に拡大。継続的なモニタリングと国際支援の必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Rio Branco concentra 61% dos casos confirmados de dengue no Acre em 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rio Branco accounts for 61% of confirmed dengue cases in Acre in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Rio Branco remains the dengue epicenter in Acre, Brazil, with 607 of 993 confirmed cases (61.1%) through weeks 1–20 of 2026. The state totals 1,455 probable dengue notifications, with 993 confirmed. Despite an 84.5% drop in positive diagnoses from 2025 (6,407 cases that year), the incidence is 165.2 per 100,000, indicating active transmission. By region, the Lower Acre Region accounts for 660 confirmed cases (66.5%), led by Rio Branco and Sena Madureira (19). The Juruá Region has 266 cases (26.8%), concentrated in Cruzeiro do Sul (153) and Mâncio Lima (66). The Alto Acre Region records 67 cases (6.7%), notably Brasiléia and Xapuri with 20 each. There are 15 dengue with warning signs; two suspected deaths under investigation. Laboratory confirmation (706, 71.1%) predominates; 286 (28.8%) were confirmed clinically.

triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・アクレ州のデング熱は地域流行性疾患であり、2025年比で84.5%減少している定例サーベイランス報告であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Japanese vaccine becomes 1st vaccine approved by India to fight dengue
article.articleSummary: On 2026-07-20, India approved Takeda Pharmaceutical's dengue vaccine QDENGA for use in individuals aged 4–60 years, making it the first dengue vaccine cleared in India by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO). This milestone comes as dengue cases rise globally, with India—one of the world's largest dengue-endemic countries—recording 121,824 cases and 131 deaths last year. Dengue is caused by four related viruses and transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, which can cause fever, severe pain, and, in some cases, death. The approval represents a key step in strengthening dengue prevention for affected communities. The article notes no specific laboratory confirmation details or infection sources beyond mosquito transmission, nor any imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola/RDC: A epidemia mais veloz de sempre já fez 930 mortos em mais de 2.300 casos registados
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola/DRC: The fastest epidemic ever has already claimed 930 lives in more than 2,300 recorded cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the Bundibugyo strain, marks the 17th outbreak and the fastest-spreading yet, expanding from Bunia in Ituri toward Uganda and into North and South Kivu. From May to June 20, 930 deaths and about 2,350 laboratory-confirmed cases were reported. The outbreak lacks a vaccine or proven treatment for Bundibugyo, and sociocultural factors—especially reliance on traditional healers and burial practices—heighten transmission. Congolese authorities, with international support, have intensified risk-communication and redirected funding; Angola has border screening (including Luanda airport). The United States, Canada, and some European countries have imposed 21-day Congo-exposure entry restrictions with quarantine abroad. WHO and Africa CDC warn of potential further geographic spread, drawing parallels with the 2013–2015 West Africa crisis (over 11,000 deaths). In the last 24 hours, 37 additional deaths and dozens of suspected deaths were added, with an estimated 30–40% fatality.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ/DRC：史上最速の流行、2,300例超で死者930人に
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最速とされるエボラ(ブンディブジョ株)流行が拡大中で、死者930人・症例2,300件超、致死率30-40%、複数国が渡航制限を導入するなど国際的影響が顕著であるため。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC（イトゥリ州ブニアから北・南キヴ州、ウガンダ方向への拡大）が主題。アンゴラ・ウガンダ・米国・カナダ等は国境対応・渡航制限の文脈で言及されているが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。ワクチン・確立された治療法が存在しないブンディブジョ株であることも重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: QDENGA: India approves first dengue vaccine for people aged 4-60 years
article.articleSummary: India's DCGI has granted market authorization for Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India's QDENGA dengue vaccine for individuals aged 4–60 years, with vaccination not requiring prior dengue screening. QDENGA is given as two subcutaneous injections of 0.5 ml, three months apart, and protects against all four dengue serotypes. Since its 2022 launch, the vaccine has been approved in 43 countries, with over 32 million doses distributed. India's approval draws on a global Phase I–III programme (19 trials, >28,000 participants) and the Phase III DEN-302 trial conducted in India. Seven-year follow-up data indicate sustained protection against dengue infection and dengue-related hospitalization for all serotypes. Takeda frames the approval as strengthening India's dengue prevention alongside vector control, surveillance, and community measures.

article.articleHeadline: भारत में डेंगू से बचाव को बड़ी राहत: CDSCO ने पहली डेंगू वैक्सीन 'क्यूडेंगा' (QDENGA) को दी मंजूरी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A major relief for dengue prevention in India: CDSCO approves the first dengue vaccine 'Qdenga' (QDENGA).
article.articleSummary: India's CDSCO has approved Takeda's Qdenga (TAK-003), the first dengue vaccine for India. Qdenga is a live-attenuated, tetravalent vaccine protecting against all four dengue serotypes (DENV-1–DENV-4) and does not require prior dengue testing before vaccination. It has approvals in over 40 countries, including EU members, the United Kingdom, Brazil, Indonesia and Argentina. In Phase III TIDES trials across eight dengue-affected countries with over 20,000 children and adolescents over roughly four years, the vaccine reduced dengue-related hospitalizations by about 84% and prevented 61% of laboratory-confirmed dengue illness, including in those without prior exposure. For India, which accounts for a large share of global dengue and has seen more than an 11-fold rise in infections over two decades, Qdenga could strengthen public health measures and outbreak control. The two-dose regimen is spaced three months apart; production in Hyderabad through Biological E is planned to reach about 50 million doses annually, with price to be announced.

triage.headline_ja: インドのデング熱予防に大きな前進：CDSCOが初のデングワクチン「Qdenga(クエデンガ)」を承認

article.articleHeadline: India's 1st dengue vaccine approved
article.articleSummary: QDENGA becomes India's first dengue vaccine approved by the drug regulator, covering all four dengue serotypes for ages 4–60. In 2024, dengue caused 14.4 million global cases and 11,201 deaths; India reported 232,425 cases and 233 deaths. Over two decades, India's dengue cases reportedly rose about 11-fold. The two-dose, 0.5 ml injection given three months apart can be used regardless of prior exposure, with efficacy of 80.2% against confirmed dengue one year after the second dose and 90.4% against dengue-related hospitalizations after 18 months. Takeda India has partnered with Biological E for manufacturing. Dengvaxia is not approved in India and is recommended only for those with prior infection; regulators may require post-marketing safety data. Separately, Indian Immunologicals Ltd is beginning mid-stage trials of its own dengue vaccine candidate.

article.articleHeadline: India approves first dengue vaccine for individuals aged 4 to 60 years
article.articleSummary: As of 20 July 2026, India's DCGI approved Takeda QDENGA (TAK-003) dengue vaccine for prevention in people aged 4–60 years. The live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine is given in two doses, three months apart, and may be administered regardless of prior dengue infection or pre-vaccination screening. India bears a substantial dengue burden, accounting for about one-third of global cases. Approval rests on Takeda global programme of 19 Phase I–III trials with more than 28,000 participants. In DEN-301, efficacy was 80.2% against virologically confirmed dengue at 12 months and 90.4% against dengue-related hospitalization at 18 months; longer-term data show sustained protection across all four serotypes. QDENGA is approved in 43 countries, WHO prequalified, and included in Brazil National Immunization Program; Argentina, Colombia and Indonesia publicly programme it. India will plan rollout with regulators and health providers.

triage.notes: 記事はインドDCGIによるQDENGAワクチン承認の発表であり、疾病発生・アウトブレイクの報告ではないためトリアージ対象外と判断。ブラジル・アルゼンチン・コロンビア・インドネシアは既存承認国としての言及のみで、発生地域ではない。

article.articleHeadline: At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: Eastern Congo's Ebola outbreak has caused at least 930 deaths out of 2,344 lab-confirmed cases as of July 18, 2026. The Ministry of Health reported 37 new deaths in the preceding 24 hours, one of the highest single-day totals. Declared May 15 in eastern Congo, this Bundibugyo virus outbreak is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. The Bundibugyo strain is less common than others, and there is no approved vaccine or treatment available. The report emphasizes rapid escalation and high mortality, with ongoing transmission in the region as of July 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行で少なくとも930人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱（Bundibugyo株）による大規模流行で930人死亡、2344例確認、過去最速の拡大速度かつ承認ワクチン・治療法がなく、IHR基準複数該当およびWPRO基準も複数該当するため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Al menos 930 personas han muerto en el brote de ébola en República Democrática del Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: At least 930 people have died in the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed at least 930 people, with 2,344 confirmed cases reported by the Ministry of Health. In the 24 hours before the update, 37 new deaths were recorded, one of the highest daily tallies. The outbreak has also claimed the lives of at least 36 health-care workers infected with the virus. Counts reflect confirmed cases up to Saturday, with the update released late Sunday night into Monday morning. The brief provides no further details on geographic hotspots, transmission sources, or laboratory methods. The information underscores ongoing transmission and the substantial impact on frontline health staff as the outbreak continues in the country.

article.articleHeadline: 曾赴越南！嘉義市現今年首例登革熱 | 中華日報|中華新聞雲
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Visited Vietnam! Chiayi City reports its first dengue fever case of the year.
article.articleSummary: Chiayi City, Taiwan, confirmed its first dengue fever case of the year, an imported infection with travel history to Vietnam. The patient, a local national, developed fever, headache, and retro-orbital pain on July 15 and sought medical care on July 16; dengue was laboratory-confirmed by PCR on July 18. In response, the Chiayi City Health Bureau launched emergency vector-control measures around the patient’s residence, completing indoor and outdoor chemical control within a 100-meter radius on July 20 and conducting mosquito density surveys and source reduction. Public-health education was provided to the patient and contacts. Officials warn dengue is peak season with hot, humid weather favoring Aedes mosquitoes; residents are advised to practice surveillance and source reduction using the Sweep-Turn-Empty-Clean method, wear light clothing, use government-approved repellents, and inspect screens to reduce transmission risk.

article.articleHeadline: DRC Ebola deaths top 900 as WHO warns outbreak is outpacing response
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak tops 900 deaths with 2,344 confirmed cases across five provinces (Ituri, Haut-Uélé, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Tshopo). As of 2026-07-20, 930 deaths, 466 recoveries, and 724 patients in isolation; case fatality rate 39.7%. About 85.8% of identified contacts are traced. Ituri remains the epicentre with 2,073 cases and 796 deaths; transmission continues to evade surveillance, with >80% of new infections detected outside known contact lists. 83 new confirmed cases since the previous update and 22 new recoveries; Sud-Kivu and Tshopo report no new health zones. Two-thirds of deaths occur in communities before care, highlighting delayed treatment. Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccines or treatments; survival seen with early diagnosis and supportive care (377 recoveries). Uganda reports last confirmed patient discharged within a 42-day surveillance window. Security challenges in eastern DRC hinder access (Bunia treatment centre attacked). WHO/Africa CDC warn funding shortfall of >$400 million for continental preparedness and response, urging international support as an investment in national security.

article.articleHeadline: 민주콩고 에볼라 확산 계속...확진 2천300명·사망 900명 넘어
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo... confirmed cases exceed 2,300, deaths exceed 900.
article.articleSummary: Ebola continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with cumulative confirmed cases reaching 2,344 and deaths 930 as of July 18. Since July 15, 220 more cases and 102 more deaths were recorded, yielding a case‑fatality rate of 39.7%. Recoveries total 466. Contact tracing of exposed individuals stands at 85.8%. The World Health Organization warned that about 80% of new infections arise from transmissions not linked to known prior cases, indicating many undetected infections. Attacks on health facilities and personnel—driven by misinformation and hostility—have hampered response, with at least 12 such incidents since the outbreak was declared on May 15, and some treatment centers have faced wage‑related work stoppages. The ongoing Ebola outbreak remains a major public health challenge in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

article.articleHeadline: Ебола в Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease is spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths as of 19 July 2026. The outbreak began on 15 May in eastern DRC, centered in Ituri province, from which the virus has spread to Uganda. The World Health Organization calls this the largest, most dynamic Ebola outbreak to date. The involved strain is Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare variant for which there is no approved vaccine or licensed therapy. The health system is strained, with at least 12 attacks on medical facilities and rapid-response teams; many health workers have resigned due to delayed salaries, and 36 healthcare workers have died. Currently, 724 patients are in isolation and under treatment. CDC Director Jason Acher warned of a potential large humanitarian crisis.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak Death Toll Climbs Above 930
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak, centered in Ituri, has killed more than 930 people as of July 20, 2026, with 2,344 cases logged through July 18 (case fatality rate about 40%). Uganda has confirmed two deaths; no new cases there recently. Congo’s update shows 724 patients isolated or hospitalized and 466 recoveries. Ituri remains the epicenter while surveillance and contact tracing stay fully mobilized; 83 new confirmed cases nationwide and 22 new recoveries; South Kivu and Tshopo remain stable with no new affected zones. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, historically with lower fatality than Zaire/Sudan variants; there are no approved vaccines or treatments, though a clinical trial began in Congo in July. Symptoms include fever, severe headache, vomiting, and bleeding. International guidance includes U.S. and Canadian advisories and border measures limiting travel for those recently in Congo, Uganda, or South Sudan.

article.articleHeadline: Число жертв вспышки Эболы в ДР Конго достигло 930
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Death toll from Ebola outbreak in DR Congo reaches 930.
article.articleSummary: As of 20 July 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has 2,344 confirmed infections and 930 deaths, a case-fatality rate around 40%. Most cases are in the northeastern Ituri province, where insecurity and difficulties tracing contacts hinder containment. The outbreak involves Bundibugyo ebolavirus circulating in the DRC; the World Health Organization notes there is no approved vaccine for this strain, making early diagnosis, contact tracing, and supportive therapy critical. The virus was first identified in 1976 near the Ebola River, with historic outbreaks in Sudan and the DRC. The 2013–2014 West Africa epidemic infected about 30,000 people and caused over 11,000 deaths. Current response emphasizes early detection, contact tracing, isolation, and supportive care.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、死者930人に達する
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約40%の大規模エボラ流行（感染2,344人、死亡930人）で、承認済みワクチンがない株が流行し、治安不安により対応が困難な状況であり、深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威かつ国際的関心事項に該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域にSudanとAngolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRC（特にIturi州）のみが実際の発生地として言及されており、これらは対象国リストに含まれないか、あるいは主題ではないため除外した。Bundibugyoエボラウイルス株には承認ワクチンがなく、治安問題が対応を困難にしている点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Canadá prohibirá la entrada a extranjeros debido al brote de ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Canada will ban foreigners from entering due to the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Canada will ban foreign nationals who have recently visited the Democratic Republic of the Congo from entering the country, in response to the Ebola outbreak affecting that African nation. Effective July 20, 2026 at 23:59 EDT, individuals who have been in the DRC within the last 21 days will be temporarily barred from traveling to Canada. The government states that border measures are designed to reduce the risk of Ebola entering and spreading in Canada, and that the current public health risk is considered low. The restriction is described as temporary and applies to those with recent residence or travel in the DRC, illustrating a precautionary approach to ongoing Ebola transmission in the region.

triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱流行を受け、カナダが渡航制限を実施するなど国際的な公衆衛生対応が既に発生しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: カナダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。エボラ発生地であるDRCのみを記載。カナダの入国制限措置は国際的拡大リスクを示す重要な指標。

article.articleHeadline: Khởi tố nhóm đối tượng tiêu thụ hơn 250 tấn lợn nhiễm dịch tả lợn châu Phi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Group of individuals charged for consuming more than 250 tons of pigs infected with African swine fever.
article.articleSummary: Six individuals in Quảng Trị Province, Vietnam, were charged under Article 317 for violations of food safety regulations in a large-scale scheme that bought, transported, slaughtered, and sold more than 250 tons of pigs infected with African swine fever (ASF), risking serious food safety. On 20 July 2026, the Quảng Trị Police Department announced the charges. The investigation spanned February–May 2026, with more than 250 tons of ASF-infected pork marketed. The suspects are Mai Văn Quang (53) and Hà Văn Nghĩa (48), both of Nga Sơn, Thanh Hóa; Trần Thị Ngọc Hiền (Hoa Châu, 62) of Đông Hà, Quảng Trị; Hoàng Thị Mộng Truyền (Nương, 54); Trương Văn Quốc (53); and Trần Ngọc Bắc (55), all from Nam Đông Hà, Quảng Trị. The case is ongoing and being further investigated in accordance with law.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ豚熱感染豚250トン以上を消費・流通させた集団を起訴
triage.triage_reason: アフリカ豚熱（ASF）は非ヒト感染性の家畜疾病であり、本記事は食品安全法違反による摘発事案の報道であって新規の公衆衛生シグナルではないため。

article.articleHeadline: अब डेंगू से बचाव होगा आसान! भारत में जापानी QDENGA वैक्सीन को मिली मंजूरी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Now dengue prevention will be easy! The Japanese QDENGA vaccine has been approved in India.
article.articleSummary: India's CDSCO has approved Takeda's QDENGA dengue vaccine, a tetravalent live attenuated vaccine protecting against DENV-1 to DENV-4. It is suitable for people regardless of prior dengue infection and does not require pre-screening for dengue antibodies. In a country with a high dengue burden—exacerbated during the monsoon—the approval is a major public health development. Takeda has partnered with Biological E in 2024 to enable domestic production of up to 50 million doses annually in India, with a global goal of 100 million doses per year by the end of the decade. Since its 2022 launch, QDENGA has received regulatory clearance in 43 countries, with over 32 million doses distributed. Long-term studies indicate reduced dengue infection and dengue-related hospitalizations. Experts note vaccination should complement, not replace, vector-control measures; further details on availability, pricing, and guidelines will be issued by health authorities.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱予防が容易に！日本のQDENGAワクチンがインドで承認
triage.triage_reason: デング熱ワクチンの承認に関するニュースであり、アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示すものではないため、シグナルとしての基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 本記事はワクチン承認という規制的・政策的ニュースであり、感染症の発生や流行を報じるものではない。日本は対象国リストに含まれないため、Japanは除外。

article.articleHeadline: 沉寂14年的病毒突然苏醒，两个月杀了828人_腾讯新闻
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A virus dormant for 14 years suddenly awakens, killing 828 people in two months.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus has caused 828 deaths and 377 recoveries after awakening from a 14-year dormancy, with ongoing transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and related regional concerns. There is no approved antiviral; care is entirely supportive (fluids, oxygen, nutrition) and includes treating coinfections such as malaria and typhoid to maintain body function while the immune system responds. Three therapies show promise: MBP134, a pan-ebolavirus bispecific antibody targeting two sites on the surface glycoprotein (active against Zaire, Sudan, and Bundibugyo viruses); maftivimab, a monoclonal antibody prioritized by WHO but not yet in trials; and remdesivir, a broad-spectrum RNA polymerase inhibitor. In June, Uganda received over 2,000 remdesivir vials. The PARTNERS trial in the DRC began July 2, randomizing confirmed cases to four arms (supportive care alone; plus MBP134; plus remdesivir; or plus both MBP134 and remdesivir) aiming 700–1,000 participants over six months. July 14 launched obeldesivir (oral remdesivir prodrug) trials with donations of 2,400 obeldesivir and 2,000 remdesivir. Xylomed of South Africa plans 3B trials in DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan for an oral small-molecule inhibitor, potentially usable at home for children over two.

triage.headline_ja: 14年間眠っていたウイルスが突然活動を再開、2ヵ月で828人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でブンディブジョウイルス（エボラ関連ウイルス）が14年ぶりに再燃し、2ヵ月で828人が死亡するなど深刻な公衆衛生被害が発生。IHR基準を複数満たし、WHOや国際機関が治療薬・臨床試験で介入している重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・南アフリカ・スーダンは臨床試験・薬剤供与の対象として言及されているが、実際の発生地はDRCのみ。ウガンダ等は対象国リストにも含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: 5 người ở TP.HCM tử vong do bệnh dại
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Five people in Ho Chi Minh City died of rabies.
article.articleSummary: Five people in Ho Chi Minh City died of rabies in 2026: three in Long Hải commune, one in Cu Chi, and one in Hòa Hiệp. All fatalities were unvaccinated and did not receive rabies immunoglobulin. About 40% of wound-care after bites was improper, delaying treatment. In southern Vietnam, 20 rabies deaths occurred January–June 2026; nationwide total reached 30. Extreme heat is linked to transmission. HCMC health authorities have intensified controls; HCDC will coordinate with the Department of Livestock and Veterinary to strengthen surveillance, education, and outbreak containment. Rabies is 100% fatal after symptoms, but preventable with timely vaccination and post-exposure prophylaxis. Immediate steps: rinse wounds with soap and water for 15 minutes, disinfect with 45–70% alcohol, then seek vaccination and immunoglobulin. The public should follow five 'NOs' regarding vaccination, reporting, roaming, bites, and environment; vaccination is advised for high-risk groups.

article.articleHeadline: 10 Monsoon Diseases To Watch Out For And How To Prevent Them
article.articleSummary: Mumbai dengue cases rose 734–938 since January; malaria 3,115–3,681; leptospirosis 136–157, prompting BMC to inspect 3,000 construction sites and fog nearly 800,000 homes. Delhi records 162 dengue, 42 malaria and nine chikungunya cases so far this year as rains loom. National dengue reached 6,927 by end-February 2026. Ten monsoon diseases to watch include: Dengue fever with fever, severe headache and rash; prevention: empty standing water weekly, nets/repellents, test if fever lasts over three days. Malaria with cyclical fever; prevention: cover water storage, test promptly, complete treatment. Leptospirosis from contaminated water/soil; about 7.5% fatal if untreated; prevention: avoid floodwater, wash feet, report exposure. Chikungunya with joint pains; Typhoid from contaminated water/food; prevention: boiled water, avoid street food, confirm with blood culture. Hepatitis A from contaminated water/food; Cholera with dehydration; prevention: hygiene, boiled water and ORS; Viral fever; Fungal skin infections.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : 2 344 cas confirmés et 930 décès, selon le rapport officiel arrêté au 18 juillet
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths, according to the official report as of July 18.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo reached 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths as of July 18, 2026 (case fatality rate 39.7%), per a situation report published July 19 by the INSP and Ministry of Communications. Ituri remains the epicenter with 27 of 36 zones affected (including Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu, Nyankunde, Mahagi); Nord-Kivu 11 zones; Haut-Uélé 4; Tshopo 3; South Kivu is affected only in Miti-Murhesa, with 52 days without a new case, suggesting a possible end there. The Bundibugyo strain has no licensed vaccine or specific treatment; management relies on early detection, isolation and supportive care. Nationally, 83 new cases and 22 recoveries were reported; contact tracing stands at 85.8%. The response includes over 14 laboratories, 700+ beds and 16 testing sites (INRB); Canada announced July 19 a temporary border closure for travelers who had stayed in the DRC.

article.articleHeadline: India Approves First Dengue Vaccine as Takeda's QDENGA Receives DCGI Nod
article.articleSummary: India grants marketing authorisation for Takeda’s QDENGA (TAK-003), the country’s first dengue vaccine, as dengue continues to expand in India and worldwide. DCGI approval targets ages 4–60 and permits use without prior dengue infection screening, contrasting with Dengvaxia’s requirement for prior infection. QDENGA is a tetravalent live-attenuated vaccine designed against all four dengue serotypes. Clinical data: 80.2% efficacy against confirmed dengue one year after the second dose; 90.4% efficacy against hospitalization after 18 months. Production expansion: Takeda, with Hyderabad-based Biological E, to manufacture up to 50 million doses annually; goal 100 million doses per year by 2030. WHO prequalified QDENGA in May 2024; now approved in 43 countries, >32 million doses distributed since 2022. Rollout dates in India pending; vaccination may complement, not replace, vector control, surveillance, and public awareness.

If needed, samples from the patient’s family, who had been in contact with him, will be collected and tested. The article provides no further details about contacts or transmission beyond this case.

article.articleHeadline: Lâm Đồng siết chặt phòng, chống dịch tay chân miệng sau 2 ca tử vong do nhiễm virus EV71
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lam Dong Province tightens prevention and control of hand-foot-mouth disease after two deaths from EV71 virus infection
article.articleSummary: Lam Dong Province, Vietnam reports 3,072 hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD) cases through July 2026, up from 2025, with two Enterovirus 71 (EV71)–related deaths in Ta Nang commune. Investigations link fatalities to delayed detection, monitoring gaps, and late treatment, with caregivers failing to recognize warning signs or relying on non-inpatient care. The provincial Department of Health will mobilize the Center for Disease Control to form rapid response teams, support outbreak investigations, and implement control measures. Community outreach will be intensified, especially in ethnic minority areas, engaging local authorities, trusted community figures, religious leaders, and organizations to promote early recognition and timely hospital referral. All health facilities, including private clinics, must enforce strict triage and treatment protocols to avoid emergency delays. A door-to-door survey will identify hidden cases; inspections of kindergartens and private centers will suspend facilities not meeting hygiene standards. Ta Nang will receive intensified supervision, distribution of Cloramin B, and home hygiene guidance.

article.articleHeadline: Holiday hotspots where four rare diseases cause joint pains and bleeding gums
article.articleSummary: Chikungunya, dengue, schistosomiasis and Lyme disease are highlighted as travel-related risks for Britons this summer. Chikungunya is spread by daytime-biting Aedes mosquitoes and is found in over 120 countries from the Caribbean to Sri Lanka and Thailand; UK travellers returning with it are up about 43%. Dengue, also carried by Aedes, affects India, Barbados, Thailand and parts of the Americas and southern Europe, including France, Italy and Spain; symptoms typically start 4–10 days after a bite and include fever, headache, rash, and muscle or joint pain, with severe forms causing bleeding gums, vomiting or breathing problems. Schistosomiasis, caused by parasitic worms in freshwater, occurs in Africa, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and the Caribbean, with 200 million cases worldwide; Europe has seen Corsica and Spain outbreaks. Lyme disease, tick-borne bacterial infection, is present in Europe, North America and Asia; about 10% of UK ticks carry it, with a 20% yearly increase. Prevention: cover up, use mosquito nets and repellents; avoid freshwater swimming and seek care if symptoms appear.

article.articleHeadline: Wabah Ebola di RD Kongo Tewaskan Sedikitnya 930 Orang
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo kills at least 930 people.
article.articleSummary: By 18 July 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed at least 930 people, with 2,344 laboratory-confirmed cases. In the last 24 hours, 37 deaths were recorded, one of the highest daily tolls of the outbreak. The outbreak, first declared on 15 May 2026, is described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak to date. It is caused by the Bundibugyo variant, a less common form of Ebola, for which there is no vaccine or treatment specifically approved. The government of the DR Congo continues active surveillance and response, urging the public to stay vigilant to curb transmission. The information is reported as of 18 July 2026, with ongoing monitoring by health authorities.

article.articleHeadline: भारत ने 4 से 60 साल की उम्र के लोगों के लिए पहली डेंगू वैक्सीन 'क्यूडेंगा' को दी मंजूरी | Dengue Vaccine Qdenga
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India approves the first dengue vaccine 'Qdenga' for people aged 4 to 60 years | Dengue Vaccine Qdenga.
article.articleSummary: India’s Drugs Controller General (DCGI) has granted approval to Takeda’s dengue vaccine Qdenga for ages 4–60 years, marking India’s first dengue vaccine. The shot can be given to anyone regardless of prior dengue infection; no pre-vaccination testing is required. It is administered as two 0.5 mL subcutaneous injections 3 months apart. The approval strengthens India’s dengue prevention strategy at a time when the country has among the highest dengue burdens and multiple serotypes circulate in many areas. Globally, Qdenga has been approved in 43 countries with over 32 million doses distributed since its 2022 launch. Takeda cites data from more than 28,000 participants across dengue-affected and non-affected countries in 19 Phase 1–3 trials, showing safety and immune response; long-term follow-up up to seven years indicates protection against infection and hospitalization from all four serotypes. The company notes vaccination complements vector control, surveillance and public health measures.

article.articleHeadline: DCGI approves Takeda's QDENGA, India's first dengue vaccine
article.articleSummary: India's DCGI granted market authorisation for QDENGA, Takeda's tetravalent dengue vaccine, for ages 4–60, regardless of prior exposure and without pre-vaccination testing. It is a two-dose, 0.5 mL subcutaneous regimen given three months apart. Approval is based on the global program with 28,000+ participants, including Phase III DEN-301 and Indian DEN-302 trials showing safety and immunogenicity. In DEN-301, 12-month efficacy against virologically confirmed dengue was 80.2%; at 18 months, efficacy against dengue-related hospitalization was 90.4%; after 4.5 years, 84.1% protection against hospitalization. The vaccine provides protection against all four serotypes and is approved under NDCT rules 2019. India, bearing about one-third of the global dengue burden, reported over 113,000 cases in 2025, with true burden likely higher. QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries since 2022, with over 32 million doses distributed; WHO endorses its use in endemic settings.

article.articleHeadline: Research advances offer hope, but prevention remains key in Rabies control: AIIMS Neurologist
article.articleSummary: Darbhanga, 20 Jul — Rabies remains almost 100% fatal once clinical symptoms appear; prevention via timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) is the only proven life-saving strategy, AIIMS neurologist Prof (Dr) Achal Kumar Srivastava told the 26th National Conference of APCRI in Darbhanga. While highlighting research advances—monoclonal antibodies, gene therapy, next-generation mRNA vaccines, and advanced molecular diagnostics—he cautioned that these will require extensive trials before clinical adoption. Global estimates from WHO: about 59,000 rabies deaths annually, ~95% in Asia and Africa; children under 15 account for ~40%. The rabies virus travels to the brain via peripheral nerves; two clinical forms: furious and paralytic. Encouraging preclinical results for F11 monoclonal antibody; other therapies under study. Milwaukee Protocol not reliably effective. Current management focuses on intensive supportive care; real-time RT-PCR and LAMP improve early diagnosis. One Health: dog vaccination, public awareness, timely PEP, and cross-sector coordination are essential.

article.articleHeadline: Brasil ativa banco contra febre aftosa na Argentina; entenda
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Brazil activates a bank against foot-and-mouth disease in Argentina; understand.
article.articleSummary: Brazil activates the National Bank of Antigens for Foot-and-Mouth Disease, stationed in Garín, Argentina, to bolster emergency response and protect the Brazilian herd. The facility stores antigens used to produce vaccines against foot-and-mouth disease, enabling rapid vaccine production if an outbreak is detected and accelerating response times. The bank is part of Brazil’s contingency plan and gains strategic value after the 2025 WOAH recognition of Brazil as FMD-free without vaccination, helping preserve access to major meat import markets. The project selected Biogénesis Bagó for its international experience in immunobiologicals for animal health. Minister André de Paula says the bank reinforces Brazilian sanitary defense and international credibility, even as EU restrictions on animal-origin products persist; the UK continues importing Brazilian products, and Brazil pursues solutions with the European Union while monitoring China and the United States markets. The bank is a key tool to ensure market access during outbreaks.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India gets its first dengue vaccine, DCGI approves the market launch of 'Qdenga'.
article.articleSummary: India's DCGI has approved the market launch of Qdenga, a dengue vaccine produced by Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India, for individuals aged 4–60 under NDCT CT-20 rules. The subcutaneous vaccine (0.5 mL) is given in two doses, three months apart, and may be administered regardless of prior dengue infection. This marks the first dengue vaccine approved in India. Dengue remains a global public health challenge in over 125 countries, with India accounting for roughly one-third of cases; 2025's India's reported dengue cases exceeded 113,000, though many go undiagnosed. Phase-3 data from Indian participants showed good tolerability in adults, adolescents, and children, with protection against all four serotypes and reduced risk of infection and hospitalization. WHO recommends Qdenga for dengue-endemic areas and supports its inclusion in high-transmission vaccination programs. Since 2022, it has gained approvals in 43 countries with over 32 million doses distributed.

article.articleHeadline: 4 ರಿಂದ 60 ವರ್ಷದೊಳಗಿನವರಿಗೆ ಭಾರತದ ಮೊದಲ ಡೆಂಗ್ಯೂ ಲಸಿಕೆ 'QDENGA'ಗೆ ಅನುಮೋದನೆ | Indiaâs first dengue vaccine âQDENGAâ approved for those aged 4 to 60 years.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India's first dengue vaccine 'QDENGA' approved for those aged 4 to 60 years.
article.articleSummary: Dengue vaccine QDENGA from Takeda has been approved by India's DCGI for ages 4–60 under 2019 NDCT rules, becoming the country’s first dengue vaccine. It is a live-attenuated, tetravalent vaccine given as two 0.5 mL subcutaneous doses three months apart, with no pre-screening required. India faces a heavy dengue burden, accounting for about one-third of global cases and reporting 113,000+ cases in 2025. WHO prequalification supports its use; it has been approved in 43 countries across Asia, Latin America and Europe, with over 32 million doses distributed, including Brazil’s program and entries in Argentina, Colombia and Indonesia. Phase III DEN-301/DEN-302 show 80.2% efficacy against virologically confirmed dengue at 12 months, 90.4% protection against hospitalization at 18 months, and 84.1% protection at four years, with durability to seven years. Vaccination is to be complemented by vector control and awareness efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhea is rising in Europe, health agency says
article.articleSummary: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhoea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae) is rising across Europe, with local transmission now evident in France, Germany, Sweden and the United Kingdom. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) reports 106,331 confirmed European cases in 2024—the highest since EU surveillance began in 2009—and a 303% rise over the past decade, driven in part by expanded screening and reporting. Between 2023–2024, overall rates rose 7.9% among men and fell 8.6% among women; men who have sex with men accounted for 62% of 2024 cases. Ceftriaxone, with or without azithromycin, remains the main treatment, but resistance to both drugs is increasing, undermining effectiveness. Importation from outside Europe—especially from Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam—continues to seed resistant strains; local transmission signals potential escalation if controls lapse. The general population risk is low, but rises for high-risk groups and travelers to areas with high resistance.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Viral fever, itching and burning eyes... after the rains, monsoon illnesses heighten concerns as Bettiah GMCH's medicine ward fills up.
article.articleSummary: After persistent rainfall, Bettiah Government Medical College Hospital (GMCH) in Bihar reports a surge in monsoon illnesses, with viral fever, skin infections, and ocular infections predominating. In the hospital’s Monday OPD, 1,842 patients sought care. The medicine ward is fully occupied, forcing admissions to other wards. Over the past week, patient numbers have risen, especially in Medicine (650) and Dermatology (695), with Ophthalmology (207), Pediatrics (105), Gynecology (50), Orthopedics (40), and ENT/Cancer/other departments (95) also seeing increases. Clinically, most patients present with fever, cold, rashes/itching, and eye burning or watering. Doctors attribute the surge to fluctuating monsoon temperatures and humidity, waterlogging, and mosquito proliferation, raising risks of viral fever, typhoid, diarrhea, dengue, malaria, and skin diseases. Public advice emphasizes clean water, avoiding stagnant water, mosquito protection, and consulting clinicians rather than self-medicating.

article.articleHeadline: MALÁRIA: ESTUDO MINEIRO PODE ACELERAR VACINA - Carmo Web TV 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malaria: Minas Gerais study could accelerate the vaccine - Carmo Web TV 2026.
article.articleSummary: Malaria vaccine research from Minas Gerais could accelerate global efforts. Scientists Camila Barbosa, Luna de Lacerda, and Caroline Junqueira at CT-Vacinas in Belo Horizonte mapped Plasmodium antigens across species and life stages, identifying conserved targets that may enable a universal malaria vaccine. The Nature study, the first Brazilian-led article in 157 years, confirmed that 71% of identified antigens are conserved across species and 75% are expressed in multiple life-cycle stages, supporting vaccines that stimulate both antibodies and T-cell responses. This could boost efficacy of existing vaccines by targeting cellular immunity and addressing diverse parasite forms in Brazil and Africa. Brazil recorded 44,871 malaria cases from January to June 2026, with 96% in the Amazon region (Acre, Amazonas, Amapá, Pará, Rondônia, Roraima, Tocantins, Mato Grosso, Maranhão); 19 diagnoses occurred outside the region (Ceará, Espírito Santo, Goiás, Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, São Paulo). Mortality risk is higher outside the Amazon.

article.articleHeadline: Surto de Ébola na RDCongo faz quase mil óbitos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the DRC kills nearly 1,000.
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak has caused 930 deaths, with 37 fatalities in the last 24 hours—one of the largest daily totals on record. Ituri province is the hardest hit, where attacks on health facilities and response teams have reached at least 12 incidents. Health workers are also affected by pay disputes, with strikes contributing to operational strain; 36 health workers have been infected and died. The Ministry of Health reports 724 patients currently hospitalized and isolated in affected areas. Hospitals face severe pressure and limited resources, sustaining a critical challenge to containment efforts by Congolese public health authorities.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、死者数がほぼ1000人に達する

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Canada bans entry to foreigners who have passed through the DRC.
article.articleSummary: Canada bans entry of any foreign national who has been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo within the last 21 days, effective July 20, 2026 at 23:59, to curb Ebola import risk, per the Public Health Agency of Canada. The measure aims to protect Canadians and improve border-control effectiveness, with no specified exemptions or duration beyond the initial period, and may affect humanitarian workers returning to Canada. The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was declared two months ago and is spreading faster than previous epidemics. As of now, 2,003 cases and 796 deaths have been reported. By contrast, the 2018–2020 outbreak in the same country caused about 3,500 infections and nearly 2,300 deaths, taking more than 10 months to reach 2,000 cases. The current surge underscores urgency of border measures and international response.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in Congo claims more than 930 lives
article.articleSummary: Despite containment efforts, the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has risen to at least 930 deaths and 2,344 cases as of Saturday, with 37 fatalities in a 24-hour period. Declared on May 15, the Bundibugyo strain—no approved treatment or vaccine—drives the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. Transmission occurs from wild animals to humans and through contact with contaminated materials and bodily fluids. Five provinces are affected, with Ituri the hardest hit. Security challenges hinder response, including at least 12 attacks on health facilities and personnel, fueled by scepticism and rumours. Internal labor disputes have led health workers to protest over pay, contributing to delayed response; at least 36 health workers have died from infection. WHO warns that 80% of new cases come from unknown transmission chains. The ministry reports 724 patients in treatment or isolation, with 22 recoveries in the latest 24-hour window.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Avian influenza arrives in Rio Grande do Sul, authorities issue a new alert; see what happens now after confirmation of the first case and whether it is still safe to eat chicken and eggs.
article.articleSummary: First avian influenza case in Rio Grande do Sul backyard poultry, detected in Coqueiros do Sul in the state’s Northwest region. Confirmation on Friday, July 17, 2026, by the Federal Laboratory of Agricultural Defense (LFDA-SP) after samples analyzed by the Department of Vigilance and Animal Health (DDA) of the Rio Grande do Sul Agriculture Secretariat. The finding does not change RS or Brazil’s Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza status and poses no risk to consumers; properly cooked chicken and eggs remain safe. Preventive actions include inspections within a 10-km radius of the outbreak, farm monitoring, enhanced sanitary education, and guidance to producers to prevent spread. Avian influenza mainly affects birds; human infections are rare and linked to direct contact with sick or dead birds, not food. If birds appear ill, do not touch and report to the nearest Inspectorate or via WhatsApp: (51) 98445-2033.

article.articleHeadline: India News | DCGI Approves Takeda's QDENGA, India's First Dengue Vaccine
article.articleSummary: DCGI approved Takeda’s QDENGA dengue vaccine for prevention in individuals aged 4–60 in India, marking the country’s first dengue vaccine approval and allowing use regardless of prior exposure or pre-vaccination testing. India bears about one-third of the global dengue burden; 2025 reported dengue cases exceeded 113,000, with modelling suggesting tens of millions of infections annually. The global program includes 19 Phase I–III trials with over 28,000 participants; the pivotal DEN-301 trial enrolled more than 20,000 across eight countries, showing 12-month overall efficacy of 80.2% against virologically confirmed dengue and 18-month efficacy of 90.4% against dengue-related hospitalisation; after 4.5 years, hospitalisation prevention remained 84.1%. Phase III DEN-302 in Indian participants demonstrated tolerability, safety and immunogenicity in ages 4–60. Since 2022, QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries with over 32 million doses distributed.

article.articleSummary: Chiayi City reports its first imported dengue fever case this year in a Taiwanese man who had traveled to Vietnam. Returning travelers with fever or retro-orbital pain should seek prompt medical care and report travel history to doctors.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: AI and climate alerts, massacre in Honduras, Ebola, and migrant women... Friday's news.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, is being stretched by population movement, with the IOM reporting seven million checks and more than 200 points monitored for cross-provincial movement. Authorities say over 50 bodies have been moved between provinces, districts and health zones, all Ebola-positive, though none crossed international borders. WHO notes families try to repatriate bodies for burial, complicating containment. In Honduras, a United Nations special rapporteur calls for independent investigation into the May 21 mass killing of 20 campesinos near Rigores, Bajo Aguán, including 14 men, 3 women and 3 minors aged 14, 14 and 17, urging accountability and reparations. Separately, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres says AI can expand early warnings for floods, storms, fires, and droughts, but vulnerable nations lacking meteorological stations must receive technology and training; system coverage stands at 128 countries, with calls for renewable energy powering data centers by 2030.

article.articleHeadline: Aumentano in Europa i casi di gonorrea resistente agli antibiotici
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhea cases on the rise in Europe.
article.articleSummary: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhea is spreading in Europe with increasing local transmission beyond imported cases. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) reports rising Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections across Europe, with increases in France, Germany, Sweden, and the United Kingdom since 2025; other countries report sporadic cases. While general population risk remains low, resistance threatens treatment effectiveness. Ceftriaxone, alone or with azithromycin, is still the reference therapy, but strains resistant to both drugs are increasing. Importations from outside Europe remain the main entry route; Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam are key sources, some linked to therapeutic failures in Europe and North America. In 2024, Europe recorded 106,331 confirmed cases, a 303% rise over ten years. MSM accounted for 62% of 2024 cases; highest rates among men 25–34 and women 20–24. Risk is low for most, but moderate for high-risk groups and travelers to resistant areas; vigilance and health measures are needed.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: European Health Agency: Increase in Antibiotic-Resistant Gonorrhea
article.articleSummary: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhea is spreading across Europe, per the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). In 2024, 106,331 laboratory-confirmed gonorrhea cases were reported in the EU/EEA—the highest since EU surveillance began in 2009, with global estimates around 82 million cases annually among 15–49-year-olds. Initially travel-associated, local transmission is now rising in several countries, notably France, Germany, Sweden, and the United Kingdom. Southeast Asian countries—Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam—remain core sources of cephalosporin- and azithromycin-resistant strains that have disseminated internationally. Imported cases continue to be the main route for resistant strains entering Europe, though community spread is increasing. Highest incidence is in men aged 25–34 and women aged 20–24; among men who have sex with men, 62% of 2024 cases. Standard treatment (ceftriaxone plus azithromycin) is increasingly challenged by resistance; if unchecked, options will thin. Untreated infection can cause PID, infertility, and ectopic pregnancy.

article.articleSummary: Hong Kong's Centre for Health Protection reports rising summer influenza activity with 130 influenza outbreaks recorded to July 15, 2026, since week 26. From July 5–11, 27 influenza outbreaks in schools or elderly residences affected 136 people. Lab testing of 10,601 respiratory samples found 8.75% positive for influenza A or B, comprising 53% A(H3) and 14% B. The period coincides with dual influenza and COVID-19 activity; locally circulating SARS-CoV-2 lineages NB.1.8.1 and PQ.16.1.1 are Omicron subvariants. Most infections in healthy people are mild, but high-risk groups—elderly, those with chronic conditions, infants, unvaccinated or previously uninfected—face higher risk of severe disease. For COVID, Week 28 data show 572 positive local samples (9.79%), and 31 school or care-home outbreaks affecting 154 people (elderly homes 17, disabled 9, primary 1). Week 29 (first four days) recorded 23 influenza outbreaks affecting 149 people and 15 COVID outbreaks affecting 85 people (elderly 11).

article.articleHeadline: India Approves First Dengue Vaccine As Takeda's QDENGA Gets Nod
article.articleSummary: India approves Takeda's dengue vaccine QDENGA, the first vaccine approved in the country to help prevent dengue. Dengue cases in India have risen nearly elevenfold over the past two decades, and India accounts for nearly one-third of the global dengue burden, with recurring outbreaks across several states. QDENGA is a tetravalent live-attenuated vaccine providing protection against all four dengue serotypes and can be administered irrespective of prior dengue infection or pre-vaccination testing, supporting large-scale immunisation. To strengthen supply, Takeda partnered with Hyderabad-based Biological E in 2024 to build capacity for up to 50 million doses annually, contributing to a target of 100 million doses globally each year by the decade's end. Since its 2022 global launch, QDENGA has approvals in 43 countries and distributed more than 32 million doses; long-term data show sustained protection against symptomatic dengue and dengue-related hospitalisations.

article.articleHeadline: Takeda's dengue vaccine QDENGA gets DCGI approval for use in India
article.articleSummary: India's Drug Controller General (DCGI) has granted market authorisation for Takeda's dengue vaccine QDENGA for individuals aged 4–60, making it the first dengue vaccine approved in India and permitting use without pre-vaccination testing. India accounts for nearly one-third of the global dengue burden, with 2025 reported cases exceeding 113,000; modelling suggests the dengue burden may be tens of millions of infections annually. QDENGA is a tetravalent, live-attenuated vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue serotypes, irrespective of prior exposure. Global data from 19 Phase 1–3 trials (over 28,000 participants) underpin the approval, including DEN-301: 12-month efficacy 80.2% against virologically confirmed dengue and 18-month efficacy 90.4% against dengue-related hospitalisation; after 4.5 years, 84.1% efficacy against hospitalisations. An Indian Phase III DEN-302 study showed safety and immunogenicity in 4–60-year-olds. Since 2022, QDENGA has been approved in 43 countries with >32 million doses distributed, aiming to strengthen dengue prevention alongside vector control and surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: 'Very high risk' rare Ebola strain causes chaos as outbreak warning issued
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola strain remains at very high risk in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) as of 20 July 2026, while Uganda reports control. The World Health Organization links continued transmission to conflict-driven displacement, food and clean water insecurity, and a mass-unrest setting that hampers healthcare delivery. The outbreak is expanding into new health zones in DR Congo, raising national and regional spillover risk amid highly mobile and displaced populations. Factors amplifying transmission include crowded internally displaced person camps, inadequate infection prevention and control in health facilities, and unsafe burial practices. Security incidents hinder surveillance and response, limiting access for health workers and risking undetected transmission. Rapid case recognition, testing, and optimized supportive care are emphasized to reduce mortality and improve community trust in health services, with hospitals described as poorly equipped.

article.articleSummary: Four confirmed Ebola cases in Lolwa Health Zone, Babika-Bakwaza chiefdom, Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, as of July 19, 2026. At a Sunday briefing, Zone Medical Chief Dr. Patrick Mbarikale reported that three of ten health areas in Lolwa have been affected by the outbreak, the 17th Ebola outbreak in this part of Mambasa. Despite four confirmed cases, response capacity is limited by shortages of logistics and patient-care kits. In response, the health zone is intensifying community awareness in other areas to prevent further spread. Authorities are calling on national authorities and humanitarian partners to bolster support for the Ebola response in Ituri. The information highlights the early outbreak stage with ongoing containment and surveillance in Lolwa.

article.articleHeadline: Numărul cazurilor de Ebola din R.D. Congo a depăşit 2.300
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 2,300.
article.articleSummary: Lab-confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have risen to more than 2,300, with at least 930 deaths. Official health authorities reported the surge as the outbreak continues to spread across the country. The Ministry of Health said response teams have intensified surveillance, case finding, and contact tracing of people exposed to infection to curb transmission. The updated tally emphasizes the ongoing severity of the outbreak and the essential role of rapid laboratory confirmation, isolation, and follow-up of contacts in reducing spread. No details are provided on specific affected provinces or dates of new infections in the briefing. The report, attributed to BBC World Service, is dated 20 July 2026, reflecting the latest official figures at that time.

article.articleHeadline: Les cas de gonorrhée résistante aux antibiotiques en hausse en Europe, alerte l'agence sanitaire
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhea cases on the rise in Europe, health agency warns.
article.articleSummary: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhea cases are rising across Europe per the ECDC. After initially sporadic and travel-associated cases, local transmission has grown since 2025, with France, Germany, Sweden, and the United Kingdom reporting marked increases. Local spread signals a potential expansion that could tighten treatment options if not controlled. Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes gonorrhea and, if untreated, can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease, infertility and ectopic pregnancy. Ceftriaxone, alone or with azithromycin, remains the reference therapy, but resistance to both drugs is undermining effectiveness. Importation from outside Europe remains the main route for ceftriaxone-resistant strains; Southeast Asia—Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam—are major hubs disseminating strains with treatment failures in Europe and North America. In Europe, gonorrhea diagnoses rose 303% over ten years; 2024 had 106,331 confirmed cases, the highest since surveillance began. Globally, about 82 million new cases annually among 15–49-year-olds. Between 2023 and 2024, rates rose 7.9% in men and fell 8.6% in women; 62% of 2024 cases were in MSM, 37% in heterosexuals.

triage.headline_ja: 欧州で抗菌薬耐性淋菌感染症の症例が増加、保健当局が警告

triage.notes: 記事の主眼は欧州（フランス・ドイツ・スウェーデン・英国）でのECDC報告だが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。東南アジア諸国（ベトナム・タイ・インドネシア）は耐性株の拡散源として明示的に言及されているため verified_locations に含めた（カンボジアは対象国リスト外のため除外）。

article.articleHeadline: Couple tests Covid positive in Bihar's Bhagalpur
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 infections confirmed in a couple in Bhagalpur district, Bihar. Subsequently, his 55-year-old wife tested positive. Both patients are under intensive medical care at JLNMCH, with a team of doctors closely monitoring them. COVID-19 protocols are being enforced. The district programme manager has been directed to conduct testing of residents in the Laluchak locality near the couple's residence. No information on vaccination status or infection source is provided. This report indicates a local testing and care response in Bhagalpur, with ongoing surveillance in the affected area.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市、狂犬病による死亡者5人を確認
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病はベトナムで既知の流行性疾患であり、ヒト-ヒト感染もなく国際的拡大リスクは低いが、重症度（致死率ほぼ100%）と暴露継続が見られるため、続報を注視する。

article.articleHeadline: Half of approved diagnostics for Africa's priority epidemic diseases unavailable at primary healthcare level - Report
article.articleSummary: Half of approved diagnostics for six Africa CDC priority diseases—Mpox, dengue, cholera, bacterial meningitis, malaria and Ebola—cannot be used at primary healthcare centres because they require laboratory infrastructure beyond frontline facilities. Ebola diagnostics are the most laboratory-dependent, with 88% needing a lab; across the six diseases, 577 diagnostics exist with 288 requiring clinical lab infrastructure and 59 still under development. Malaria has 83% deployable at primary care, but most Ebola and Mpox tests remain lab-based. Funding for diagnostic R&D has declined since 2015, from about $55 million to under $26 million in 2024, a nearly $4 million annual drop, signaling underinvestment amid rising outbreak risk. The Diagnostics Deficit report, by PATH and Impact Global Health, launched ahead of the AU Extraordinary Health Summit in Accra, Ghana, warns of gaps in access, affordability, deployment, and manufacturing readiness. The 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak highlighted detection delays due to strain-mismatch tests, underscoring urgent needs.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカの優先流行病に承認された診断薬の半数が、一次医療レベルでは利用できない - 報告書
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はアフリカの流行病診断能力に関する報告書の内容を伝えるものであり、特定の新規感染症アウトブレイクの発生を報じるものではない。ウガンダのエボラ流行は既知の過去事例として言及されているのみ。
triage.notes: 記事はPATHとImpact Global Healthによる診断薬ギャップ報告書に関するもので、AUの臨時保健サミット（ガーナ・アクラ）で発表された。具体的な新規アウトブレイクの発生報告ではなく、診断インフラの課題を論じる政策系記事。ウガンダ（対象国リスト外）のエボラ流行（Bundibugyo, 2026年）は文脈として言及されているのみで、ガーナは会議開催地であり疾病発生地ではないため、対象国は該当なし。

article.articleHeadline: Terrifying Ebola outbreak kills 800 as disease spreads from dead bodies
article.articleSummary: 800 Ebola deaths in Congo as an outbreak accelerates, with transmission driven by handling of dead bodies. Two-thirds of Ebola deaths occur outside hospitals, and burials are harder to control, increasing spread. Ebola transmits via direct contact with bodily fluids from infected people or animals. The first-known case emerged on April 24. The nurse’s death, and the transport of her body back to her hometown, is cited by Congolese health minister Samuel Roger Kamba as a key factor in rapid dissemination. Dr. Andrew Mbala of the IOM emphasizes that poor dead-body management and limited community engagement fuel transmission. The report underscores burial practices and movement of bodies as critical in ongoing transmission dynamics, with authorities monitoring the outbreak as of 2026-07-20.

triage.headline_ja: 恐ろしいエボラ出血熱の流行、遺体からの感染拡大で800人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国におけるエボラ出血熱の大規模流行（死者800人）で、遺体を介した感染拡大が続いており、IHR基準の複数項目（深刻性、異常性、国際拡大リスク）に該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 死者800人という規模と、遺体管理・葬儀慣習が感染拡大の主要因である点から、地域内・国際的拡大リスクが高い。続報でWHOの対応状況や国際的な渡航制限の有無を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: ارتفاع الإصابات المؤكدة بإيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية إلى 2344 حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo rise to 2,344.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 2,344 confirmed Ebola cases and 930 deaths as of July 18, 2026, per local authorities cited by Reuters. The outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, is described as the fastest-spreading on record, with most new infections arising from transmission chains that are unknown. The World Health Organization warned on July 14 that the outbreak’s transmission is accelerating. The latest update does not specify affected provinces, indicating ongoing transmission nationwide. Counts reflect laboratory-confirmed cases; no recoveries or suspected-case data are provided. Health authorities continue case finding and contact tracing, along with public health measures, to interrupt transmission from unknown chains and mitigate the impact of this highly active outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ確定感染者数が2,344人に増加
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が2,344例・930死亡と大規模化し、WHOも感染拡大の加速を警告しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 感染経路不明の伝播チェーンが多く、WHOが史上最速の拡大と警告している点で監視強化が必要。罹患率・致死率（930/2344）が高い点も特記事項。

article.articleHeadline: Antimicrobial resistance patterns and treatment outcomes of S. suis infections in Southeast Asia
article.articleSummary: Streptococcus suis infections in Southeast Asia show low penicillin resistance: pooled 2% (95% CI 0-18%) across 763 bacterial isolates from 618 patients, with a pooled human mortality of 16% (95% CI 11-22%), based on 10 eligible studies from Thailand and Vietnam through December 2024. Country-stratified analyses reveal Thailand exhibits non-linear resistance dynamics, while Vietnam maintains consistently low resistance. Ceftriaxone, penicillin, and vancomycin remain effective first-line treatments. Although penicillin resistance is generally low, reports of intermediate resistance underscore ongoing regional surveillance needs and strengthened antibiotic stewardship in pig farming, given the zoonotic risk from consumption of raw or undercooked pork. Interpret findings cautiously due to limited eligible studies and substantial heterogeneity (I2 ~68.8%). The article is published in Zoonoses (2026) by Numpong et al. Source: Compuscript Ltd.

triage.headline_ja: 東南アジアにおけるS. suis感染症の抗菌薬耐性パターンと治療転帰

triage.notes: 本記事は2024年12月までのタイ・ベトナムにおけるS. suis感染症研究のメタ分析であり、抗菌薬耐性率は低く既知の人獣共通感染症リスク（生豚肉摂取由来）に関する監視強化を提言する学術的レビュー。新規アウトブレイクの報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Canada imposes temporary Ebola travel ban
article.articleSummary: Canada imposes a temporary Ebola travel ban effective July 20, barring foreign nationals who have been in the Democratic Republic of Congo within the prior 21 days from entry. The measure aims to reduce public health risks, though Canada’s Public Health Agency says the risk to Canadians remains low. The World Health Organization discourages travel bans, warning they can stigmatize outbreaks and hinder control. Ebola spreads via direct contact with bodily fluids of an infected person. Congo has reported more than 2,100 cases and over 800 deaths. The United States has similar restrictions; European health officials oppose such bans.

triage.headline_ja: カナダが一時的なエボラ渡航禁止措置を実施

article.articleHeadline: British vial of smallpox scabs triggered the devastating 1789 outbreak among Indigenous Australians, study finds
article.articleSummary: A 1789 smallpox outbreak among Indigenous Australians is traced by computer modeling to have been introduced in 1788 by the British First Fleet, likely via dried smallpox scabs kept for inoculations, with possible replenishment during stops at Cape Town or Rio de Janeiro. The model rejects the Makassar/Sulawesi contact hypothesis and places the origin in the Port Jackson/Sydney area, not the northern coast. About 220,000 Indigenous Australians died, and the outbreak contributed to drastic cultural decline. The study, published in Nature Human Behaviour (July 9), revises estimates of pre-contact Indigenous populations upward to around 3–5 million, challenging earlier figures near 300,000 and reshaping understanding of Australia’s population and disease history prior to 1788.

triage.headline_ja: 英国から運ばれた天然痘のかさぶたが1789年の先住民オーストラリア人の大流行を引き起こしたことが研究で判明
