triage.notes: 本記事は1789年の歴史的天然痘流行に関する学術研究（Nature Human Behaviour誌）の報告であり、現代の感染症危機管理事案ではない。発生地域として付与されているインドネシア・ブラジル等も歴史的経路の議論であり、現在の発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Zustand des Ebola-Patienten verbessert sich weiter
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola patient's condition continues to improve.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-20, a US-American logistics worker for Samaritan's Purse infected with Bundibugyo ebolavirus is improving one week after arrival at Frankfurt University Hospital’s special isolation unit. He contracted Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo and presented with typical Ebola symptoms. His condition has stabilized thanks to intensive care and isolation; staff report no danger to personnel. The case emphasizes ongoing challenges in containing the Bundibugyo variant, for which there is currently no vaccine or specific therapy. The patient arrived in Frankfurt on 13 July. Earlier in May, a US doctor treated for Ebola at Berlin’s Charité was discharged after about two weeks. Ebola spreads via direct contact and body fluids, and the article notes prior Ebola/Lassavirus cases in Germany.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ患者の状態はさらに改善
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国由来のブンディブジョ型エボラウイルス感染症例がドイツへ輸入され、国際的な感染拡大と重篤な公衆衛生上の懸念を示すため、フルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断する。
triage.notes: 本症例はコンゴ民主共和国で感染し、ドイツ・フランクフルトの特殊隔離病棟で治療されている輸入例である。発生源はDRCであり、ドイツは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。ワクチン・特異的治療法が存在しないブンディブジョ型の流行継続が懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : le Canada interdit temporairement l'entrée des étrangers qui ont séjourné en RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Canada temporarily bans entry of foreigners who have stayed in the DRC.
article.articleSummary: Canada announced new Ebola containment measures, banning entry to any foreign national who has stayed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the 21 days before arrival. Earlier, Ottawa suspended immigration documents for residents of Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan. The move runs counter to WHO guidance, which recommends no travel or trade restrictions with Congo, warning that such measures can stigmatize affected populations and hinder outbreak response. The latest Ebola wave, ongoing since May and centered mainly in the DRC, has infected over 2,100 people and caused 828 deaths. Doctors Without Borders has warned that transmission is accelerating and spreading to new areas. They attribute this to limited access to care, an overwhelmed surveillance system, and mounting pressure on treatment centers, leaving many communities outside major urban areas without adequate support.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：カナダがコンゴ民主共和国(RDC)に滞在した外国人の入国を一時禁止
triage.triage_reason: DRCで進行中のエボラ流行が2100人超の感染・828人の死亡に達し、感染拡大が加速。カナダによる入国制限措置も実施されWHO勧告に反する対応が取られており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはウガンダ・南スーダン・カナダも含まれるが、記事の主題はDRCでの感染拡大とそれに対するカナダの入国制限措置。ウガンダ・南スーダンは対象国リストに含まれず、カナダも対象国外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: WHO quan ngại việc dịch Ebola lây lan nhanh
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO is concerned about the rapid spread of the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Fears grow as Ebola continues to spread rapidly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with 2,011 laboratory-confirmed cases and 754 deaths reported as of July 17, marking the fastest-spreading outbreak in the country. WHO warns the true scale may be 2–4 times higher than official counts due to surveillance gaps, as security deteriorates in eastern DRC’s Ituri province and humanitarian access is constrained. OCHA notes staff evacuations and constrained access threaten surveillance, contact tracing, and community outreach. WHO has mobilized about 40% of the $115 million required; a $69 million shortfall could undermine core response activities. In Uganda, the last Ebola patient has been discharged after a negative test; under WHO rules, 42 days without new cases are needed to declare end of the outbreak. Rwanda has not reported cases but has been allocated $2 million CERF to bolster readiness amid cross-border risk from eastern DRC.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、エボラ出血熱の急速な拡大を懸念
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上最速のエボラ拡大が続き、死者754人・確認例2,011人に達し、WHOが強い懸念を表明。資金不足や治安悪化によりサーベイランスが困難で、ウガンダ・ルワンダへの越境リスクもあり国際的拡大の懸念が高い。
triage.notes: ウガンダは最後の患者が退院済み（42日間の新規発生ゼロ確認待ち）、ルワンダは症例未報告だがCERF資金2百万ドルを準備金として配分。両国は対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Second U.S. Citizen Tests Positive for Bundibugyo Ebola in DRC and Is Medically Evacuated to Germany
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo ebolavirus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has become the third-largest Ebola epidemic on record, with 1,926 confirmed cases and 702 deaths reported by July 13, 2026, per DRC figures to WHO. A second U.S. citizen, a humanitarian worker, tested positive for Bundibugyo virus and was confirmed on July 10, 2026 by the CDC and ECDC; the patient was evacuated to a university hospital in Frankfurt, Germany, on July 13 and is in stable condition. No Bundibugyo cases have been confirmed in the United States. The outbreak began May 15, 2026 in Mongbwalu, Ituri Province, and WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17. Five provinces are affected (Ituri, North Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, South Kivu); Uganda reports Kampala cases linked to travel from DRC, and France reported an imported case June 24. No licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment exists; care is supportive. Vaccines/trials in development include Oxford BD-Ebov and MBP134/remdesivir.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでのブンディブギョ型エボラ出血熱、2人目の米国籍者が陽性判定、ドイツへ医療搬送
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言した史上3番目に大規模なエボラ流行であり、複数国（ウガンダ、フランス、ドイツ）への国際的拡大が確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当。
triage.notes: 感染は主にDRC（イトゥリ、北キブ、上ウエレ、ツォポ、南キブの5州）で発生。ウガンダ（カンパラ）、フランス、米国籍者のドイツ搬送など国際的な波及が確認されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCが唯一の対象国発生地。

article.articleHeadline: Tshopo-Ebola : le ministère provincial de la Santé promet d'accompagner le festival Kongo River - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tshopo-Ebola: the Provincial Ministry of Health promises to accompany the Kongo River Festival - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in Kisangani, capital of Tshopo Province in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with the provincial Health Ministry pledging to accompany the 6th Kongo River Festival as part of outbreak response. Dr. Augustin Mandela, adviser to the provincial health minister, says Ebola is a highly resistant virus and festival activities will include control measures, expanding to Basoko, Isangi, and Yahuma territories. The ministry is already conducting field awareness and has posted posters detailing barrier measures to curb transmission, aiming to prevent wider disruption if the outbreak worsens. The outbreak is noted as the 17th mortal outbreak in the DRC. The festival was launched in Kisangani on Sunday and runs until July 27, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: チョポ・エボラ:州保健省がコンゴ川フェスティバルへの同行支援を約束 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: DRCで新たなエボラ出血熱の発生（第17次流行）が確認され、致死率が高く人-人感染のリスクがあるため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: コンゴ川フェスティバルの開催がエボラ対策活動と並行して行われている点が特徴的。感染拡大リスクや地域の脆弱性を踏まえ、フルRRAでの詳細評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: India approves first dengue vaccine amid rising disease burden | Today News
article.articleSummary: India approves Takeda’s QDENGA, the first dengue vaccine for ages 4–60, with no pre‑vaccination screening required. The DCGI granted market authorization under CT-20/NDCT Rules 2019 to Takeda Biopharmaceuticals India Pvt. Ltd. Dengue remains a major public health burden in India, which accounts for about one‑third of global cases; 2025 reported cases exceeded 113,000, with model estimates suggesting tens of millions infected annually. QDENGA is a tetravalent, live‑attenuated vaccine administered subcutaneously in a two‑dose schedule (0.5 mL, three months apart). Its approval rests on Takeda’s global programme (19 phase I–III trials; >28,000 participants) including DEN‑301 (over 20,000 participants across eight countries) showing 12‑month efficacy of 80.2% against virologically confirmed dengue and 18‑month hospitalization efficacy of 90.4%; after 4.5 years, hospitalization protection was 84.1%. WHO prequalification enables procurement via UNICEF, and Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, and Indonesia already include QDENGA in public programs. India will receive delivery coordination with authorities and providers.

article.articleHeadline: Omicron RF.5 Variant Detected In Four COVID-19 Patients In Andhra Pradesh: Know Symptoms, Risks
article.articleSummary: Four COVID-19 cases in Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh, have been identified as the Omicron RF.5 sublineage after genome sequencing at a Pune virology lab. The positive samples were collected from Kadapa, with Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav confirming RF.5 lineage. Officials say RF.5 evolved from Omicron variants and is not more dangerous based on current data; there is no evidence of heightened public health risk. Symptoms align with other Omicron infections: sore throat, cough, fever, headache, and body aches. Routine surveillance continues, with health authorities advising vigilance but not panic. Emphasis on vaccination, hygiene, and prompt medical consultation for persistent symptoms, especially in elderly or immunocompromised individuals. The report highlights laboratory confirmation and a traceable infection pathway from initial testing to Pune sequencing, but no imported/exported case details are provided.

triage.headline_ja: オミクロンRF.5variant、アンドラ・プラデシュ州の4人のCOVID-19患者から検出：症状とリスクを知る

triage.notes: RF.5はオミクロン系統の一亜系統であり、症状も既知のオミクロン感染と同様。当局は危険性増大の証拠はないとし、通常のサーベイランス継続を強調している。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola Death Toll Hits 930, Among 2,344 Confirmed Cases
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths as of Saturday, the fastest-growing on record. Most new cases are detected outside known contact lists, and about two-thirds of deaths occur in communities, complicating containment. The toll comes amid violence against Ebola treatment centers, including an attack in Bunia that endangered patients and health workers. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warns that health interventions alone cannot stop the outbreak and calls for urgent political action to secure access, protect responders, and scale up the response, potentially including a temporary ceasefire. The situation underscores security and access challenges in outbreak control and the need for intensified surveillance and community-based measures to halt transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数930人に、確認感染者2,344人に達す
triage.triage_reason: 史上最速の拡大ペースを示すエボラ流行で、死者930人・感染者2,344人に達し、コミュニティ内感染や治療センターへの攻撃により制御が困難化しており、WHOが緊急の政治的対応を求めている。
triage.notes: コミュニティ内感染の割合が高く接触者追跡が困難な状況に加え、治療施設への暴力行為が対応を阻害。WHOは治安対策を含む政治的介入（一時停戦含む）を要請しており、国際的な支援ニーズが高い。

article.articleHeadline: Po dovolenke ju čakoval šokujúci objav. V mozgu jej našli 38 parazitov
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: After a vacation, a shocking discovery awaited her: 38 parasites were found in her brain.
article.articleSummary: Neurocysticercosis caused by Taenia solium larvae was diagnosed in Lowri Denman after a 2007 three‑month trip to India. An MRI revealed 38 brain cysts; initial suspicion of toxoplasmosis was ruled out. Transmission occurs from ingesting eggs in contaminated water or food, not pork, with hygiene gaps increasing risk. Neurocysticercosis is a common cause of acquired epilepsy in developing regions of Latin America, Africa, and Asia; in the UK and most of Europe it remains rare and usually travel- or immigrant‑associated. After a two‑week hospitalization, antiparasitic therapy with steroids reduced inflammation, but later cerebral swelling and neuropsychiatric symptoms required six weeks in a neuropsychiatric unit. The parasites died and calcified, leaving a lifelong need for antiepileptic treatment. Clinicians in Britain and the US deem this a rare, travel‑linked case, underscoring the importance of food and water safety and hygiene for travelers.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fatehpur News: Dengue and malaria cases increasing every year, department on alert.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-07-20, Fatehpur in the Doab region sees heightened risk of vector-borne diseases as monsoon rains cause waterlogging and mosquito proliferation. Health authorities have intensified surveillance to prevent dengue, malaria, and filariasis. In the past three years, malaria and dengue fluctuated, while filariasis cases declined gradually; there were no deaths from these diseases in that period. Field teams are surveying 14 sensitive areas, destroying larvae, and warning residents. Nodal officer Dr. KK Singh advised preventing water accumulation around homes, regularly changing water in coolers and tanks, and wearing full-sleeve clothing. The report emphasizes ongoing monitoring and community outreach, with no current outbreak reported, but warns transmission can rise if preventive measures are neglected.

article.articleHeadline: 嘉義市今年首例境外移入登革熱確診　籲全民落實「巡、倒、清、刷」
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chiayi City's first imported dengue fever case this year; urges the public to implement 'Inspect, Drain, Clean, Scrub'.
article.articleSummary: Chiayi City, Taiwan, reports its first imported dengue fever case of the year. The patient, a Taiwanese national with travel history to Vietnam, developed fever, headache and retro-orbital pain on July 15, sought medical care July 16, and was PCR-confirmed on July 18. The Health Bureau activated control measures, conducting vector surveillance and source reduction around the home, with indoor/outdoor chemical spraying within a 100-meter radius completed by July 20. Health education for the patient and contacts was provided. Nationally, as of July 20, Taiwan has 97 confirmed dengue cases: 90 imported and 7 locally acquired. With dengue season and hot, humid weather promoting Aedes breeding, the public is urged to Inspect, Drain, Clean, Scrub, and to wear protective clothing and use government-approved repellent. Returning travelers with fever should visit one of 41 NS1 rapid-test clinics in Chiayi City and report travel history.

Chikungunya has 37 suspected cases, 6 confirmed, 5 hospitalizations, and no deaths; Zika Virus has no notifications, confirmations, hospitalizations, or deaths this year. Among neighborhoods, the Centro leads with 292 notifications, followed by São José (191), Catalão (152), Planalto (147), Belvedere (125), Tietê (123), São Roque (115), Campina Verde (103), Afonso Pena (95), Niterói (86), Santa Lúcia (82) and Bom Pastor (82). Age distribution shows adults 20–29 years (828) the largest group, then 30–39 (759), 40–49 (678), 60+ (595), and 50–59 (494). Women account for 55.8% (2,403) and men 44.2% (1,901). Prevention focuses on eliminating Aedes aegypti breeding sites; consult the Health Ministry portal for guidance.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Bunia : un kiosque d'information installé au centre-ville pour contrer les rumeurs - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Bunia: an information kiosk installed in the city center to counter rumors - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in Bunia, Ituri province, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, is being addressed with an information kiosk in Bunia’s city center to counter rumors and improve outbreak response. Located along Boulevard de la Libération, the kiosk will function as a permanent awareness hub, broadcasting audible messages and distributing leaflets and posters in at least three local languages to reach a broad audience. Abbé Chrysanthe Ngabu, CDJP provincial coordinator, emphasizes dispelling misinformation that delays care and increases fatalities, and urges community involvement and adherence to barrier measures while collaborating with health teams. The initiative, by Caritas Bunia with support from the international NGO Trócaire and Irish government funding, aims to strengthen risk communication during the Ebola response. Published July 20, 2026.

article.articleHeadline: 🔴ଦେଶର ପ୍ରଥମ ଡେଙ୍ଗୁ ଟିକା India Gets Its First Dengue Vaccine, QDENGA | India's first dengue vaccine

The report centers on regulatory approval and the defined eligible population, signaling a potential public health tool against dengue in India as of 2026-07-20.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : des actions de sensibilisation renforcées au sein de l'archidiocèse de Kisangani - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Strengthened awareness campaigns within the Archdiocese of Kisangani - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola awareness campaigns have been strengthened in the Archdiocese of Kisangani, in Tshopo Province, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Through the diocesan Office of Medical Works, the archbishop’s pastoral letter is read each Sunday in parishes to warn the faithful and urge adherence to barrier measures. Besides handwashing kits at church entrances, priests read the message during Eucharist to reinforce prevention. Masks remain insuffciently used. Other denominations, including Protestant and revival churches, are also mobilizing, with handwashing devices installed at some worship sites, though challenges remain in teaching Sunday school children and maintaining physical distancing. In large congregations such as Cité de Refuge and Hebron, no visible prevention measures were observed. Ebola cases with deaths have been recorded in the area, though exact numbers are not provided. The public health message stresses taking Ebola seriously and following authorities’ sanitary guidelines.

article.articleHeadline: الهند تحصل على أول لقاح ضد حمى الضنك
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India gets its first dengue fever vaccine.
article.articleSummary: India approves Takeda’s dengue vaccine, QDENGA, the country’s first dengue vaccine authorization. For ages 4–60, the two 0.5 mL doses are given three months apart and do not require prior dengue infection status or pre-vaccination screening. QDENGA covers all four dengue serotypes. Approval cites data from 19 trials (Phase I–III) with more than 28,000 participants in dengue-endemic and non-endemic settings; India-specific Phase 3 data show safety and immunogenicity in 4–60-year-olds. Seven-year follow-up indicates durable protection against dengue infection and hospitalization across all serotypes. India accounts for roughly one-third of global dengue cases, driven by urbanization, climate change, and widespread mosquito proliferation. WHO recommends use in high-transmission areas, and QDENGA has WHO prequalification, making it eligible for procurement by UNICEF and PAHO.

article.articleHeadline: Brasil recebe banco de antígenos contra febre aftosa após acordo com empresa argentina
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Brazil Receives Foot-and-Mouth Disease Antigen Bank After Agreement with Argentine Company
article.articleSummary: Brazil received from Argentine company Biogénesis Bagó a strategic antigen bank for foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) emergencies, during a July 17, 2026 ceremony in Garín, Buenos Aires Province. The agreement, announced in December 2025, establishes a bank storing 10 million doses of antigens for the two FMD serotypes most circulating in Brazil, with the ability to immediately supply up to 10 million vaccine doses in case of outbreaks. The facility is integrated with Brazil’s Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAPA) and the Paraná Technology Institute (Tecpar), and the supplier. The system enables rapid vaccine production from pre-validated antigens stored under controlled conditions, reducing response time in surveillance and contingency programs. Attendees included MAPA and Tecpar representatives, Biogénesis Bagó executives, Argentine sanitary service officials, and Brazil’s embassy staff in Buenos Aires.

article.articleHeadline: Banco de antígenos amplia proteção do rebanho brasileiro contra a febre aftosa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Antigen Bank Expands Protection for Brazil's Herd Against Foot-and-Mouth Disease
article.articleSummary: Brazil inaugurated the first Brazilian Antigen Bank for emergency response to foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), installed in Buenos Aires, Argentina. The initial stock comprises 10 million doses of antigens corresponding to the two FMD virus serotypes most historically circulating in Brazil, with a contract allowing another 10 million doses over the next ten years for potential outbreaks. The initiative is a partnership between Tecpar (Institute of Technology of Paraná) and Argentina's Biogénesis Bagó. For biosafety, the material is stored outside Brazil, a model also used by the United States and United Kingdom at Bagó's facility. The bank enables rapid vaccine production to quickly isolate affected areas without compromising the country's sanitary status, a key requirement to maintain Brazil's recognition by the World Organisation for Animal Health. It strengthens the agro-industrial sector by ensuring a prompt response to localized FMD foci.

article.articleHeadline: Weak surveillance, research gaps driving persistent Ebola outbreaks -Expert
article.articleSummary: Persistent Ebola outbreaks in the DRC and Uganda are driven by weak surveillance, insufficient funding, and research gaps, according to Prof. Bamidele Iwalokun. Four major gaps: inadequate genomic surveillance, weak implementation research, limited understanding of Bundibugyo and other non-Zaire Ebola virus species, and underinvestment in diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines. He notes the lack of comprehensive genomic intelligence for all human pathogenic Ebola species hampers surveillance and response, and limited understanding of the evolution and transmission of Bundibugyo strains. Community resistance and burial practices impede containment, with many cases detected at advanced stages. Calls for proactive community-level surveillance, rapid immune-based diagnostics, and more funding for point-of-care tests. Transmission is not airborne; it spreads by direct contact with infected blood, bodily fluids, or contaminated materials, risking healthcare workers and caregivers. As of July 15, WHO reports 2124 confirmed DRC cases and 828 deaths; ongoing Bundibugyo outbreaks in the DRC and Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: 監視体制の弱さと研究の遅れが持続的なエボラ流行の要因—専門家
triage.triage_reason: DRCで2124例・828死亡、ウガンダでもBundibugyo株の流行が継続中であり、ヒト-ヒト感染・監視体制不備・資金不足など複数のIHR/WPRO基準に該当するため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダも発生地域として挙げられているが、対象国リストにUgandaが含まれていないため verified_locations には含めていない。WHO報告に基づく累積データ（2124例・828死亡）は既知の進行中アウトブレイクの延長線上と見られるが、専門家が構造的な監視・研究の欠陥を指摘している点で重要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: AIIMS Bhopal Organises Dengue, Malaria Awareness Drive For School Students
article.articleSummary: AIIMS Bhopal organised a health awareness programme at Barkhedi School, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, to boost prevention of dengue, malaria, chikungunya, and other seasonal infections during the monsoon. The session educated students, teachers, and the local community on preventing mosquito-borne diseases by eliminating breeding sites: regularly cleaning coolers, water storage tanks, flower pots, discarded tyres, and other water-holding containers; wearing full-sleeved clothing; using mosquito repellents and nets; avoiding self-medication; and seeking prompt medical care for fever. An interactive Q&A demonstrated practical prevention methods and stressed maintaining a clean environment, preventing water stagnation, and active community participation as essential. Led by Dr Kuldeep Gupta, Senior Resident, with Dr Abhishek Kumar, Dr Malav, and other team members from the Department of Community and Family Medicine, the campaign highlighted evidence-based practices and the community’s role in public health.

article.articleHeadline: La riposte contre Ebola freinée à Goma par la méfiance communautaire
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola response slowed in Goma due to community mistrust.
article.articleSummary: Ebola response in Goma has slowed due to community mistrust, according to CONAFOD-RDC. Despite medical advances, rumors, refusals to follow up on contacts, and persistent unsafe clandestine burials fuel transmission chains. To break mistrust, local actors argue for shifting the paradigm toward empowerment of local actors: field NGOs, women's and youth associations, and Ebola survivor networks are frontline responders during outbreaks and remain best suited to accompany communities after international agencies depart. Yet funding gaps severely constrain these efforts. CONAFOD-RDC calls for direct emergency funds to reach grassroots groups, enabling faster alerts and more effective rumor debunking and prevention messaging through trusted local actors. They propose an innovation: the Action locale de lutte contre Ebola to channel funds directly to community structures, bypassing bureaucratic bottlenecks. Strengthening local financing and accountability is seen as the only durable safeguard for East Congo's current and future epidemics.

article.articleHeadline: Αντιμικροβιακή αντοχή και αποτελέσματα θεραπείας λοιμώξεων από S. suis στη Νοτιοανατολική Ασία " OnCamera.gr
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Antimicrobial resistance and treatment outcomes of infections caused by S. suis in Southeast Asia OnCamera.gr
article.articleSummary: Streptococcus suis infections in Southeast Asia are evaluated for antimicrobial resistance and treatment outcomes. A systematic review and meta-analysis of nine databases up to December 2024 included 763 bacterial isolates and 618 patients from Thailand and Vietnam. Cumulative penicillin resistance is low at 2% (95% CI 0-18%), but substantial inter-study heterogeneity (I2 68.8%) and country-specific patterns were observed: Thailand showed nonlinear resistance trends, while Vietnam remained consistently low. Overall mortality among patients was 16% (95% CI 11-22%). First-line therapies ceftriaxone, penicillin, and vancomycin remain effective, though signals of intermediate penicillin resistance call for caution. The findings underscore the need for ongoing antimicrobial surveillance and improved antibiotic stewardship in pig farming. Linkage to infection through consumption of undercooked pork emphasizes the public health relevance in the region, with calls for cautious treatment and further research given limited study numbers and data variability.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Africa out of control; the number of infections in Congo has surpassed 2,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), centered in the eastern region near the Uganda border, with 2,011 confirmed infections and 930 deaths as of July 20, 2026. The outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, began in May and is advancing faster than any previous Congo outbreak. WHO notes about 80% of new cases involve unknown transmission chains, while conflict-affected areas hinder medical access. Bunia General Hospital, the region’s largest center, faced a staff strike over unpaid wages, complicating response. Across settings, 753 patients are in isolation or hospitalized, and 366 have recovered. This marks the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC since 1976; the prior September 2025 Kasai outbreak (southwest) killed more than 40 and was declared over after about three months.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : à Djugu, neuf postes de santé sur douze ont fermé leurs portes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: in Djugu, nine health posts out of twelve have closed their doors.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo worsens in Djugu, Ituri, with 2,344 cases and 930 deaths reported as of 18 July; Ituri now has 27 of 36 health zones affected. In Limani's Héritage health area, nine of twelve health posts have closed, crowding the few remaining facilities. On 15 July, local leaders warned the situation is grave, with over a hundred deaths reported locally, though officials have not confirmed these provisional figures. Denial of preventive measures by communities in Djatsi and Pitsi—parallels observed north in Haut-Uele—fuel transmission. Kinshasa reported on 16 July that all suspected cases are tested and diagnoses provided within 24 hours by INRB, yet this requires functioning clinics. Limani’s closures impede screening, isolation, and supportive care for Bundibugyo, the Ebola strain there, for which no vaccine or specific treatment exists.

article.articleHeadline: India Approves First Dengue Vaccine! Eligible for People Aged 4 to 60
article.articleSummary: India has approved Takeda’s dengue vaccine QDENGA, the first dengue vaccine in the country for ages 4–60. The two-dose, subcutaneous schedule (three-month interval) requires no prior dengue testing. India, accounting for about one-third of global dengue cases, reported over 113,000 cases in 2025, though actual numbers may be higher. QDENGA targets all four dengue serotypes and showed 80.2% efficacy against dengue 12 months after the second dose, and a 90.4% reduction in dengue-related hospitalizations; long-term data indicate 84.1% hospitalization protection after 4.5 years, with safety and efficacy up to seven years. WHO has recommended and prequalified QDENGA; the vaccine is approved in 43 countries with over 32 million doses distributed, including use in Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, and Indonesia. Precautions against mosquitoes remain essential post-vaccination: eliminate standing water, wear protective clothing, use nets/repellents. Seek care for fever, body aches, or low platelets.

article.articleHeadline: बरसाती बीमारियों को लेकर झारखंड सरकार अलर्ट, मंत्री इरफान अंसारी ने 108 एंबुलेंस और अस्पतालों को दिए खास निर्देश - jharkhand irfan ansari alerts civil surgeons on monsoon diseases
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Jharkhand Government on Alert Regarding Monsoon Diseases; Minister Irfan Ansari Issues Special Instructions to the 108 Ambulance Service and Hospitals.
article.articleSummary: July 20, 2026 — Jharkhand Health Minister Irfan Ansari ordered Civil Surgeons to keep monsoon-era infectious and seasonal diseases on high alert. The season brings malaria, dengue, chikungunya, cholera, diarrhea, typhoid, viral fever, and increased snakebite cases. Hospitals and health facilities must operate at full capacity 24/7 with adequate doctors, specialists, nurses (ANMs, GNM), lab technicians, pharmacists and other staff. The 108 ambulance service must run uninterrupted; until a new agency is ready, civil surgeons will directly supervise government ambulances to ensure timely hospital access. Special monitoring for pregnant women, newborns, children, the elderly and severely ill; refer without delay to higher institutes if needed, with families informed. Pediatric wards, SNCU, NBSU and emergency services must be fully active; ensure stocks of ORS, zinc, antibiotics, antipyretics, nebulization meds, oxygen, dengue/malaria testing kits, vaccines and other life-saving drugs.

triage.headline_ja: モンスーン期の疾病に関してジャールカンド州政府が警戒、イルファン・アンサリ大臣が108救急サービスと病院に特別指示

article.articleHeadline: No combate à dengue, receba o agente de saúde | JC Rio Claro
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the fight against dengue, meet the community health worker
article.articleSummary: Preventive home visits by Rio Claro's Center for Zoonosis Control (CCZ) health agents target Aedes aegypti, the dengue vector. Agents, identifiable by uniform and badge, inspect residences for mosquito breeding sites and advise on measures to prevent dengue, chikungunya, Zika virus, and yellow fever. Residents should verify the agent’s badge and call CCZ at 3522-1435 if in doubt before entry. The program covers the entire city, with daily neighborhood updates from the Fundação de Saúde and CCZ on social media about where teams are working. As of July 20, 2026, Rio Claro reports 21 dengue cases this year; there are no reported cases of Zika, chikungunya, or yellow fever in the municipality. The initiative emphasizes public health engagement to reduce transmission of dengue and other Aedes‑transmitted diseases.

article.articleHeadline: Araçatuba registra queda no índice de infestação do Aedes aegypti, mas resultado mantém cidade em estado de alerta
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Araçatuba records a drop in the Aedes aegypti infestation index, but the result keeps the city on high alert.
article.articleSummary: Araçatuba's Municipal Health Secretariat completed the third Larval Density Assessment (ADL) of the year, showing a drop in Aedes aegypti infestation, the vector for dengue, chikungunya, and Zika virus. The Predial Infestation Index (IIP) for July reached 2.1%, down from 3.80% in January and 2.54% in May, but the city stays on high alert. The survey, conducted July 1–15, inspected 4,443 properties across 865 blocks in 16 urban areas, by 60 vector-control agents and 14 UVZ supervisors. A total of 110 larval breeding sites were found in drains, animal troughs, plant pots, pools, buckets, and cans. The neighborhoods with the highest indices were Morada dos Nobres, TV, Umuarama, Alvorada, and Maria Tereza de Andrade. Since year‑start, dengue has 2,005 positives with one death; chikungunya has 739 cases and two deaths; 10,174 cases were discarded and 213 await results, totaling 12,392 notifications.

article.articleHeadline: ابولا در کنگو از کنترل خارج شد/ سریع‌ترین شیوع تاریخ ثبت موارد ابتلا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo has gotten out of control / The fastest outbreak in history of recorded infections.
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, is spreading at an unprecedented rate—the fastest growth since case reporting began. About 90% of registered cases are in a province bordering Uganda, where ongoing conflict has severely limited access to care. Mortality ranges from 25% to 90% depending on the virus strain. Bunia General Hospital, the region’s largest medical center, has seen healthcare workers strike over unpaid wages. Since May, the outbreak has persisted despite intensified response efforts. The Congo Ministry of Health reports 753 patients in isolation or in hospitals, with 366 recovered. The World Health Organization notes that at least 80% of new cases have unknown transmission chains. Doctors Without Borders (MSF) corroborates the rapid spread surpassing all previous outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: Rohamosan növekszik az Ebola áldozatainak száma, már az EU-ban is regisztráltak fertőzötteket
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola victims is rising rapidly, with infections already registered in the EU as well.
article.articleSummary: By 20 July 2026, Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo approach 1,000, driven by a surge in Ituri Province linked to Bundibugyo virus, one of the outbreak’s fastest-spreading forms. Healthcare worker strikes over delayed pay contributed to at least 36 infected medical staff deaths. Despite this, the DRC health ministry reports strengthened patient care and support capacity, with 22 recoveries recorded within 24 hours. Outside DRC, 20 confirmed cases have been documented, including two deaths in Uganda and one case in France, indicating cross-border spread into the European Union. A new vaccine targeting the current outbreak variant is to be tested in adults in the United Kingdom by Oxford University; volunteers are being recruited and regulatory approval is anticipated before rollout.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: India's first dengue vaccine 'Qdenga'...
article.articleSummary: India's DCGI has approved Takeda's dengue vaccine Qdenga for individuals aged 4 to 60, making it the country's first dengue vaccine. The decision allows vaccination irrespective of prior dengue infection, with no pre-vaccination testing required. Developed in 2022, Qdenga has been approved in 43 countries and has delivered over 30 million doses worldwide. The vaccine provides protection against all four dengue virus serotypes and is administered as two 0.5 mL injections spaced three months apart. The approval confirms compliance with international standards for quality, safety, and efficacy, and positions India to expand dengue prevention using a globally recognized vaccine.

article.articleHeadline: 930 Dead in Outbreak; FDA Backtracks on Iceberg Lettuce; Chronic Cough Drug Fizzles
article.articleSummary: At least 930 people have died in Congo's Ebola outbreak, according to the Congo Ministry of Health, with safety fears hampering response and at least a dozen attacks on health facilities and workers. Seven Americans are under quarantine at a controversial Ebola isolation facility in Kenya following a U.S. travel ban. In New York City, a Legionnaires' disease outbreak has produced a third death. These developments underscore concurrent infectious-disease crises across Africa and the United States and the fragility of outbreak responses amid security and political challenges. Reported as of July 20, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: アウトブレイクで930人死亡；FDAがアイスバーグレタスの方針を撤回；慢性咳治療薬が不振
triage.triage_reason: コンゴのエボラ流行で930人が死亡し、暴力による対応阻害や米国渡航禁止措置など国際的な影響が拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大なシグナルである。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCのエボラ流行（930人死亡、医療施設への攻撃）、ケニアでの米国人隔離、NYCのレジオネラ症流行という3つの独立した話題を含む複合記事。対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ（ケニア・米国は対象国外）。ケニアやNYCの事案は別途評価が必要な可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: Alertă în Europa: Gonoreea rezistentă la antibiotice câștigă teren. Unde sunt cele mai multe cazuri
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Alert in Europe: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhea is gaining ground. Where the most cases are.
article.articleSummary: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhea is spreading in Europe, with local transmission rising since 2025, not just imported cases. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) reports growing numbers in France, Germany, Sweden, and the United Kingdom, while other countries report sporadic cases. Although overall risk to the sexually active general population remains low, rising resistance to first-line therapies threatens treatment effectiveness. Neisseria gonorrhoeae is the pathogen; the main current regimen is ceftriaxone, alone or with azithromycin, but resistance to both drugs is increasing. Imports from outside Europe remain the primary route for ceftriaxone-resistant strains entering the region, notably from Southeast Asia (Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam), which have caused treatment failures in Europe and North America. In 2024, 106,331 confirmed gonorrhea cases were reported in Europe—the highest since EU surveillance began in 2009; globally, about 82 million new cases occur annually among ages 15–49.

triage.headline_ja: 欧州で警戒：抗生物質耐性淋菌が拡大。最も症例が多い地域はどこか
triage.triage_reason: 記事の主題は欧州（フランス・ドイツ・スウェーデン・英国）における薬剤耐性淋菌の拡大であり、東南アジア諸国（ベトナム・インドネシア・タイ）は耐性株の輸入元として言及されているのみで、当該国での発生事象を報告するものではないため対象国イベントとして該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事は欧州における薬剤耐性淋菌拡大に関するもので、東南アジア諸国は耐性株の起源として言及されているに過ぎず、当該国内での発生報告ではないため verified_locations は空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Apstiprināto Ebolas upuru skaits Kongo DR sasniedzis 930
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of confirmed Ebola victims in the DR Congo has reached 930.
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 2,344 confirmed Ebola virus disease (EVD) cases and at least 930 deaths, with 37 deaths in the last 24 hours. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant, which was not initially detected by conventional diagnostics, and there is no vaccine for this variant. The Ituri Province is the hardest hit, with response efforts hampered by deteriorating security conditions. Since outbreak confirmation on May 15, there have been at least 12 attacks on health facilities and workers. Widespread healthcare disruption is evident as many clinicians have stopped working due to low pay; at least 36 infected health workers have died. Currently, 724 Ebola patients are in isolation or hospitalized.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ確定死者数が930人に達した
triage.triage_reason: ワクチンのないブンディブギョ株による大規模流行で死者930人・症例2,344人に達し、治安悪化による対応困難も加わり、国際的拡大リスクと深刻な公衆衛生影響が認められるためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ワクチン未対応のブンディブギョ株、治安悪化による医療施設攻撃、医療従事者の死亡・離職など対応能力低下が顕著。国際的な支援・監視強化が急務。

article.articleHeadline: " Ebola qui marche " : ce que la lenteur de la souche Bundibugyo dit de l'épidémie en RDC, et de la manière de la soigner
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Walking Ebola": what the slow pace of the Bundibugyo strain tells us about the outbreak in the DRC, and how to treat it.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in the DRC, centered in Ituri with Bunia as epicenter, began in May and is the largest outbreak for this strain. By July 17, 2,267 confirmed cases and 893 deaths were reported (about 40% CFR), with Ituri ~90% of cases. Clinicians describe 'walking Ebola': the slower-replicating Bundibugyo virus leaves patients ambulatory and infectious in the community, hindering surveillance since over 80% of new infections occur outside known contacts; two-thirds of deaths occur outside health facilities. Early treatment improves survival; the slower progression could widen the therapeutic window, though this awaits evidence. Trials in Bunia: PARTNERS testing MBP134 and remdesivir (and their combination), and EBO-PEP testing obeldesivir for post-exposure prophylaxis; coordinated by WHO with INRB Kinshasa, ITM Antwerp, Oxford, and supported by ALIMA and MSF. A funding gap exceeds $400 million. The virus was first identified in Uganda in 2007; largest Bundibugyo outbreak to date.

triage.headline_ja: 「歩くエボラ」：ブンディブジョ株の進行の遅さがDRCのアウトブレイクと治療法について示すこと
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大のブンディブジョ株エボラアウトブレイクが発生し、致死率約40%、地域内での追跡困難な感染拡大が確認されており、国際支援も必要とされているためフルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: ベルギー・英国・ウガンダは研究機関の連携先や過去の発生地として言及されているのみで、現在のアウトブレイク発生国はDRC（イトゥリ州、ブニア中心）のみ。40%の致死率と資金不足（4億ドル超）が特に懸念事項。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola deaths soar as total nears 1,000 amid attacks on health centres and staff
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reports a Bundibugyo virus–driven Ebola outbreak with 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths; 37 deaths were recorded in the last 24 hours. Ituri province is the worst hit, accounting for most cases, with five of 26 provinces affected. Attacks on health centres and frontline workers—at least 12 since mid-May—have hampered the response, with security fears prompting staff relocations and walkouts over unpaid salaries. 724 patients remain in isolation or hospital care, and 22 recoveries were recorded in the latest 24 hours. The Bundibugyo virus has no approved vaccine or treatment; transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids, contaminated surfaces, and zoonotic spillover from wild animals. WHO reports 80% of new cases originate from unknown chains, underscoring rapid, hard-to-trace spread.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ死者数が急増、医療施設・職員への攻撃の中で1,000人に迫る
triage.triage_reason: DRCでブンディブギョウイルスによるエボラ様アウトブレイクが2,344例・930死亡と大規模化し、ワクチン・治療法未承認、医療施設への攻撃や感染経路不明の新規例が多く、国際的拡大・公衆衛生上の深刻な影響が明確なためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョウイルス(Bundibugyo virus)によるエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク。ワクチン・治療薬未承認で、医療施設への攻撃や職員の安全確保問題が対応を著しく阻害している。WHOによると新規感染例の80%が感染経路不明であり、急速かつ追跡困難な拡大が懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: La RD del Congo eleva a 930 el número de muertos y a 2.344 los casos confirmados de ébola - Hondudiario
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo raises the death toll to 930 and 2,344 confirmed Ebola cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) tallies 930 deaths and 2,344 confirmed cases as of July 18, 2026, with a 39.7% case fatality. Of cases, 724 are in isolation or hospital, and 466 have recovered; contact tracing stands at 85.8%. Five affected provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo. Community transmission continues, reinforcing the need for intensified epicenter interventions and neighboring-province preparedness, per the INSP. The outbreak began May 15 in Ituri near borders with South Sudan and Uganda; spread to Uganda with 20 cases (15 imported) and 2 deaths, and a 42-day countdown without new cases. Bundibugyo strain has 30–50% fatality; no approved vaccine or specific treatment (WHO). Third-worst Ebola epidemic; seventeenth in DRC. Compared with 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak (≈11,000 deaths, 28,000 cases) and 2018–2020 DRC outbreak (2,299 deaths, 3,481 cases). Transmission via bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and hemorrhaging.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ死者数930人、確定感染者数2,344人に増加
triage.triage_reason: DRCで大規模なエボラ流行が継続し死者930人・感染者2,344人に達し、ウガンダへの越境拡大も確認されているためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの感染拡大が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。致死率39.7%と高く、承認されたワクチン・治療法がない点、また地域社会での感染継続が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Prefeitura de Caucaia faz mutirão contra a dengue e atende 1,6 mil moradores
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Caucaia City Hall launches an anti-dengue drive and serves 1,600 residents.
article.articleSummary: Caucaia's City Hall conducted an anti-dengue operation in the Parque das Nações neighborhood, reaching about 1,600 residents across 17 blocks. On Friday, July 17, a task force aimed to eliminate Aedes aegypti breeding sites to curb dengue and reduce risks for Zika and chikungunya. Activities included street cleaning, weed clearing, and whitewashing, and the Cata-treco bulk waste removal program to prevent standing water in yards. Seventeen endemic disease control agents conducted technical visits, identifying risk areas and distributing educational leaflets. Residents were advised to keep preventive measures at home and eliminate any containers that can collect water. The operation involved multiple municipal departments—the SMS Health, Seinfra Infrastructure, SME Education, SDS Social Development, IMAC Environment Institute, Patrimony, and Communications—with plans for similar actions in other neighborhoods.

triage.headline_ja: カウカイア市役所がデング熱対策の一斉活動を実施、住民1,600人に対応
triage.triage_reason: 通常の予防的なデング熱対策活動（清掃・ボウフラ駆除・広報）であり、異常な感染拡大や重症例の報告はなく、ルーティンの公衆衛生活動に過ぎない。
triage.notes: 記事は感染症の発生報告ではなく、自治体による予防的な媒介蚊対策活動の紹介記事。

article.articleHeadline: BMC Intensifies Dengue Prevention Drive In Bhubaneswar, 12 Cases Reported This Year
article.articleSummary: As of 20 July 2026, Bhubaneswar reports 12 dengue cases this year, with a 0.11% positivity rate (10,618 samples tested; 12 positives; one imported). The BMC intensified dengue prevention through three-zone door-to-door surveillance. Since July 1, teams surveyed 40,639 households and reached 127,517 residents; 3,554 breeding sites detected and 2,968 sources destroyed. A source-reduction drive removed 34,283 water-holding containers. Anti-larval operations involve 220 trained personnel and 90 spray machines, using larvicides such as Temephos. IEC activities total 2,403, along with 45 community meetings and 75 school programmes, plus leaflets. Mayor Sulochana Das attributes the decline to early measures; 70 outsourced workers and 150 BMC staff assist with fogging when weather allows. Residents are urged to prevent water stagnation and regularly clean water storage containers.

triage.headline_ja: BMC、ブバネスワルでデング熱予防対策を強化 今年の感染者数は12件
triage.triage_reason: 感染者数12件と低水準で陽性率も0.11%と低く、既に行政による予防対策が効果を上げている通常の季節性デング対応であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは見られない。
triage.notes: 地方自治体（BMC）による通常のデング熱予防活動の報告記事であり、感染者数も少なく管理下にある。

article.articleHeadline: Ministério da Saúde recomenda 'dose zero' contra sarampo em São Bernardo do Campo após casos suspeitos; entenda
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health recommends 'zero-dose' against measles in São Bernardo do Campo after suspected cases; find out more.
article.articleSummary: Measles: Brazil's Ministry of Health recommended a 'zero-dose' of the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine for children aged 6–11 months in São Bernardo do Campo, São Paulo, after two suspected cases were investigated. The extra dose precedes the routine D1 at 12 months and D2 at 15 months, enhancing protection for under-1-year-olds in areas with transmission risk, but it does not replace routine vaccination. The measure is already adopted in São Paulo city and Guarulhos. Between June 2 and July 17, 2026, São Paulo city confirmed eight measles cases, all imported or linked to importation; 16 additional cases are under investigation (13 in São Paulo city, 2 in São Bernardo do Campo, 1 in Guarulhos), and five cases have been ruled out. The strategy aims to reduce susceptibles, interrupt transmission, and prevent severe disease.

triage.headline_ja: 保健省、サンベルナルド・ド・カンポでの疑い症例発生後、麻疹に対する『ゼロ回接種』を推奨
triage.triage_reason: サンパウロ州で輸入関連の麻疹症例が確認され、追加接種措置が取られているが、現時点では大規模な公衆衛生危機や国際的拡大の証拠はなく、続報を注視すべき段階。
triage.notes: 症例は輸入関連であり、地域内での限定的な感染拡大に対する予防的ワクチン接種強化措置。重症例や死亡の報告はなく、国レベルでの対応で管理可能と見られる。

article.articleHeadline: Guinée équatoriale : une alerte à l'Ebola dans l'hôtel où Washington déporte des migrants
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Equatorial Guinea: an Ebola alert at the hotel where Washington is deporting migrants.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola alert centers on a Malabo hotel in Equatorial Guinea where 17 migrants deported from the United States are being held under a government detention program. Lawyers and two anonymous deportees allege that a man, then a woman, were brought to the hotel by medical staff in protective gear and placed on a floor below detainees; a doctor allegedly told them in English that they were suspected Ebola cases. No health authority—Ministry of Health, WHO, or Africa CDC—has confirmed or denied the claim, and Equatorial Guinea is not listed in current outbreak bulletins. The Associated Press has seen footage of staff transporting patients to the hotel, which previously functioned as a Covid-19 isolation site. The 17 detainees (four women, 13 men) originate from Angola, Mauritania, and Ethiopia, detained since October 2025 under a US deportation agreement worth about $7.5 million. Context notes a Congo outbreak (Bundibugyo strain) with thousands of cases in the DRC, but no confirmed link to Equatorial Guinea.

triage.headline_ja: 赤道ギニア:米国が移民を送還するホテルでエボラ警戒
triage.triage_reason: 赤道ギニアのホテルで移民収容者にエボラ疑い例が報告されたが、保健当局・WHO・Africa CDCいずれも確認・否定しておらず、情報が極めて不確実なため続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は赤道ギニア（対象国外）のホテルでの未確認エボラ疑い例。DRCのエボラ流行は背景文脈として言及されているのみで、記事の主題ではないため除外した。確定診断・当局確認がなく、情報の信頼性が低い点に留意が必要。

article.articleHeadline: A deadly Ebola crisis is accelerating -- and health workers face mounting obstacles
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri province, Bunia) driven by the Bundibugyo strain with no approved vaccine or specific treatment. As of Saturday, 930 deaths among 2,344 confirmed cases, plus 37 deaths in 24 hours, the deadliest single-day rise in recent weeks. Declared May 15 in eastern Congo, the outbreak is described as the fastest-growing Ebola epidemic ever recorded in the country. Security constraints and violence hinder response, with attacks on health facilities and teams and staffing shortages as workers report unpaid wages. Dozens of frontline staff have died after infection while treating patients. More than 700 patients remain in isolation or hospital treatment as response teams conduct contact tracing and disease-control measures, with many new infections not linked to known transmission chains, complicating containment.

triage.headline_ja: 致死的なエボラ危機が加速している――医療従事者は増大する障害に直面
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州で発生中のエボラ出血熱がこれまでで最速の拡大を見せ、致死率が高く未承認ワクチンのブンディブギョ株であること、また感染経路不明の新規感染が増加している点から、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 930人死亡・2344人確認感染、致死率約40%。ブンディブギョ株で承認ワクチンなし。治安悪化と医療従事者への攻撃・未払い賃金により対応が困難化。感染経路不明の新規感染が多く、封じ込めが複雑化している。

article.articleHeadline: At Least 930 People Have Died in DR Congo amid Reports Ebola Outbreak Could Be 'Deadliest on Record'
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus: 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths as of July 18, with 724 in isolation; 37 deaths in the 24 hours to July 19–20. Declared May 15 and May 17 emergency status, it is the fastest-growing outbreak. There is no approved treatment or vaccine for Bundibugyo; transmission occurs via body fluids and from infected animals, people, or contaminated surfaces. At least 12 attacks on health workers and facilities have been recorded; protests in Kenya over a quarantine center have left one protester dead. At least 36 health workers have died after infection. WHO warns up to 80% of new cases come from undetected transmission chains. Outside DRC, 20 confirmed cases and two deaths; Uganda has one probable case and one probable death; France one confirmed case. Oxford researchers are developing a Bundibugyo-targeted vaccine, with testing on healthy adults and 6–9 months to development.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国で少なくとも930人が死亡、エボラ出血熱の流行は「記録上最悪」になる可能性との報道
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で確認2,344例・930人死亡という大規模なエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行が急速に拡大しており、承認済み治療薬・ワクチンが存在せず、国境を越えた感染例（ウガンダ、ケニア、フランス）も確認されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはウガンダ、ケニア、フランスも含まれるが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。主発生国はDRC。WHOは新規感染の80%が未検出の感染経路によるものと警告しており、感染拡大の継続リスクが高い。

article.articleHeadline: Delhi Health Minister reviews hospital readiness for Monsoon diseases
article.articleSummary: New Delhi, 20 July 2026 — Delhi Health Minister Dr. Pankaj Kumar Singh directed all government hospitals to stay on high alert for monsoon-related illnesses, notably dengue, malaria and chikungunya, and to ensure uninterrupted access to medicines, diagnostics, and essential healthcare services. In a high-level review, authorities emphasized strengthened service delivery, stock adequacy for medicines, and functional diagnostic and laboratory investigations across hospitals to manage any surge during the monsoon. The briefing also covered vacancies in technical Health Department posts, with instructions to expedite recruitment to bolster workforce capacity. Separately, a committee headed by the Special Secretary (Health) will investigate the GTB Hospital incident and report within three days, with strict departmental action for negligence. The government reaffirmed its commitment to accessible, affordable, high-quality care and improved disease preparedness.

triage.headline_ja: デリー保健大臣、モンスーン期の疾病に対する病院の準備状況を確認
triage.triage_reason: デリーでの季節性のデング熱・マラリア・チクングニアへの警戒・準備に関する行政的な報道であり、具体的な患者数増加や異常な流行拡大の情報がないため、経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: モンスーン季節に毎年発生するベクター媒介性疾患への予防的な行政対応であり、現時点で異常な流行や重症例の急増を示す情報はない。続報で症例数の動向を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: People with type 2 diabetes face higher risk of severe dengue, study finds
article.articleSummary: Dengue is a viral disease transmitted by mosquitoes, infecting millions annually, with tropical nations like India particularly affected. A new study finds adults with type 2 diabetes may have a higher risk of severe dengue, including plasma leakage, heavy bleeding, or organ failure. Diabetes may provoke inflammation and suppress immune responses, and poorly controlled blood sugar may heighten vulnerability. The study, published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases, underscores the need for early monitoring and timely treatment for dengue symptoms in people with diabetes. WHO notes diabetes can impact blood vessels and immune defense, with high glucose potentially weakening immunity, promoting inflammation, damaging vessels, and delaying recovery. Dengue symptoms typically appear 4–10 days after a mosquito bite and include high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle/joint pain, nausea, rash, and fatigue. Preventive measures focus on avoiding bites: repellents, protective clothing, nets, eliminating standing water, and screens.

triage.headline_ja: 2型糖尿病患者は重症デング熱のリスクが高いことが研究で判明
triage.triage_reason: 特定の発生イベントではなく、糖尿病患者における重症デング熱リスクに関する研究結果の紹介記事であり、公衆衛生上の新規シグナルとは言えない。
triage.notes: 記事は研究結果の解説であり、特定国での発生状況やアウトブレイクを報じるものではないため、対象国での具体的イベントとして扱わない。

article.articleHeadline: 花百萬相親閃婚！孕檢報告驚呆人夫　妻是癮君子「坐過牢還染梅毒」
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Spent a fortune on a blind date and a shotgun wedding! The pregnancy test report stuns the husband—the wife is a drug addict who has served time and even contracted syphilis.
article.articleSummary: From Jiangxi Province, China, a man traveled to Guiyang, Guizhou Province, through a matchmaking intermediary and quickly married, spending over 300,000 yuan. Prenatal health screening revealed the wife concealed a history of drug use, involvement in a money-laundering case, and prior imprisonment, and she tested positive for syphilis. The premarital medical report is suspected to be forged, prompting the family to allege that the matchmaking agency and bride hid crucial facts, causing marriage registration without full disclosure. Following the discovery, the husband sought to recover costs and hold those responsible; the pursuit has lasted more than six months with no recovery yet. Local authorities have formed a dedicated task force to investigate potential matchmaking fraud, forged documents, and other violations to protect citizens.

triage.headline_ja: 花百万で相親・電撃結婚！妊娠検査報告に夫が驚愕――妻は元受刑者で梅毒感染も判明
triage.triage_reason: 個人の婚姻トラブルと詐欺疑惑に関する事件報道であり、公衆衛生上の集団感染事象ではないため、いずれの基準にも該当しない。
triage.notes: 個人の婚姻詐欺・結婚仲介トラブルに関するゴシップ的報道であり、梅毒は個人の既往症として言及されているのみで公衆衛生上のアウトブレイクではない。

article.articleHeadline: The African Development Bank Group to provide $13 million to bolster Ebola response-outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan and Uganda
article.articleSummary: USD 13 million has been approved by the African Development Bank Group to bolster the Ebola virus disease (EVD-B) outbreak response in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Uganda, and South Sudan. On 15 May 2026, DRC declared a new EVD outbreak centered in Ituri province, with cases in Bunia, Rwampara and Mongwalu. The package comprises a USD 10 million grant from reallocated DRC resources channeled through WHO, and USD 3 million from Africa CDC’s Multi-Country Emergency Assistance Project for DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. It allocates USD 11 million to DRC and USD 1 million each to Uganda and South Sudan. Funds will support early case diagnosis, epidemiological surveillance, community engagement, public awareness, and regional coordination under the Ebola Virus Disease Outbreak Response Plan to halt transmission and reduce mortality. Bundibugyo strain is involved, with no approved vaccine or specific treatment, and the outbreak has spread to North Kivu and South Kivu.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ開発銀行グループ、コンゴ民主共和国・南スーダン・ウガンダのエボラ対応強化に1300万ドルを提供

article.articleHeadline: गुजरात में बढ़ा Chandipura Virus का खतरा! बच्चों में दिखे ये लक्षण तो हो जाएं सावधान; वरना पड़ेगा पछताना - chandipura virus alert in gujarat 5 critical symptoms in children parents must not ignore
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Chandipura virus threat has increased in Gujarat! If these symptoms appear in children, be vigilant; otherwise you will regret it - Chandipura virus alert in Gujarat: five critical symptoms in children that parents must not ignore.
article.articleSummary: Chandipura virus outbreaks are rising in Gujarat, India, with several pediatric infections and four reported deaths to date (three earlier deaths and a fresh five-year-old death). Chandipura virus, a member of the Rhabdoviridae family, can cause acute encephalitis syndrome (AES), leading to brain inflammation. First identified in Chandrapur, Maharashtra (1965), it spreads mainly through bites of infected sand flies; ticks may also play a role. It is not known to spread between people by coughing, sneezing, or casual contact. Symptoms appear suddenly and can worsen rapidly: high fever, severe headache, vomiting, weakness, irritability, excessive sleepiness, seizures, confusion, and possible coma. Young children (under 15) and residents in sand fly–endemic areas, with poor sanitation, are at higher risk, especially during the monsoon. Preventive measures: insect nets at night, covering clothes, repellents, and sanitation. Seek urgent care if a child has fever with vomiting, seizures, or extreme drowsiness.

triage.headline_ja: グジャラート州でChandipuraウイルスの脅威が拡大！子どもにこれらの症状が出たら要注意 - 保護者は見逃してはならない5つの重要症状
triage.triage_reason: インド・グジャラート州でChandipuraウイルスによる小児脳炎の死亡例が報告されているが、これは季節性（モンスーン期）に周期的に発生する既知の疾患であり、規模や拡大傾向、社会的関心の程度が不明なため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: Chandipuraウイルスはサシチョウバエ媒介性で、ヒト-ヒト感染は知られていない。グジャラート州・マハーラーシュトラ州で毎年モンスーン期に散発的に発生する既知の疾患であり、今回の症例数・死亡者数の全体像や過去との比較データが記事から不明。続報での症例数の推移確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Sốt 5 ngày, bé gái 2 tuổi thoát khỏi sốc nhiễm khuẩn nhờ phát hiện vết đốt mò
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Five-day fever, a 2-year-old girl survived septic shock thanks to detection of a mosquito bite mark.
article.articleSummary: A 24-month-old girl from Lao Cai, Vietnam, survived septic shock due to scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi) after five days of fever and a day of diarrhea. On admission to Hai Phong National Pediatric Hospital, she was lethargic with signs of severe infection; a abdominal eschar—a classic diagnostic clue for scrub typhus—was identified. She required aggressive critical care, including endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, central venous catheter, vasopressors, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. After 24 hours vasopressors were withdrawn, after 3 days she was weaned from ventilation, and after 11 days of intensive care she was stabilized and discharged. Scrub typhus is transmitted by chigger mite bites in areas with dense vegetation and can rapidly progress to multi-organ dysfunction if not promptly treated. Thorough full-body examination for eschars is essential to guide timely therapy and prevent mortality.

triage.headline_ja: 発熱5日間、2歳女児がツツガムシ刺咬痕の発見により敗血症性ショックから生還
triage.triage_reason: 単一の小児例で、ツツガムシ病はベトナムの当該地域で既知の風土病であり、異常性・国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 単一症例報告であり、ヒト-ヒト感染しない媒介動物由来疾患（ツツガムシ病）の既知風土病地域での事例。臨床的な啓発目的の記事であり、公衆衛生危機を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: TP.HCM thêm 5 ca tử vong do dại, đều không tiêm vắc xin ngay sau bị thương
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ho Chi Minh City reports 5 more deaths from rabies, all unvaccinated after exposure.
article.articleSummary: Rabies deaths in Ho Chi Minh City rose to five in the first half of 2026, all among people who neither were vaccinated nor received post-exposure rabies immunoglobulin after bites from dogs or cats suspected of rabies. Three cases occurred in Long Hai commune, Long Dat district, Ba Ria-Vung Tau; one in Cu Chi district, Ho Chi Minh City; and one in Hoa Hiep, Xuyen Moc district, Ba Ria-Vung Tau. About 40% used improper post-exposure practices, such as self-treating with home remedies or oils, delaying care. Rabies is 100% fatal once symptoms appear but preventable with timely wound care, vaccination, and immunoglobulin. Guidance: wash wounds with soap for at least 15 minutes, then disinfect with 45-70% alcohol or povidone-iodine, and seek medical care promptly. Authorities will coordinate surveillance, health education, and outbreak control across agencies.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市で狂犬病による死亡者がさらに5人、いずれも受傷後にワクチン接種をしていなかった

triage.notes: 狂犬病はベトナム国内で既知の流行病であり、今回の記事はワクチン未接種による予防可能な死亡例の報告。中国（Henan省）は記事本文中で言及されておらず、発生地域リストのノイズと判断し除外した。

article.articleHeadline: ফের বাড়ছে করোনা আতঙ্ক! কারা বেশি ঝুঁকিতে, কী কী উপসর্গ দেখলেই সতর্ক হবেন? জানালেন বিশিষ্ট চিকিৎসক
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fear of COVID-19 rising again! Who is at greater risk, and what symptoms should you watch out for? A renowned physician says.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 is resurfacing across parts of India, including Kolkata as of July 20, 2026. While no recent reports of severe illness have emerged from new infections, anyone can be infected. Those at higher risk include people over 60, and individuals with diabetes, heart disease, chronic lung disease, other comorbidities, or weakened immunity; children appear at relatively lower risk of severe disease. Common current symptoms resemble other viral infections: runny nose, cough, fever, sore throat, loss of smell, and fatigue. Seek medical care promptly if fever, cough, or throat pain lasts several days; loss of smell or taste; or if multiple family members share similar symptoms, especially for the elderly or those with comorbidities. Under medical guidance, arrange RT-PCR testing and isolate if positive. Avoid unnecessary antibiotics; most patients recover with rest and paracetamol. Take fluids, wear a mask as needed, and follow doctor’s advice.

triage.headline_ja: 再びコロナへの不安が高まる！誰がより高リスクか、どのような症状に注意すべきか？著名な医師が解説
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19の季節的な再流行に関する一般向け健康アドバイス記事であり、重症例の報告もなく、既知の疾患のため異常性・国際的拡大リスクは低い。

article.articleHeadline: Europom se širi spolna bolest iz Azije, otporna je na antibiotike: Ovo su najugroženije skupine
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A sexually transmitted infection spreading across Europe from Asia, resistant to antibiotics: These are the most at-risk groups.
article.articleSummary: Antibiotic-resistant gonorrhoea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae) is spreading across Europe with rising local transmission. In 2024, EU/EEA surveillance confirmed 106,331 cases—the highest annual total since 2009—reflecting a 303% increase over the past decade. The 2023–2024 rise was driven by men (up 7.9%), while cases among women fell 8.6%. The burden is greatest among men aged 25–34 and women aged 20–24; 62% of cases were in men who have sex with men, versus 37% among heterosexuals. France, Germany, Sweden, and the United Kingdom recorded the largest increases; other countries remain sporadic. Importation from outside Europe remains the main entry route for ceftriaxone-resistant strains, especially from Southeast Asia (Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam), but accumulating evidence shows growing local transmission across Europe. Current treatment remains ceftriaxone, with azithromycin in combination; resistance threatens efficacy. If untreated, gonorrhoea can cause pelvic inflammatory disease, infertility, and ectopic pregnancy.

triage.headline_ja: 薬剤耐性の性感染症がアジアからヨーロッパに拡大：最も危険なグループとは
triage.triage_reason: 記事の主題はヨーロッパ（EU/EEA）における薬剤耐性淋菌の拡大であり、東南アジア諸国（ベトナム・タイ・インドネシア・カンボジア）は輸入元として言及されているのみで、当該国での具体的な発生・流行の記述がないため対象国イベントとしての該当性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事はヨーロッパ（フランス・ドイツ・スウェーデン・英国）での薬剤耐性淋菌の増加を主題とし、東南アジア諸国は輸入株の起源として言及されるのみで、当該国自体での発生状況の詳細は記載されていない。ルールに基づき対象国は除外。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola Death Toll Hits 930 as Three Drug Trials Race to Fill Vaccine Gap
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo's Ituri Province has 2,344 confirmed cases and 930 deaths, with 37 new deaths in the latest 24-hour window, marking it as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. The Bundibugyo virus has no licensed vaccine or approved treatment; vaccines and monoclonal antibodies targeted at Zaire ebolavirus do not reliably protect Bundibugyo due to about 30% genome divergence. WHO advised against using Ervebo for Bundibugyo outside controlled research settings. Three experimental countermeasures are in human trials, including an Oxford Phase I vaccine trial in the UK; results are months away. Diagnostic limits: Cepheid GeneXpert does not detect Bundibugyo, with confirmation only after samples were sent to Kinshasa (May 14; outbreak declared May 15). Ituri hosts roughly 1,900 of 2,344 cases, and about 80% of new cases have unknown transmission sources, while strikes and attacks have disrupted contact tracing and response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数930人に達する、3つの治験薬がワクチン不足を埋めるべく競争
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最速拡大とされるエボラ（ブンディブギョ種）の流行が続き、死者930人・確定例2,344人に達し、ワクチン・治療薬が存在せず接触者追跡も攻撃により阻害されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。

article.articleHeadline: Tshopo : le CDC américain s'engage à renforcer la riposte contre Ebola - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tshopo: the U.S. CDC pledges to strengthen the Ebola response - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola response bolstered in DRC's Tshopo Province as the U.S. CDC pledges to strengthen coordination and field assessment. In Kisangani, on July 20, 2026, CDC mission leader Dr. Mike Kenzer announced an initial deployment of at least one month to better understand the field situation, coordinate with stakeholders and the government, and reinforce efforts to ensure a robust response to halt transmission. The on‑the‑ground work will focus on Bafwasende Territory near the Ituri border, epicenter of the current outbreak, with intensified surveillance and stronger partner coordination to prevent spread across the province. Experts will assess barriers and prevention measures at health zones currently affected and at cross‑border points to Ituri. Interim Tshopo governor Didier Lomoyo Iteku welcomed international support and urged evaluation of border controls to protect the province and propose adjustments as needed.

triage.headline_ja: チョポ州：米国CDCがエボラ対応強化を約束－ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国チョポ州で継続中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクに対し、米CDCが現地派遣を行い対応強化に乗り出している。重篤な疾患であり、国境を越えた拡大リスクと国際支援の必要性が明確なため、フルRRAへ進めるべきシグナルと判断。

article.articleHeadline: Irumu : Ebola classé première menace devant les terroristes ADF (Administrateur militaire) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Irumu: Ebola ranked as the number-one threat ahead of the ADF terrorists (military administrator) - ACP
article.articleSummary: As of July 20, 2026, Ebola is ranked the number-one threat in Irumu territory, Ituri province, in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, ahead of the ADF insurgents. Military administrator Colonel Jean Siro Simba led an Ebola awareness event in Nyankunde, urging community ownership of the response and respect for health workers facing the outbreak with limited resources. He affirmed the quality of care at Nyankunde General Referral Hospital (HGR Nyankunde), noting patients travel from Bunia to seek treatment and, after several days, recover from clinical Ebola signs, attributing this to the hospital’s reputation for high-quality care on the African continent. The administrator also intends to engage health partners who had withdrawn due to security troubles to return to Nyankunde to continue interventions. The report does not provide case or death figures.

triage.headline_ja: イルム：エボラがADFテロリストを上回り最大の脅威に位置づけられる（軍政管理官）- ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イツリ州イルム地域でエボラ出血熱の流行が継続中であり、治安上の問題で保健パートナーが撤退するなど対応リソースが不足している。Ebolaは重症度・国際拡散リスクが高い既知の高懸念病原体であり、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事には具体的な患者数・死亡者数の記載がなく、現行の流行状況の規模は不明。治安問題により保健パートナーが撤退している点は対応能力上の懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Dez anos depois, famílias convivem com impactos da zika
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ten years on, families live with the impacts of Zika.
article.articleSummary: More than a decade after the Zika virus outbreak that marked Brazil, families in Amazonas continue to cope with its legacies. The Weekly Report feature shows today there are children diagnosed with microcephaly and follows the daily routines of parents and guardians living with the syndrome’s ongoing impacts. The piece highlights enduring challenges for families in Amazonas state as they navigate care and daily life shaped by congenital Zika exposure. By foregrounding these personal stories, the report underscores the long-term public health footprint of Zika in Brazil and the ongoing need for support for families affected by microcephaly.

triage.headline_ja: 10年後、家族はジカ熱の影響とともに生きている

article.articleHeadline: Tshopo : sensibilisation contre Ebola et l'insalubrité lors d'une parade mixte à Kisangani - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tshopo: Ebola awareness and unsanitary conditions during a mixed parade in Kisangani - ACP
article.articleSummary: Kisangani, capital of Tshopo in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, held a mixed parade on July 20, 2026 to raise Ebola awareness and promote sanitation. Organized by Kisangani city hall, the National Police (PNC), and Makiso commune, the event emphasized barrier measures: frequent handwashing, avoiding handshakes, and promptly seeking hospital care for Ebola symptoms such as severe headache, high fever, vomiting, or bleeding. Mayor Delly Likunde Litawehe and PNC provincial commissioner Elvis Palanga Nawej underlined these messages. The authorities declared a mandatory collective 'salongo' effort in Tshopo to clear gutters and sweep roads in front of parcels, with police enforcing compliance and prohibiting police sub-commissariats from serving as motorcycle parking. Makiso mayor Simon Lowawa welcomed the collaboration, noting strong participation near Kisangani's central market, where attendees, including motorcycle taxi drivers, raised diverse concerns. No outbreak details.

triage.headline_ja: チョポ州：キサンガニで行われた合同パレードにおけるエボラおよび不衛生に対する啓発活動 - ACP

article.articleHeadline: 刚果（金）埃博拉疫情已致930人死亡
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed 930 people.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri Province) has reached 2,344 laboratory-confirmed cases with at least 930 deaths as of July 20, 2026. Africa CDC announced the Ituri outbreak on May 15, and the World Health Organization declared, on May 17, that the Ebola outbreaks in the DRC and Uganda constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). There is currently no approved vaccine or specific therapy for this strain. The figures come from the DRC Ministry of Health; no infection source details or information on imported/exported cases are provided. The report underlines ongoing regional public health concern and the need for continued surveillance and response efforts in central Africa.

article.articleHeadline: افزایش آمار مرگ و میر ناشی از ایبولا در کانگو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rising Ebola death toll in Congo
article.articleSummary: Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is facing the fastest Ebola outbreak in history, driven by the Bundibugyo strain. Since mid-May, 2,344 confirmed cases, 930 deaths, and 370 recoveries; 724 patients remain in isolation. In the last 24 hours, 37 deaths and 22 recoveries were recorded. Security concerns impede response, with at least 12 attacks on treatment centers and health teams since May due to distrust and rumors. No licensed vaccine or treatment exists for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease. WHO cautions that 80% of new infections originate from unknown transmission chains, underscoring rapid spread. The UN's International Organization for Migration warns that corpse transfers for funerals risk further dissemination; safe burial practices are essential. Authorities report expanding care and support capacity to manage cases.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラの死者数が急増
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ東部で史上最速とされるエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)の流行が進行し、致死率も高く、ワクチン・治療法未確立、治安不安による対応阻害も発生しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Beni : le Parlement des jeunes s'engage " fermement " dans la riposte - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Beni: The Youth Parliament commits firmly to the response - ACP.
article.articleSummary: On 20 July 2026 in Beni, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, members of the Youth Parliament reaffirmed commitment to the Ebola virus disease response. In a written statement, president Samuel-Don Katembo said youth leaders will deploy leadership, citizen platforms, and the Citizen Voice Lab to raise community awareness, counter misinformation, and support the Ebola response. They pledged to be ambassadors of prevention in their neighborhoods, sharing measures to prevent transmission and signs of illness, and to collaborate with response teams. The group will use Citizen Voice Lab channels and social media—Facebook, WhatsApp, X, TikTok, YouTube—to disseminate reliable information and promote responsible civic dialogue. They also vowed to mobilize youth for awareness, alerts, and protection, declaring that a responsible, connected, engaged youth is a bulwark against Ebola.

triage.headline_ja: ベニでのエボラ出血熱：青年議会が対応に「強く」取り組む - ACP
